THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 13, 1937 /8386

（批：D. 7675
14 / 37）

N.C.D.N. Photo.
Fraulein G. Walsemann

Revolt Described
By German Lady
Here From Sian

Fraulein Walsemann and
Brother "Prisoners"

CELEBRATED X'MAS IN
GUARDED HOUSE

A young German lady who lived through the anxious days of the Sian revolt, a virtual prisoner of "Marshal" Chang Hsueh-liang's troops was in Shanghai yesterday, apparently not a bit shaken by her experience.

Fraulein Gertrud Walsemann, who had only been in China about two months when the trouble started, arrived in Shanghai from the Shensi capital by air on Monday afternoon. When interviewed yesterday, by the "North-China Daily News" she described the exciting events of the early days of the coup without reluctance and said that she and her brother were not greatly inconvenienced, although they were, for three days, the virtual prisoners of the rebelling troops in a Chinese house in the inner city.

They were held there mainly for their own safety, they being the only foreigners residing at the time away from large, protected compounds. The other foreigners, missionaries, were not compelled to leave their houses.

On Visit to Brother

Fraulein Walsemann had gone to Sian to help her brother, Herr Roland Walsemann, who is the representative there of the large German dye firm "Defag." Herr Walsemann, during thirty years in China, had seen trouble before, but his sister was a new arrival and she admits it was a thrilling experience. They were the only Germans in Sian.

On the day the revolt started, when Gen. Chiang Kai-shek was taken prisoner, there was much firing of rifles and intense excitement in the streets. Fraulein Walsemann and her brother, however, were not permitted to see any actual fighting, for they were quickly disposed of by "Marshal" Chang's forces.

"We lived in a large house near the East Gate, but as soon as the revolt was under way, one of Chang's officers, with a detachment of men, came to our house and told us we must vacate immediately," Miss Walsemann related. "He spoke in Chinese to my brother and he seemed polite enough. We were then taken to a Chinese house in the central part of the city, under military escort. The streets were full of soldiers in their campaign kit, but we saw no actual fighting. We were quickly installed in what was to be our home for the next couple of days.

"Our servants were allowed to accompany us and in the Chinese house, which was fairly comfortable, we suffered no privation. Our 'boy' was permitted to go out and buy provisions and other necessaries, but my brother and myself had to remain in the house. There were armed guards outside and we knew we wouldn't be allowed to pass them. Anyway, we felt safe in the house, but we heard, through our servants, of others being injured or molested in other parts of the city —of trouble at the office of the China Travel Service, at the aerodrome and at the railway station. Most of the shops in the neighbourhood remained open and did business almost as in normal times.

"The shooting lasted only one day and it was all rifle or pistol fire. But it did not occur near enough to permit us to see any encounters.

Christmas Celebrated

"We spent Christmas in the house which had been assigned to us, and we contrived to have a fairly good holiday.

"After two and a half days we were allowed to return to our own house, again under escort. The streets presented a warlike appearance—there were many soldiers, all carrying rifles with fixed bayonets, and many carrying hand-grenades also. Some of the streets were barricaded and there were large barbed-wire entanglements. The atmosphere was quite tense, but we saw no fighting. Then the situation eased gradually and the outcome of the affair is well known to everybody."

Miss Walsemann is in Shanghai visiting friends. She had hoped to be able to return to Sian, but that plan has now been frustrated by the serious turn of events in Shensi.

《字林西报》照片。
G. 瓦尔瑟曼小姐 (Fraulein G. Walsemann)

一位来自西安的德国女士
描述事变经过

瓦尔瑟曼小姐及其兄弟
沦为“囚徒”

在受监视的住宅中
度过著名的圣诞节

一位年轻德国女士经历了西安事变那些令人焦虑的日子，她实际上是张学良“元帅”部队的囚徒，昨天抵达上海，显然未因这段经历而受到丝毫惊吓。

格特鲁德·瓦尔瑟曼小姐 (Fraulein Gertrud Walsemann) 在事变开始时仅在中国居住了约两个月，于周一下午乘飞机从陕西省会抵达上海。昨日接受《字林西报》采访时，她毫不迟疑地描述了政变初期那些激动人心的事件，并表示她和她的兄弟并未感到太大不便，尽管他们在内城的一所中国房屋里，作为叛军的实际囚徒被拘禁了三天。

扣留他们主要是为了他们自身的安全，因为他们是当时居住在大型受保护租界区之外的唯一外国人。其他外国人，即传教士们，并未被强迫离开他们的住所。

探望兄弟

瓦尔瑟曼小姐前往西安是为了帮助她的兄弟罗兰·瓦尔瑟曼先生 (Herr Roland Walsemann)，他是德国大型染料公司“德法格” (Defag) 驻当地的代表。瓦尔瑟曼先生在华三十年，此前曾经历过动荡，但他的妹妹是新来者，她承认这是一次惊险的经历。他们是西安仅有的两名德国人。

事变发生当天，蒋介石将军被扣押，街上枪声大作，气氛极度紧张。然而，瓦尔瑟曼小姐和她的兄弟不被允许目睹任何实际战斗，因为他们很快就被张“元帅”的部队安置好了。

“我们住在东门附近的一所大房子里，但事变一开始，张的一名军官就带着一队人马来到我们家，告诉我们必须立即搬离，”瓦尔瑟曼小姐叙述道。“他用中文对我哥哥说话，态度似乎相当礼貌。随后，我们在军事护送下被带到市中心的一所中国房屋里。街上满是身穿作战装备的士兵，但我们没有看到任何实际战斗。我们很快被安顿下来，那里成了我们接下来几天的家。

“我们的仆人被允许随行，在那所还算舒适的中国房屋里，我们没有遭受任何匮乏。我们的‘男仆’被允许外出购买食物和其他必需品，但我哥哥和我必须留在屋内。外面有武装警卫，我们知道不允许通过他们。无论如何，我们在屋里感到安全，但通过仆人，我们听说城市其他地区有人受伤或受到骚扰——在中国旅行社办事处、机场和火车站都发生了麻烦。附近的大部分商店仍然开门营业，生意几乎如常。

“枪战只持续了一天，全是步枪或手枪射击。但发生地点离我们要远，使我们无法看到任何交战场面。

庆祝圣诞

“我们在被分配到的那所房子里度过了圣诞节，并设法过了一个相当不错的节日。

“两天半后，我们获准返回自己的家，同样是在护送之下。街道呈现出一派战争景象——有许多士兵，全都携带装有刺刀的步枪，许多人还携带手榴弹。一些街道设置了路障，并有大量的铁丝网障碍。气氛相当紧张，但我们没有看到战斗。随后局势逐渐缓和，此事的结果已为众人所知。”

瓦尔瑟曼小姐目前在上海拜访朋友。她原本希望能返回西安，但鉴于陕西局势的严重转折，该计划现已落空。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, January 13, 1937
CONCENTRATING ON SIAN
Situation Unliquidated
As Red Forces Combine
With Northwest Armies
Harried “Bandits” Find Ancient Capital Second
Juikin; True Situation Remains In Doubt;
Soviet Mongolia Aid Called Absurd
Eyes On Lanchow-Hami Silk Trail
WITH Sianfu, capital of Shensi, rapidly taking on all the outward aspects of a second Juikin since the detention and later release of the Generalissimo, attention has again centered on that remote Northwestern city so recently relieved of the restraining presence of Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang. Those who spend the greater part of their time verbally plotting the changing political map of China are again speculating on the amount of support allegedly being received by the Chinese Communists in Shensi from confederates farther to the west.
While the average observer on the China seaboard was laboring under the illusion that General Chiang’s release and General Chang’s surrender automatically brought an end to the so-called Sian Revolt, it was noted that Nanking troops stopped their advance on the city and withdrew, and for a period of time little or no information came out of the Northwest at all. News agencies in the capital and elsewhere were so busy celebrating actuality of Chiang’s release that Sian itself appeared to have vanished completely from the map, and Lanchow as well. But with several thousand troops of Chang’s Northeastern Army still in Shensi and Kansu, and the presence there of more thousands of Communist troops, it was inconceivable that anyone could expect a waiting world to suppose that those forces had, like the Arabs, folded their tents and silently stolen away into the vastnesses of the hinterland, leaving the Sian affair “liquidated,” as the despatches so humorously employ that abused term.
A Danger Center
Now the fact that the tension in Sian has not been eased at all, and that the absence of the Generalissimo and the Young Marshal from the scene has little effect on developments there, is becoming more apparent. Observers, foreign and Chinese, realize that Sian is still the center of a movement potentially dangerous to Nanking—and to Nippon. The troops are still there, Nanking’s authority at the moment in that region is nominal only, and the seriousness of the situation is indicated by the belief on the part of reliable foreign authorities that foreign nationals there are still very much in danger, that they should evacuate immediately, and that events may soon prove to be very menacing indeed.
Contact Alleged
WHEN the Reds “swept down like the wolf on the fold” from the bleak Northwest to fraternize with the Young Marshal’s army in Shensi, thus bringing about a crisis in Sian, political wiseacres, particularly those with axes to grind, took up the old cry that the Communists had indeed established contact with their confederates in the frontier regions of Outer Mongolia and specially in Sinkiang, and were receiving support from them.
So far as support from Sovietized Mongols is concerned, this was held patently absurd by those acquainted even second-hand with the situation. Between Ulan Bator and Lanchow is a thousand-mile barrier of the vast and forbidding Gobi and the mighty Ala Shan. The roving Banners of Ningshia and Suiyuan were disorganized and politically uncertain; there was fighting in Suiyuan itself; communications of any value to whole armies have never existed in that region; the reason militated against any such activity.
But three years ago the Communists, after a protracted siege, lost their stronghold at Juikin, in Kiangsi, and began an epic march that took the main body of them down through Hunan, Kweichow, Yunnan, up across Szechuen (where they made a bitter stand in the borderland mountains), circling back into Kansu and northern Shensi. Offshoot columns of that march scattered in other directions to reinforce the remnant bands in Fukien and northern Kwangtung. For a time the Nipponese were agitated by the fear that the march could not be stopped and that the horde would sweep across Shansi into the Hopei plains. Through it all the government still pursued them.
Conditions Unknown
The inevitable assertion that the Communists were now in direct contact with Sinkiang sympathizers cannot be dismissed, however, for conditions beyond Sian can only be conjectured. No reliable information can be obtained. Lanchow remains silent.
It has been established, of course, that Communists are active in both Lanchow and Sian, and may very easily be holding the reins there. That the armies are in contact across the intervening country is unconfirmed. But whether this is a self-contained and more or less self-supporting region now, observers cannot say. What is going on at the back-door, where the old Silk Road leads out through Kansu through Liangchow, Kanchow, Suchow to Hami, is open to question.
Saw Trucks?
AT any rate, it is a long distance over which to establish contact, from Hami to Lanchow. It is over a thousand miles, and the road is a fearfully difficult one, even in summer-time. It can be negotiated by motor truck in season. Olmarron Hathaway, the young American who recently came out of the region after being held captive by the Soviets in Urumchi for several months, was reported —by the local office of a European news agency—as having seen Soviet truckloads of arms in Hami, destined for an unknown goal in Kansu. Hathaway subsequently denied the agency report.
That Hami and Urumchi themselves are the center of Soviet activity in Sinkiang has been well established by a variety of sources over a period of several years. But it must not be forgotten that Urumchi is a very long distance from Sian, much farther than Sian is from Shanghai, and communications are relatively normal. Sian and Lanchow are in contact with one another by plane now. A few months ago it was reported on fairly reliable information that the Soviet network of airways, which had previously been extended to Urumchi, was operating now to Hami. An inter-Soviet airway from Urumchi to Sian would not be inconceivable now. But planes in that vast and unpeopled region cannot do much in the matter of carrying troops, supplies, arms, etc. That is a matter for trucks, or more probably for slow caravans.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年1月13日，星期三
聚焦西安
局势未平
随着红军与西北军联合
受困“匪徒”发现古都是第二个瑞金；真实情况仍存疑；
称苏蒙援助荒谬
目光投向兰州-哈密丝绸古道

随着陕西省会西安府迅速呈现出第二个瑞金的所有外在特征——自委员长被扣及随后获释以来——人们的注意力再次集中到这座偏远的西北城市，它不久前才摆脱了张少帅的制约性存在。那些大部分时间都在口头上谋划中国变幻莫测的政治版图的人，再次推测陕西的中国共产党人据称从更西边的盟友那里获得了多少支持。

虽然中国沿海地区的普通观察者还在这样一种错觉中挣扎，即蒋将军的获释和张将军的投降自动结束了所谓的“西安事变”，但人们注意到，南京军队停止了对该城的推进并撤军，且在一段时间内，西北地区几乎没有传出任何消息。首都及其他地方的新闻机构忙于庆祝蒋获释这一既成事实，以至于西安本身似乎完全从地图上消失了，兰州也是如此。但是，鉴于张的东北军仍有数千人留在陕西和甘肃，且那里还有数千名共产党军队，任何人若指望等待中的世界相信这些部队像阿拉伯人那样收起帐篷，悄无声息地潜入广阔的内陆腹地，从而让西安事件得以“解决”（正如电报幽默地滥用这个被滥用的术语那样），那是不可想象的。

危险中心

现在，西安的紧张局势丝毫没有缓解，而且委员长和张少帅不在现场对那里的局势发展影响甚微，这一事实正变得愈发明显。中外观察家意识到，西安仍然是一场潜在危及南京乃至日本运动的中心。部队仍在那里，南京当局在该地区的权威目前仅是名义上的，可靠的外国人士认为那里的外籍国民仍处于极大危险之中，应立即撤离，且事态可能很快证明确实非常具有威胁性，这表明了局势的严重性。

涉嫌接触

当红军“如狼扑羊群般”从荒凉的西北横扫而下，与张少帅在陕西的军队结盟，从而引发西安危机时，政治上的自作聪明者，特别是那些别有用心的人，重提旧调，声称共产党人确实与其在外蒙古边境地区，特别是新疆的同伙建立了联系，并正从他们那里获得支持。

就来自苏维埃化蒙古人的支持而言，那些即使只是间接了解局势的人也认为这显然是荒谬的。乌兰巴托和兰州之间横亘着浩瀚且令人望而生畏的戈壁沙漠以及强大的阿拉善山脉，构成了一道千里的屏障。宁夏和绥远的游牧旗队组织涣散，政治局势不明；绥远境内本身就有战事；该地区从未存在过对整支军队有任何价值的通讯手段；客观条件阻碍了任何此类活动。

但在三年前，共产党人在长期围困后失去了他们在江西瑞金的 stronghold（据点），并开始了一场史诗般的长征，主力部队穿过湖南、贵州、云南，向上跨越四川（他们在边界山区进行了艰苦的抵抗），然后折回甘肃和陕西北部。长征的分遣队向其他方向分散，以增援福建和广东北部的残余帮派。有一段时间，日本人因担心长征无法阻止，且这股洪流将横扫山西进入河北平原而感到不安。在整个过程中，政府军一直在追击他们。

情况不明

然而，关于共产党人现在与新疆同情者直接接触的说法不可避免，不能不予理会，因为西安以外的情况只能靠猜测。无法获得可靠信息。兰州保持沉默。

当然，已经确定共产党人在兰州和西安都很活跃，并且很可能在那里掌控着局面。军队是否穿越 intervening country（中间地带）建立了接触，尚未得到证实。但是， observers（观察家）无法说明这现在是否是一个自给自足且或多或少能自我维持的地区。在后门发生了什么，即古老的丝绸之路经甘肃通过凉州、甘州、肃州通往哈密的那条路线，情况尚存疑问。

看到了卡车？

无论如何，从哈密到兰州建立联系的距离很长。超过一千英里，即使在夏季，道路也极其难行。在适宜的季节，汽车卡车可以通行。年轻的美国人奥尔马伦·哈撒韦 (Olmarron Hathaway) 最近刚从该地区出来，他此前在乌鲁木齐被苏维埃人员扣押数月，据一家欧洲通讯社当地分社报道，他在哈密看到了满载武器的苏联卡车，目的地是甘肃某未知地点。哈撒韦随后否认了该通讯社的报道。

哈密和乌鲁木齐本身是苏联在新疆活动的中心，这一点多年来已通过多种来源得到充分证实。但切勿忘记，乌鲁木齐距离西安非常遥远，比西安距离上海还要远得多，且通讯相对正常。西安和兰州现在通过飞机保持联系。几个月前，有相当可靠的消息报道称，此前已延伸至乌鲁木齐的苏联航空网络，现在已运营至哈密。一条从乌鲁木齐到西安的苏维埃内部航线，现在并非不可想象。但是，在那片广阔且人烟稀少的地区，飞机在运送部队、物资、武器等方面起不了多大作用。那是卡车的事，或者更可能是缓慢的骆驼商队的事。

18395-

Soviets Active
Sinkiang's connections with
Communism are, of course, too
well known to repeat at any
length. The authorities have
"permitted" the entrance of So-
viet troops into the border region
in order to strengthen the Soviet
Far Eastern defense. The Soviet
Army cooperates with the Sin-
kiang forces. An eastern military
and political school has been
established in Urumchi for Chin-
ese. Russian arms cross the bord-
er freely. High Soviet military
men act in Sinkiang as advisers
and educators. Loans have been
reported made by Russian to Sin-
kiang for the development of in-
dustries and for reconstruction. A
branch of the Soviet State Bank
had been established in Urumchi,
and it issues notes. Soviet con-
sulates are scattered through the
province.
Other reports have it that So-
viet loans to Sinkiang have
amounted to about $200,000,000, of
which half is devoted to general
establishments and the rest divid-
ed between military expenditure
and improvement of transporta-
tion.
At any rate, whatever support
the armies in the Northwest are
receiving, Sian is undoubtedly the
center of it, for the Communists
have apparently concentrated on
it as they have concentrated on
no other single point since they
abandoned Juikin.

On Yellow River
THE city in the Yellow River
has a population of about
a million. The founders of the
Chinese race are said to have
settled in that loess plain. The
city was once the capital of the
Tangs, then known as Siking, and
later it was the capital from 206
B.C. to 605 A.D. It was the capital
of China as late as 1900, when
the Empress Dowager fled there
during the Boxer Rebellion.
It has seen great movements
come and go. Mohammedanism
gained its entrance to China in
Sian, and wandering Jews settled
there centuries ago. Buddhism
established its strength in the city,
and Nestorians brought Christian-
ity from Asia Minor to Sian.
The walls are 10 miles around,
30 feet high, and visible for many
miles. They were built in 1370.
As in Peiping, there are a Tartar
and a Chinese city. The neigh-
borhood abounds in imperial
tombs and relics of the past.
Among these are the tomb of Em-
peror Shih Hwang-ti, the Burner
of the Books, the Empress Wu
Tse-tien, and the Forest of Stones
—some 1400 monuments inscribed
with historical data.
Its population today is a good
part Mohammedan. Its wealth is
now in its furriers and its coal
field.—L. S. G.
pages.zh:
18395-

苏维埃活动频繁

新疆与共产主义的联系众所周知，无需赘述。当局已“允许”苏军进入边境地区，以加强苏联在远东的防御。苏军与新疆部队协同作战。乌鲁木齐已为中国人设立了一所东部军事政治学校。俄国武器自由越境。苏联高级军官在新疆担任顾问和教育者。据报道，俄方向新疆提供贷款，用于发展工业和重建。苏联国家银行已在乌鲁木齐设立分行，并发行钞票。苏联领事馆遍布全省。

另有报告称，苏联向新疆提供的贷款总额约为2亿美元，其中一半用于一般建设，其余部分用于军事开支和改善交通。

无论如何，无论西北军队正接受何种支持，西安无疑是其中心，因为共产党显然已将重心集中于此，自他们放弃瑞金以来，从未如此集中于单一地点。

黄河畔

黄河畔的这座城市人口约一百万。据说中华民族的祖先就定居在这片黄土平原上。该城曾是唐朝的都城，当时称为西京；后来，从公元前206年到公元605年，它也是都城。直到1900年，它仍是中国的首都，当时慈禧太后在义和团运动期间逃往此地。

它见证了无数重大运动的兴衰。伊斯兰教经由西安传入中国，流浪的犹太人在几个世纪前便定居于此。佛教在该城确立了势力，聂斯托利派（景教）将基督教从小亚细亚带至西安。

城墙周长10英里，高30英尺，数英里外清晰可见。它们建于1370年。与北平一样，这里分为鞑靼城和汉城。附近遍布皇家陵墓和古代遗迹。其中包括秦始皇（焚书者）的陵墓、武则天女皇的陵墓，以及碑林——约1400块刻有历史资料的石碑。

如今，其居民中穆斯林占相当大比例。其财富现在在于皮货商和煤矿田。——L. S. G.

January 13, 1937.

D.C. 4 17

MAINICHI

BOUNDS OF JAPANESE MARINES TO BE EXTENDED

Owing to the acts of anti-Japanese terrorism, places and areas which Japanese marines were permitted to visit were limited. Commencing from spring this year, these bounds will be extended so that groups of ten marines may walk about in the suburbs because the local situation has much improved. The bounds will be limited to a part of Western Recreation Road, the Garden belonging to the Japanese Club and the Bridge of Light Characters ("Fa Tz Chiao") in Chapei.

GENERAL CHANG HSUEH LIANG AND THE ANTI-JAPANESE MOVEMENT

The Shanghai Mainichi publishes the following leading article:-
After General Chiang Kai Shek's return to Nanking, the Government announced that General Chang Hsueh Liang had surrendered unconditionally to Nanking, but the "Chia Fang Daily News", an official paper of General Chang Hsueh Liang's Party in Sian, published a contradictory report to the effect that General Chiang Kai Shek had accepted the demand to co-operate with the Reds. General Chiang Kai Shek is now recuperating in Fenghua; he will attend the third plenary assembly to be held on February 15 at Nanking.
The "Chia Fang Daily News" of January 6 published a manifesto addressed to General Ho Ying Chin and the Chinese people in the North-West by General Yang Hu Chen and General Yu Hsueh Choong stating that the present situation was due to the fact that the Nanking Government had failed to re-organize the Government on an anti-Japanese plan or to withdraw the troops from Sian district in accordance with the promise given by General Chiang Kai Shek. Thus it will be seen that General Chiang Kai Shek was not released unconditionally. The present question is not the failure of the Central Government to carry out its promise, it is a question of the military strength of the forces in the North-West. For this reason, it is probable that the military leaders in the North-West will co-operate with the red army.
Close relations between General Yang Hu Chen and General Yu Hsueh Choong's troops and the Red Army and the communist party have been frequently reported. Regarding the strength of the Red Army no reliable information can be obtained. The Sian incident of December 12 gave a good opportunity to the Red Army to enter a flourishing area. The Red Army is keeping a watch on the re-organization of the former North-East Army and will instigate the discontented soldiers to create another incident.

每日新闻

日本海军陆战队活动范围将扩大

由于反日恐怖主义行为，此前限制了日本海军陆战队获准前往的地点和区域。鉴于当地局势已大有改善，从今年春季开始，这些限制范围将予以扩大，允许十人一组的陆战队员在郊区走动。限制范围将限于闸北的西娱乐路（Western Recreation Road）的一部分、日本俱乐部所属的花园以及法租界桥（“Fa Tz Chiao”，音译：法字桥/法华桥）。

张学良将军与反日运动

《上海每日新闻》发表以下社论：

蒋介石将军返回南京后，政府宣布张学良将军已向南京无条件投降，但西安张派党部的官方报纸《解放日报》刊登了一篇与之矛盾的报道，称蒋介石将军已接受与赤色分子合作的要求。蒋介石将军目前正在奉化休养；他将出席于2月15日在南京举行的第三届中央全会。

1月6日的《解放日报》刊登了杨虎城将军和于学忠将军致何应钦将军及西北中国人民的宣言，指出目前的局势是由于南京政府未能按照抗日计划改组政府，或未按蒋介石将军所作的承诺从西安地区撤军所致。由此可见，蒋介石将军并非被无条件释放。当前的问题不在于中央政府未能履行其承诺，而在于西北军队的军事实力问题。因此，西北军事领导人很可能与红军合作。

关于杨虎城将军和于学忠将军的部队与红军及共产党之间的密切关系，已有频繁报道。关于红军的实力，无法获得可靠情报。12月12日的西安事变给红军进入繁荣地区提供了良机。红军正在监视原东北军的改组情况，并将煽动不满士兵制造另一起事件。

在这种情况下，很难看出目前身在南京的张学良将军将采取何种态度。然而，他似乎对局势漠不关心，因为据报道他正在打高尔夫球。我们可以从两个不同的角度来看待他在南京的存在

January 13, 1937. Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

SITUATION IN SIAN BECOMES SERIOUS

The situation in Shensi is different from that in Kansu. General Wong Ju Shang, the newly appointed Pacification Commissioner of Kansu, has not yet assumed the post. The attitude of General Yu Hsueh Chung is becoming clearer. Besides sending to General Ho Ying Ching, Minister of War, a telegram several days ago, expressing his loyalty to the National Government, General Yu Hsueh Chung has sent another telegram to Nanking, stating that he would detail representatives to Nanking to make a report and to ask for instructions.

Conditions in Shensi are very disturbed. The attitude of General Yang Hu Chen, the rebel leader, does not agree with that of the commanders in Shensi under General Chang Hsueh Liang, for most of General Chang's subordinates wish to obey the orders of the National Government and the instructions of General Chang, while there is no indication that General Yang is repentant.

Mr. Yu Yue Jen President of the Control Yuan, has received a telegram from General Yang Hu Chen saying that he is sending General Me Tsung Lin to Nanking to make certain arrangements with the Government. General Yang is probably working to delay the attack by Government troops.

Reports from political circles show that communists are very active at Sian and many communist organizations have been established in hotels. There are in the banks silver valued at $17,000,000 and legal tender notes to the value of $28,000,000. Despite the fact that the situation is extremely grave, the Government still hopes that General Yang Hu Chen will come to his senses. No clash has as yet taken place between Government troops and the men under Yang.

On January 12, General Wong Ju Shang, the new Pacification Commissioner of Kansu, sent a telegram to General Yu Hsueh Chung informing him that he is proceeding to Kansu in a few days.

On January 12, Mr. Yu Yue Jen received Mr. Li Tse Kong (李志刚), General Yang Hu Chen's representative, and instructed him to return to Shensi to induce General Yang to obey the orders of the Govt. Mr. Li left Nanking for Shensi by aeroplane at noon January 12.

Hwa Tung Ya Poo (華商夜報) :-

Communists Organize National Salvation Association :
Mo Tse Tung Appointed Chief of Political Department

During the Sian coup, the communist leaders Mo Tse Tung (毛澤東), Chow An Lai (周恩來) and Miss Agnes Smedley, an American who represents Soviet Russia, mingled with the soldiers and entered Sian. They are now discussing certain arrangements with General Yang Hu Chen. Red flags have appeared in Sian. The communists have formed a National Salvation Association.

General Yang Hu Chen has formed three new Divisions of soldiers; it is being organized on the lines of the Red Army of Soviet Russia. A Political Department is attached to every division. Mo Tse Tung and Chow An Lai are the Chiefs of all Political Department.

1937年1月13日。晨间译文。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸刊登以下电讯报道：

西安局势趋于严重

陕西的局势与甘肃不同。新任甘肃绥靖主任翁照垣将军尚未就职。于学忠将军的态度日益明朗。除了几天前向军政部长何应钦将军发送电报表示效忠国民政府外，于学忠将军还向南京发送了另一封电报，称他将派遣代表前往南京汇报并请示指示。

陕西局势非常动荡。叛乱首领杨虎城将军的态度与张学良将军麾下的陕西指挥官们不一致，因为张的大部分下属希望服从国民政府的命令和张的指示，而杨并没有表现出悔意。

监察院院长于右任先生收到杨虎城将军的电报，称他正派遣梅宗林将军前往南京与政府进行某些安排。杨虎城可能在努力拖延政府军队的进攻。

政界消息显示，共产党在西安非常活跃，许多共产党组织已在酒店建立。银行内有价值1700万美元的银元和面值2800万美元的法币。尽管局势极其严峻，政府仍希望杨虎城将军能迷途知返。政府军队与杨的部下之间尚未发生冲突。

1月12日，新任甘肃绥靖主任翁照垣将军向于学忠将军发出电报，通知他将于数日内前往甘肃。

1月12日，于右任先生会见了杨虎城将军的代表李志刚（Li Tse Kong），并指示他返回陕西，劝诱杨虎城服从政府命令。李志刚于1月12日中午乘飞机离开南京前往陕西。

《华商夜报》：

共产党组织救国会：毛泽东被任命为政治部主任

在西安事变期间，共产党领导人毛泽东（Mo Tse Tung）、周恩来（Chow An Lai）以及代表苏俄的美国女士艾格尼丝·史沫特莱（Agnes Smedley）混入士兵之中并进入西安。他们目前正在与杨虎城将军讨论某些安排。西安已出现红旗。共产党已成立救国会。

杨虎城将军已组建三个新的师；其编制仿照苏俄红军模式。每个师均附设政治部。毛泽东和周恩来是所有政治部的主任。

MAINICHI

BOUNDS OF JAPANESE MARINES TO BE EXTENDED

Owing to the acts of anti-Japanese terrorism, places and areas which Japanese marines were permitted to visit were limited. Commencing from spring this year, these bounds will be extended so that groups of ten marines may walk about in the suburbs because the local situation has much improved. The bounds will be limited to a part of Western Recreation Road, the Garden belonging to the Japanese Club and the Bridge of Light Characters("La Tz Chiao")in Chapei.

GENERAL CHANG HSUEH LIANG AND THE ANTI-JAPANESE MOVEMENT

The Shanghai Mainichi publishes the following leading article:-
After General Chiang Kai Shek's return to Nanking, the Government announced that General Chang Hsueh Liang had surrendered unconditionally to Nanking, but the "Chia Fang Daily News", an official paper of General Chang Hsueh Liang's Party in Sian, published a contradictory report to the effect that General Chiang Kai Shek had accepted the demand to co-operate with the Reds. General Chiang Kai Shek is now recuperating in Fenghua; he will attend the third plenary assembly to be held on February 15 at Nanking.
The "Chia Fang Daily News" of January 6 published a manifesto addressed to General Ho Ying Chin and the Chinese people in the North-West by General Yang Hu Chen and General Yu Hsueh Choong stating that the present situation was due to the fact that the Nanking Government had failed to re-organize the Government on an anti-Japanese plan or to withdraw the troops from Sian district in accordance with the promise given by General Chiang Kai Shek. Thus it will be seen that General Chiang Kai Shek was not released unconditionally. The present question is not the failure of the Central Government to carry out its promise, it is a question of the military strength of the forces in the North-West. For this reason, it is probable that the military leaders in the North-West will co-operate with the red army.
Close relations between General Yang Hu Chen and General Yu Hsueh Choong's troops and the Red Army and the communist party have been frequently reported. Regarding the strength of the Red Army no reliable information can be obtained. The Sian incident of December 12 gave a good opportunity to the Red Army to enter a flourishing area. January 12, 1937.    2    Morning Translation.    37

Hwo Lei Wen Pao dated January 11 :-

COMMUNISTS IN CONTROL AT SIAN

The situation in Sian is apparently becoming more serious. According to official information, the troops under the command of General Yang Hu Chen and General Yu Hsueh Chung have not yet been incorporated with the communist armies. Influential members of the communist party have been very active in Sian. Nearly all the public bodies and institutions have been placed under the control of communists. The situation in Sian to-day resembles that created by the Wu-Han Regime in 1927. The Sian authorities have shown no sign of repentance.

Miss Agnes Smedley, an American journalist in Shanghai, who known to be in sympathy with the communists, has proceeded to Sian where she is carrying out extensive activities. According to information secured by a representative of this paper, at the time of the arrest of I.r. Sung Chun Sz (沈钧儒) and others, Miss Smedley went to Peiping and later returned to Shanghai. Following the outbreak of the Sian mutiny, she went to Hankow. At that time, the public did not pay any particular attention to her movements. She has now become very active in communist affairs in Sian.

The developments in Sian are causing great anxiety to the Foreign Embassies in China and some of them are contemplating the withdrawal of their nationals from Shensi, because of fear that the communists in Sian might precipitate a radical political changes in Sian. However, the Nanking Government is still hoping that the troops under Generals Yang Hu Chen and Yu Hsueh Chung will soon come to their senses and submit to the orders of the Central Government.

Railway traffic to the west of Tungkwan of the Lunghai Railway is still obstructed.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

General Yang Hu Chen Still Recalcitrant

General Yang Hu Chen, the rebel leader in Sian, is still opposing the order of the National Government. He has mobilized his forces and is putting up defence works.

General Yu Hsueh Chung, Chairman of the Kansu Provincial Government, has sent a telegram to General Ho Ying Ching, Minister of War, expressing his repentance and declaring his loyalty to the National Government. General Yu has also sent a telegram to General Chang Hsueh Liang, informing him that he has pledged his loyalty to the National Government. In reply, General Chang advised General Yu to obey the orders of the National Government by taking over his new post and by persuading General Yang Hu Chen not to be misled.

According to reliable information, a clash has taken place between the troops under General Yang Hu Chen and those under the north-east commanders.

1月11日《火力文报》（Hwo Lei Wen Pao，音译）：

共产党控制西安

西安局势显然日趋严重。据官方消息，杨虎城将军和于学忠将军指挥的部队尚未并入共产党军队。共产党重要成员在西安非常活跃。几乎所有公共团体和机构都置于共产党的控制之下。今日西安的局势类似于1927年武汉政权造成的局面。西安当局未表现出任何悔意。

上海美国记者艾格尼丝·史沫特莱女士以同情共产党闻名，她已前往西安，在那里开展广泛活动。据本报代表获取的消息，在沈钧儒（Sung Chun Sz）等人被捕时，史沫特莱女士去了北平，随后返回上海。西安兵变爆发后，她去了汉口。当时，公众并未特别关注她的行踪。她现在在西安的共产党事务中变得非常活跃。

西安的事态发展引起在华外国使馆的极大焦虑，其中一些使馆正考虑从陕西撤离其侨民，因为担心西安的共产党可能会引发西安激进的政治变革。然而，南京政府仍希望杨虎城将军和于学忠将军的部队能尽快迷途知返，服从中央政府的命令。

陇海铁路潼关以西的交通仍然受阻。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸刊登下列电讯报道：

杨虎城将军仍然顽固

西安叛军首领杨虎城将军仍然反对国民政府的命令。他已动员部队并构筑防御工事。

甘肃省主席于学忠将军致电军政部长何应钦将军，表示悔悟并声明效忠国民政府。于将军还致电张学良将军，告知其已宣誓效忠国民政府。作为回复，张将军建议于将军通过就任新职并劝说杨虎城将军不要受误导来服从国民政府的命令。

据可靠消息，杨虎城将军的部队与东北军指挥官的部队之间发生了冲突。

GENERAL YANG HU CHEN TO START ANTI-JAPANESE WAR

A special telegram from Nanking
reports that on January 7 the headquarters of the anti-
Japanese united army, which is receiving assistance
from the Soviet, issued the following declaration:-
1. That the united army be advanced to central
China after driving away the enemy from the west of Tung-

affairs at the places occupied by the anti-Japanese united
army be dealt with war measures.

Japanese organizations be mobilized to present a united
front against our enemy.
The following slogans were
issued by the anti-Japanese field headquarters:-

2. Unite all the troops in the North-West! Guard
the base of anti-Japanese operations at any cost!
3. Welcome the Nanking army and the various anti-
Japanese groups which may desire to join us!
4. Urge all the anti-Japanese forces in the North-
West to unite!
5. All Chinese soldiers and people, unite and fight
against Japan!
6. Oppose civil war; down with all who are pro-
Japanese!

and fight Japan!

movement which was started on December 12.

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, JANUARY 10, 1937

Nanking Must Decide Policy
Regarding China's "Reds"

Local Japanese Press Says Central Authorities Must
Be Ready To Accept Nippon Proposals For
Joint Anti-Communist Front

Time has come, the Shanghai 'Mainichi' declared yesterday when the Nanking Government must decide once and for all its attitude towards Communism.

Having experienced the terrors of Communism, the journal asserted, the Central administration must be ready to accept Japan's proposal for the creation of a joint anti-Red front.

"If Nanking continues to hesitate, we cannot but interpret this as a manifestation of its desire to join with the Communists whenever circumstances require it," the daily said.

"The Japanese Government's China policy, we fear, will be stiffened in the coming weeks because of the parliamentary interpellations. This change will further be aggravated by Nanking's refusal for joint opposition to Communism.

"If, on the other hand, Nanking accepts Japan's proposal, a bitter struggle will be inevitable between the Government and the Communists, with the attendant intrigues and manoeuvres by petty military chieftains."

Commenting on the situation in Sian, the 'Nippo' asserted that Generals Chang Hsuch-liang and Yang Hu-cheng have completely ignored the terms of the agreement reached with General Chiang Kai-shek.

General Yang, the journal said, appears to be unwilling to accept Nanking's rulings on the disposition of his troops. This recalcitrance was explained by the "Nippo" as a result of "the Sovietization of General Yang and his younger officers." --Domei.

《上海星期泰晤士报》，1937年1月10日

南京必须决定
对华“赤色分子”的政策

当地日本报刊称中央当局必须
准备接受日本关于建立联合反共阵线的提议

上海《每日新闻》昨日宣称，南京政府必须一劳永逸地决定其对共产主义态度的时刻已经到来。

该刊断言，鉴于经历了共产主义的恐怖，中央行政当局必须准备接受日本关于建立联合反赤阵线的提议。

该日报称：“如果南京继续犹豫不决，我们不得不将其解读为一种表现，即一旦形势需要，南京便希望与共产党人结盟。”

“恐怕由于议会质询，日本政府在未来几周内对华政策将会强硬起来。南京拒绝联合反对共产主义，将使这一变化进一步加剧。

“另一方面，如果南京接受日本的提议，政府与共产党人之间将不可避免地发生激烈斗争，随之而来的是小军阀们的阴谋诡计和权术操纵。”

《日日报》在评论西安局势时断言，张学良将军和杨虎城将军完全无视与蒋介石将军达成的协议条款。

该报称，杨将军似乎不愿接受南京对其部队处置的命令。《日日报》将这种不服从解释为“杨将军及其下级军官苏维埃化”的结果。——同盟社。

January II, 1937.

NIPPO

CHINA'S POLICY TOWARDS COMMUNISTS

The Nippo publishes the following
comment on China's policy towards communists:-
It is a fact that the military
leaders of the North-West, including General Yang Hu
Chen, have been bolshevized and are now propagating
communism at Sian and Lanchow. To understand the
present situation in China the first thing one should
do is to consider the activities of the communists and
to ascertain which country is giving sincere advice to
China. Long ago, Japan foresaw the present situation
which will destroy China's unification and disturb peace
and order in the Far East. She urged China to accept
Sino-Japanese co-operation against the communists, but
she rejected it for she had some doubt about Japan's
motives. No matter how arrogant China may be, she cannot
claim that China is united in view of the present
situation. In no civilized country is the army divided
into two groups and will fight each other to decide the
country's foreign policy.
China's situation has become much
difficult since the Sian incident, because the Third
Internationale and Soviet Russia are behind the Sian
incident. Manchukuo and Japan will have to face
similar difficulties should the influence of the reds
increase in Sinkiang, Kansu, Shensi and Suiyuan provinces.
The Nanking Government has
sufficient military power to unite or disband the various
military forces, but she is not strong enough to deal with the
Third Internationale. For this reason, Japan has
suggested that Sino-Japanese co-operation against
communists be effected. At this critical moment, there
is only way for China to deal with the situation and
that is by accepting Japan's co-operative policy against
communists.
Certain influential Chinese
newspapers state that Japan, under the pretext of a
co-operative policy against communists and Soviet
Russia, is attempting to encroach upon China's territory,
but there is nothing that can cause a clash with Soviet
Russia because the Russo-Japanese Agreement has been
extended another year and Japan has announced that the
object of the German-Japanese Agreement was not directed
against Soviet Russia. The civil war in Spain shows
us what a terrible thing communism is.
The Chinese communists will pay
no attention to the measures adopted by the Nanking
Government. The Chinese authorities will be co-operating
with the communists should they accept General Yang
Hu Chen's political compromise; the other step is to
exterminate them. In case they adopt the first course
they will have to meet Japan face to face and if they
take the second course they will lose financial credit
in foreign countries.
Whatever condition Chiang Kai
Shek may have accepted to settle the Sian incident it
is an easy matter for the Nanking Government to launch
an attack on the rebels.

1937年1月11日。

《日日报》

中国的对共政策

《日日报》发表以下关于中国对共政策的评论：
事实是，包括杨虎城将军在内的西北军事领导人已经布尔什维克化，目前正在西安和兰州宣传共产主义。要了解中国目前的局势，首先要考虑共产党人的活动，并查明哪个国家在向中国提供真诚的建议。日本早已预见到当前这种将破坏中国统一并扰乱远东和平与秩序的局势。日本敦促中国接受中日合作反共，但中国因怀疑日本的动机而予以拒绝。无论中国多么傲慢，鉴于当前局势，她都不能声称中国是统一的。在任何文明国家，军队都不会分裂为两派并相互交战以决定国家的外交政策。
自西安事变以来，中国的处境变得更加困难，因为第三国际和苏俄是西安事变的幕后推手。如果红色势力在新疆、甘肃、陕西和绥远各省的影响扩大，满洲国和日本也将面临类似的困难。
南京政府拥有足够的军事力量来统一或解散各路军事力量，但其实力不足以对付第三国际。因此，日本建议实行中日合作反共。在这一关键时刻，中国应对局势的唯一途径就是接受日本的合作反共政策。
某些有影响力的中国报纸称，日本以合作反共和反对苏俄为借口，企图侵占中国领土，但由于《日俄协定》又延长了一年，且日本宣布《德日协定》的目标并非针对苏俄，因此没有任何理由会导致与苏俄发生冲突。西班牙内战向我们展示了共产主义是多么可怕的事情。
中国共产党人不会理会南京政府采取的措施。如果中国当局接受杨虎城将军的政治妥协方案，他们将与共产党人合作；另一条路则是消灭他们。如果他们采取第一条路，他们将不得不直面日本；如果他们采取第二条路，他们将在国外失去金融信用。
无论蒋介石为解决西安事变接受了什么条件，南京政府发动对叛军的攻击都是易事。

At this critical moment, we advise the Chinese authorities

MAINICHI

SIAN IS A CITY OF DEATH: ANTI-JAPANESE MOVEMENT
RAMPANT

The people of Sian are restless.
All strategic places are being guarded by soldiers
who search all pedestrians. Commercial and industrial
activities are at a standstill. On the night of
January 7 more than 17 leading merchants, bankers and
industrialists evacuated to Loyang and called on General
Kuo Chu Tung, the Field Headquarters Commissioner at Sian,
to request him to settle the Sian affair as quickly as
possible. General Kuo Chu Tung is unable to settle the
situation.

中国对共产党的政策

《日日新闻》就中国对共产党的政策发表如下评论：——
包括杨虎城将军在内的西北军事领袖已经布尔什维克化，并在西安和兰州传播共产主义，这是事实。要了解中国目前的局势，首先应该考察共产党的活动，并查明哪个国家在向中国提供真诚的建议。日本早就预见到这种会破坏中国统一并扰乱远东和平与秩序的当前局势。日本敦促中国接受中日合作以对抗共产党，但中国因怀疑日本的动机而予以拒绝。无论中国多么傲慢，鉴于目前的局势，她都不能声称中国是统一的。在任何文明国家，军队都不会分裂为两派并通过相互交战来决定国家的外交政策。
自西安事变以来，中国的处境变得更加困难，因为第三国际和苏俄是西安事变的幕后推手。如果红色势力在新疆、甘肃、陕西和绥远各省的影响扩大，满洲国和日本将不得不面对类似的困难。
南京政府拥有足够的军事力量来统一或解散各支军事力量，但其实力不足以对付第三国际。因此，日本建议实行中日合作以对抗共产党。在这一关键时刻，中国应对局势的唯一途径就是接受日本的合作反共政策。
某些有影响力的中国报纸称，日本以合作反共和对抗苏俄为借口，企图侵占中国领土，但由于《日俄协定》已再延长一年，且日本宣布《德日协定》的目的并非针对苏俄，因此没有任何理由会导致与苏俄发生冲突。西班牙内战向我们展示了共产主义是多么可怕的事情。
中国共产党不会理会南京政府采取的措施。如果中国当局接受杨虎城将军的政治妥协方案，他们将与共产党合作；另一条路则是将其剿灭。如果他们采取第一条路线，他们将不得不与日本正面相对；如果他们采取第二条路线，他们将失去在国外的金融信用。
无论蒋介石接受了什么条件来解决西安事变，南京政府发动对叛军的攻击都是易如反掌的事。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, January 8, 1937

Terms On Chiang
Release Claimed
In Sian, Tokyo

Compromise Condition
For Generalissimo's
Return Differ

NANKING DENIES
POLITICAL PACT

Yang Hu-cheng Openly
Defies Government,
Ready To Fight

While fresh friction is reported between Nanking and Shensi-Kansu leaders over the reorganization of the military and political administration in the two northwestern provinces, the existence of terms in Sian's dramatic release of General Chiang Kai-shek on the Christmas Day after a two-week captivity is claimed by two different sources today.

An account about the alleged set of six terms is contained in the December 27 issue of the "Emancipation Daily News," Sian newspaper published by the rebels. The paper was originally known as "See Ching Jih Pao" or the "West Capital Daily News" and was generally considered as a Nanking organ until its taking over by the mutineers shortly after December 12.

Six Terms
According to the "Emancipation Daily News," the terms for General Chiang's release from Sian were:
1. That the Central forces in Shensi west of Tungkuan be withdrawn as from December 25 and General Chiang should be held responsible for hostilities after that day.
2. That all civil strife be stopped in order that the national strength may be mobilized and turned against foreign aggressors.
3. That the National Government be reorganised and men of ability of various factions and those who advocate resistance against Japanese aggression be included.
4. That the foreign policy be revised in order that close relations or alliances may be arranged with countries sympathetic to China's cause.
5. That the leaders of the National Salvation Association be released immediately.
6. That the military and political administration in the Northwest be put under the control of Generals Chiang Hsueh-liang and Yang Hu-cheng.

Eight Other Terms
The second set of compromise terms allegedly reached in Sian between the envoys of the Central Government and General Chang Hsueh-liang, leader of the coup, is reported by the Domei Agency from Tokyo.
The terms, the reports asserted, were drawn up by Mme. Sun Yat-sen, widow of Dr. Sun, generally known as the "Father of the Chinese Revolution," and a prominent leader of the popular front.
The compromise, according to the reports, was guaranteed by Mr. T. V. Soong, Governor of the Bank of China; Mme. Chiang Kai-shek; Mr. W. H. Donald, British adviser to General Chiang Kai-shek; and Mr. James Elder, adviser to the "Young Marshal."

Terms Listed
The terms of the agreement, according to the reports, included:
1. Release of the Generalissimo from his captivity in Sian and guarantees for the safety of General Chang.
2. General Chiang's approval of the rebels' proposal for resistance to Japan which would be carried out with the completion of all necessary preparations, including rapprochement with Great Britain, France, Soviet Russia and the United States.
3. Suspension of punitive operations against Communists, although open co-operation with the Reds would not be effected;
4. The Nanking Government is to advance $10,000,000 to the "Young Marshal" and General Yang Hu-chen, another leader of the mutinous troops, to cover the military expenses.
5. A reorganization of the Nanking Government and dismissal of all pro Japanese officials from posts of responsibility.
6. Release of the six leaders of the popular front recently arrested in Shanghai, and now awaiting trial in Soochow.
7. Maintenance of secrecy regarding the entries made in his diary by General Chiang during his enforced stay in Sian;
8. Restoration of the status quo ante-incident in Sian and the withdrawal of all disciplinary and punitive measures against the "Young Marshal."

Chinese Denial
Chinese official circles, however, emphatically denied the existence of the reported compromise terms, claiming that General Chang had released General Chiang and escorted the latter to Loyang and Nanking because of his sincere repentance.
The situation in Shensi, according to reports today, is becoming worse. General Yang Hu-cheng, pacification commissioner of Shensi, has issued a proclamation on Tuesday announcing his determination to resist the Nanking forces because he and his colleagues have been "oppressed." The complete text of the proclamation, however, is not obtainable here today.

Clashes Reported
Sporadic clashes are reported along Hwahsien and Weinan areas between the Shensi troops and the Central armies. No major hostilities had occurred so far.
The Nanking authorities are anxiously seeking to avoid a major strife, preferring to settle the issues through political and peaceful means.

（批：D. 7675 / 9 1 37）

南京否认

杨虎城公开

尽管据报道，南京与陕甘两省领导人在重组这两个西北省份的军事和行政管理方面产生了新的摩擦，但今天有两个不同的消息来源声称，蒋介石将军在被囚禁两周后于圣诞节当天在西安戏剧性地获释，其间存在某些条件。

关于据称的六项条件的描述，刊登在叛军出版的西安报纸《解放日报》12月27日的版面上。该报原名《西京日报》，在12月12日不久后被兵变者接管之前，通常被视为南京方面的喉舌。

六项条件
据《解放日报》称，蒋介石从西安获释的条件是：
1. 中央军自12月25日起撤出潼关以西的陕西地区，此后发生的敌对行动应由蒋介石负责。
2. 停止一切内战，以便动员国力对抗外国侵略者。
3. 改组国民政府，吸纳各派能人以及主张抵抗日本侵略的人士。
4. 修改外交政策，以便与同情中国事业的国家建立密切关系或结盟。
5. 立即释放救国会领导人。
6. 西北地区的军事和行政管理置于张学良和杨虎城两位将军的控制之下。

另外八项条件
据东京同盟社报道，中央政府特使与政变领导人张学良将军在西安达成的第二套妥协条件如下。
报道称，这些条款由孙中山博士（通常被称为“中国革命之父”）的遗孀、人民阵线的著名领袖孙夫人起草。
据报道，该妥协方案由中国银行行长宋子文先生、蒋夫人、蒋介石将军的英国顾问W. H. Donald先生以及“少帅”的顾问James Elder先生担保。

列出的条款
据报道，协议条款包括：
1. 释放被囚禁在西安的总司令，并保证张学良将军的安全。
2. 蒋介石批准叛军提出的抗日提议，该提议将在完成所有必要准备工作后执行，包括与英国、法国、苏俄和美国修好。
3. 暂停对共产党的惩罚性行动，尽管不会与赤色分子进行公开合作；
4. 南京政府向“少帅”和另一位叛军领导人杨虎城将军预付1,000万美元，以支付军事费用。
5. 改组南京政府，罢免所有亲日官员的要职。
6. 释放最近在上海被捕、目前在苏州等待审判的六名人民阵线领导人。
7. 对蒋介石将军在西安被迫停留期间日记中所作记录保密；
8. 恢复西安事变前的原状，并撤销对“少帅”的所有纪律处分和惩罚措施。

中方否认
然而，中国官方圈子坚决否认存在报道中的妥协条款，声称张学良将军是因为真诚悔过才释放蒋介石将军，并护送后者前往洛阳和南京。
据今天的报道，陕西的局势正变得恶化。陕西绥靖主任杨虎城将军于周二发布告示，宣布决心抵抗南京军队，因为他和他的同僚受到“压迫”。然而，今天在此无法获得该告示的全文。

据报道发生冲突
据报道，陕西军队与中央军在华山和渭南地区发生了零星冲突。截至目前尚未发生重大敌对行动。
南京当局正焦急地寻求避免重大冲突，更倾向于通过政治和平手段解决问题。

（批注：D. 7675 / 9 1 37）

January 8, 1937.

NICH-NIC.I

CHANG HSUEH LIANG AND YANG FU CHEN'S DEMANDS IN SIAN
INCIDENT: SINO-JAPANESE RELATIONS THREATENED

According to a report published
by the Chinese newspaper "Chia Fang Daily News" of
December 13, 1936, Chang Hsueh Liang and Yang Fu Chen
issued the following demands in the Sian incident:-
1. That the Government be reorganized with members
of various political parties and cliques.
2. That the punitive campaign against bandits and
the civil war be suspended in order to deal with the
foreign enemy.
3. That the seven leaders of the national salvation
movement, including Sun Ching Tze and Chiang Nan Chi,
who were arrested in Shanghai, be released immediately.
4. That all political prisoners be released.
5. That freedom of speech, publication and assembly
be given to the people.
6. That patriotic movements be protected.
7. That a national salvation conference be called
immediately.
8. That the late Dr. Sun Yat Sen's will be sincerely
observed.

On December 15, 1936 the same
paper published a report to the effect that the anti-
bandit field headquarters was officially abolished on
December 14 thereby suspending the anti-bandit campaign.
At the same time, an anti-Japanese North-West United
Military Committee was formed with General Chang Hsueh
Liang and General Yang Fu Chen as chairman and vice-
chairman respectively.
The abolition of the anti-
bandit field headquarters in the North-West on January
5 by the Nanking Government is regarded as an acceptance
of the above demands by Nanking.

Three Japanese ministers to hold important
conference to consider Sian affair

As it is reported that the
Nanking Government appears to have accepted the demands
of General Chang Hsueh Liang for a settlement of the
Sian incident, which, if true, would endanger Sino-Japanese
relations, the War, Navy and Foreign Ministers of the
Tokyo Government will hold an important conference on
January 8 to consider the situation.

1937年1月8日。

NICH-NIC.I

张学良与杨虎城在西安事变中的要求：中日关系受到威胁

据1936年12月13日中文报纸《嘉芳日报》（音译）刊登的报道，张学良和杨虎城在西安事变中提出了以下要求：-
1. 改组政府，吸纳各政党及派系成员。
2. 停止剿匪及内战，以应对外敌。
3. 立即释放包括沈钧儒和章乃器在内的七位在上海被捕的救国会领袖。
4. 释放所有政治犯。
5. 给予人民言论、出版及集会自由。
6. 保护爱国运动。
7. 立即召开救国会议。
8. 真诚奉行已故孙中山博士的遗嘱。

1936年12月15日，该报又刊登报道指出，剿匪总司令部已于12月14日正式撤销，从而停止了剿匪行动。同时，成立了抗日西北联合军事委员会，由张学良将军和杨虎城将军分别担任正、副委员长。

南京政府于1月5日撤销西北剿匪总司令部，此举被视为南京方面接受了上述要求。

三位日本大臣将举行重要会议审议西安事件

据报道，南京政府似乎已接受张学良将军为解决西安事变而提出的要求，若此事属实，将危及中日关系，因此东京政府的陆军、海军和外务大臣将于1月8日举行重要会议，审议当前局势。

NICHI-NICHI

张学良与杨虎城在西安事变中的要求：中日关系受到威胁

据1936年12月13日中文报纸《嘉芳日报》（音译）刊登的报道，张学良和杨虎城在西安事变中提出了以下要求：-
1. 改组政府，吸纳各政党及派系成员。
2. 停止剿匪及内战，以应对外敌。
3. 立即释放包括沈钧儒和章乃器在内的七位在上海被捕的救国会领袖。
4. 释放所有政治犯。
5. 给予人民言论、出版及集会自由。
6. 保护爱国运动。
7. 立即召开救国会议。
8. 真诚奉行已故孙中山博士的遗嘱。

1936年12月15日，该报又刊登报道指出，剿匪总司令部已于12月14日正式撤销，从而停止了剿匪行动。同时，成立了抗日西北联合军事委员会，由张学良将军和杨虎城将军分别担任正、副委员长。

南京政府于1月5日撤销西北剿匪总司令部，此举被视为南京方面接受了上述要求。

三位日本大臣将举行重要会议审议西安事件

据报道，南京政府似乎已接受张学良将军为解决西安事变而提出的要求，若此事属实，将危及中日关系，因此东京政府的陆军、海军和外务大臣将于1月8日举行重要会议，审议当前局势。

January 7, 1937. Afternoon Translation

NIPPO

FIELD HEADQUARTERS IN THE NORTH-WEST ABOLISHED; ANTI-
RED CAMPAIGN SUSPENDED

Following the Government's
special pardon of Chang Hsueh Liang, the Executive Yuan
held a conference on the morning of January 5 at which
the punishment of General Yang Fu Chung and General Yu
Hsueh Chung was decided.
On the afternoon of January 6
the Nanking Government issued an order abolishing the
anti-communist Field Headquarters in the North-West. This
action has solved the doubts about a reported political
compromise between the Nanking Government and Chang Hsueh
Liang; the step will suspend the anti-Red campaign. The
Government has changed its policy towards the red army
whose influence has suddenly become greater in Kansu and
Shensi provinces since the Sian incident.
The Nanking Government has
made an evasive explanation stating that it is intended as
a measure dealing first with Chang Hsueh Liang's troops
stationed in the vicinity of Sian. General Yang Fu
Chung, rebel leader, and General Yu Hsueh Chung will
remain at their posts to atone their mistakes by good
work.
As a result of the Government's
special pardon, Chang Hsueh Liang, who has regained his
personal freedom, will return to Sian in a day or two.
The above shows that the Sian
incident has been settled by means of political measure.

1937年1月7日。下午译文

NIPPO

西北总部撤销；剿共行动暂停

继政府对张学良实行特赦后，行政院于1月5日上午召开会议，决定了对杨虎城将军和于学忠将军的惩处。
1月6日下午，南京政府发布命令，撤销西北剿共总司令部。这一举措消除了关于南京政府与张学良之间达成政治妥协传闻的疑虑；此举将暂停剿赤行动。政府改变了对红军的政策，自西安事变以来，红军在甘肃和陕西省的影响力突然增大。
南京政府作出含糊其辞的解释，称此举旨在首先处理驻扎在西安附近的张学良部队。叛军首领杨虎城将军和于学忠将军将留任原职，以良好工作表现赎罪。
由于政府实行特赦，重获人身自由的张学良将在一两天内返回西安。
以上情况表明，西安事变已通过政治手段得以解决。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JANUARY 5, 1937
Pardon Granted To Chang
Hsueh-liang; He Remains
Temporarily In Custody
Action Taken By State Council On Recommendation
Of Generalissimo; Handed Over For Time Being
To Military Affairs Commission Custody
VETERAN GENERALS ARRIVE IN NANKING
TO DISCUSS DISPOSAL OF TROOPS
NANKING, Jan. 4.--Chang Hsueh-liang, leader of the
Shensi revolt, this morning was granted a special pardon on the
recommendation of his former captive, General Chiang Kai-
shek, President of the Executive Yuan and Chairman of the
Military Affairs Commission.
This action was taken at a meeting of the State Council
after hearing explanations of their verdict by the three military
tribunal judges, Generals Li Lieh-chun, Chu Pei-teh and Lu
Chung-lin, who sentenced Chang to 10 years' imprisonment on
Thursday and by the President of the Judicial Yuan, Mr. Chu
Cheng.
The Council, however, ordered Chang Hsueh-liang to be
handed over temporarily to the custody of the Military Affairs
Commission with instructions to keep him "under strict sur-
veillance." It is not yet known whether Chang is to be rein-
stated to his command of the North-West Bandit-Suppression
forces.
Generals Liu Cheh and Mo Teh-
hui, veteran Manchurian leaders,
who arrived in Nanking this morn-
ing, called on General Ho Ying-
ching, Minister of War, to discuss
the position of Chang's troops,
which consist mainly of the former
Manchurian forces known as the
North-Eastern army. They number
about 100,000.
Chang Gets News
Chang received first news of the
pardon from Mr. T. V. Soong, head
of the National Economic Council
and Governor of the Bank of China,
who arrived in Nanking from
Shanghai by air this morning to
attend the meeting of the State
Council.
After the meeting Mr. Soong pro-
ceeded to the residence of Dr. H.
H. Kung, Minister of Finance,
where Chang is being held under
detention, and told the "Young
Marshal" of the decision.--Reuter.
State Council Meeting
NANKING, Jan. 4.--The recom-
mendation of General Chiang Kai-
shek, President of the Executive
Yuan and Chairman of the Mili-
tary Affairs Commission, for the
special pardon for Chang Hsueh-
liang, leader of the Sian revolt,
was approved at the meeting of
the State Council at 11 o'clock this
morning.
Mr. Lin Sen, President of the
National Government who presided
at the meeting, reported on the re-
sult of the examination of General
Chiang's recommendation by the
Judicial Yuan while Mr. Chu
Cheng, President of the Judicial
Yuan, supplemented by dwelling
on the legal aspects of the case.
The meeting adjourned at noon
and it is reliably learned that the
National Government will issue a
mandate to-night officially an-
nouncing the special pardon for
Chang Hsueh-liang.
Mr. T. V. Soong, Chairman of
the Board of Directors of the Bank
of China who accompanied Chang
Hsueh-liang from Sian to the
capital on December 26, arrived
here this morning from Fenghua,
via Shanghai, was also present at
the State Council meeting. Mr.
Soong went to Fenghua yesterday
to call on General Chiang Kai-shek
and to pay his respects to the late
Mr. Chiang Hsi-hou, brother of the
Generalissimo.--Central News.
Military Tribunal's Judgment
NANKING, Jan. 3.--The follow-
ing is a full translation of the
judgment rendered by the Military
Tribunal specially constituted by
the Military Tribunal specially con-
stituted by the Military Affairs
Commission for the trial of Gen-
eral Chang Hsueh-liang, leader of
the Sian revolt:--
"Accused: Chang Hsueh-liang.
The above defendant, charged
with violence against and threat to
a superior official, has been tried
by the High Military Tribunal
organized by this Commission.
Judgment is hereby pronounced
as follows:
Text: Chang Hsueh-liang, having
been found guilty of planning and
organizing a conspiracy for violence
against and threat to a superior
official, is hereby given a reduced
sentence of ten years' imprison-
ment, with deprivation of civic
rights for a period of five years.
Facts: In December of the 25th
Year of the Republic of China
(1936), Chiang Chung-cheng
(Chiang Kai-shek), President of
this Commission, proceeded from
Loyang to Shensi on official busi-
ness, taking up his temporary quar-
ters at Lintung. At dawn on the
12th, Chang Hsueh-liang, at the
head of his subordinates, seized,
and held, at Sian, and tried to
force President Chiang to accept his
proposals relating to the reorgan-
ization of the Government and
other matters.
Persons Killed
At that time Shao Yuan-chung,
member of the Central Executive
Committee, who had proceeded to
Shensi on official business; Chiang
Hsiao-hsien, Chief of the Third
Section of the Generalissimo's Ad-
jutants' Office; Hsiao Nai-hua, Sec-
retary; and several attendants,
public functionaries and guards; as
well as Yang Chen-ya, Commander
of the Military Police Regiment
stationed in Shensi, after learning
of the revolt, resisted, and were
all killed.
Chien Ta-chun, Director of the
Adjutants' Office, was also wound-
ed.

cials in Shensi, including:

张学良获特赦；暂时仍被羁押
国民政府根据委员长建议采取行动；暂移交军事委员会监管
老将抵南京商讨部队处置事宜

南京，1月4日电——陕西事变领袖张学良，今晨根据其昔日囚禁对象、行政院院长兼军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军的建议，获准特赦。

此项决定是在国务会议上作出的。会上听取了三位军事法庭法官——李烈钧、朱培德和陆钟麟将军的解释，他们于周四判处张学良有期徒刑十年；以及司法院院长居正先生的解释。

然而，会议命令将张学良暂时移交军事委员会监管，并指示对其“严加监视”。目前尚不清楚张学良是否会复任西北剿匪总司令之职。

刘哲和莫德惠两位资深东北籍将领今晨抵达南京，拜会军政部长何应钦将军，商讨张学良部队的处境。该部队主要由原被称为东北军的旧满洲军队组成，人数约十万。

张学良得知消息

张学良最初是从全国经济委员会主席兼中国银行行长宋子文先生处得知获赦消息的。宋氏今晨由上海乘飞机抵南京出席国务会议。

会后，宋先生前往财政部长孔祥熙博士的寓所，张学良正被拘禁于此，宋向这位“少帅”通报了这一决定。——路透社

国务会议

南京，1月4日电——行政院院长兼军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军关于特赦西安事变领袖张学良的建议，于今晨11时的国务会议上获得批准。

主持会议的国民政府主席林森报告了司法院对蒋将军建议的审查结果，司法院院长居正先生则从法律角度作了补充说明。

会议于中午休会，据可靠消息，国民政府将于今晚发布命令，正式宣布对张学良的特赦。

中国银行董事长宋子文先生于12月26日陪同张学良从西安来到首都，他今晨经上海从奉化抵达此处，也出席了国务会议。宋先生昨日前往奉化拜访蒋介石将军，并向委员长已故兄长蒋锡侯先生致祭。——中央通讯社

军事法庭判决

南京，1月3日电——以下是由军事委员会特别组建、用于审判西安事变领袖张学良将军的军事法庭所作判决的完整译文：

“被告：张学良。

上述被告被控对上级官员实施暴力和威胁，已由本委员会组织的高等军事法庭进行审理。

兹宣判如下：

主文：张学良因策划并组织阴谋对上级官员实施暴力和威胁罪名成立，兹减刑判处有期徒刑十年，剥夺公权五年。

事实：中华民国二十五年（1936年）十二月，本委员会委员长蒋中正（蒋介石）因公由洛阳赴陕西，暂驻临潼。12日凌晨，张学良率领部下在西安扣押并拘禁委员长，企图强迫委员长接受其关于改组政府及其他事项的主张。

遇害人员

当时因公赴陕的中央执行委员邵元冲；委员长侍从室第三处处长蒋孝先；秘书萧乃华；以及数名随从、公务人员和卫士；还有驻陕宪兵团团长杨震亚，在获悉事变后进行了抵抗，均遭杀害。

侍从室主任钱大钧亦受伤。

陕西多名政府高官，包括：

In view of these extenuating cir-
cumstances, his crime does not ex-
clude leniency. In accordance with

the first part of Section 2 of Article

his civic rights for a period of 5
years.
Sentence is hereby specially pass-

the judgment.
Judgment rendered on Dec. 31 of
the 25th Year of the Republic of
China (1936).
(Signed) Li Lieh-chun, Presiding

Chu Pei-te and Lu Chung-lin,

陈调元（军事参议院院长）；蒋作宾（内政部长）；朱绍良（兰州绥靖公署主任）；邵力子（陕西省政府主席）；蒋鼎文（福建绥靖公署主任及新任西北剿匪前线总指挥）；陈诚（军政部政务次长）；卫立煌（晋陕宁绥边区剿匪军野战司令）；陈继承（豫鄂陕边区绥靖专员）；以及万耀煌（第二十五军军长）也被扣留。

张学良受到委员长斥责后，随后表示悔悟，并于当月25日陪同委员长赴京请罪。

事变爆发时，国民政府将张学良移送本委员会从严惩处。后收到张学良所写悔过书一封。

本委员会为审理此案组织的高等军事法庭已查明上述事实。

理由：本案被告张学良率领部下（军队）扣押委员长，并施压迫使蒋介石将军接受其关于改组政府及其他事项的主张，此点由被告发布的通电证实。

杀害政府官员和扣留军事指挥官是不争的事实。虽然这些行为由其部下实施，但显然系由被告唆使，因此被告应承担责任。

从其行为来看，他违反了《陆海空军刑法》第六十七条第二款第一项；《刑法》第二百七十一条第一、二款及第三百零二条第一款。

然而，其所犯罪行性质属于一行为触犯数罪；或犯一罪而其方法或结果行为触犯他罪。

依据《陆海空军刑法》第五十五条和第十五条，以及《刑法》第六十七条第二款第一项，应按所犯最重之罪判刑。

但是，被告在受到委员长斥责后表示悔悟，并随同前往首都请罪。

判决

鉴于这些减轻情节，对其罪行不妨从宽处理。依据《刑法》第五十九条及《陆海空军刑法》第六十七条第二款第一项，被告兹减刑判处有期徒刑十年；并依据《刑法》第三十七条第二款，剥夺公权五年。

兹特依判决主文宣判。

判决于中华民国二十五年（1936年）12月31日作出。

袁祖贤、郭佐民，书记官”——《国民新闻》

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated January 4 :-

MOVEMENTS OF GENERAL CHANG CHUN

General Chang Chun, Minister for Foreign

staying at the Ta-Hwa Hotel.

Diamond (金鋼鑽), a mosquito paper :-

"A STRANGE STORY OF SHANGHAI"

Not long ago, four high class women
rented a room in a certain hotel in the International
Settlement of Shanghai to play mahjong. The game ended
late at night. Two of them left the hotel, while the
other two remained.
One of the women who remained in the
room went to sleep; the other could not sleep. The
latter saw a man sitting in front of the window and
became afraid.
She said to her companion, "Where
did this man come from? Get up quickly."
The woman was so sleepy that she gave
an indistinct reply. The other woman then quickly put
on her dress and left.
The sleeping woman woke up later.
The man in front of the window was still there. She
called a waiter whereupon the man began gradually to
fade in the direction of the bed but beneath it.
As it was thought that the man might
be an evil-doer, a telephone message was sent to the
Police. Officers soon arrived and found a dead body
secured to the mattress.
For the sake of the reputation of the
four high class women, the authorities are keeping the
matter secret.

“上海奇闻”

不久前，四位上层社会妇女在上海公共租界某旅馆租用一间房间打麻将。牌局结束得很晚。其中两人离开旅馆，另外两人留下。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JANUARY 1, 1937.
16205

Sentence Of 10 Years'
Imprisonment Passed
On Chang Hsueh-liang

Leader Of Sian Affair
Recommended To
Get Clemency

SOONG ESCORTS
HIM TO TRIAL

Gen. Li Presides And
Defendant Examined
For 1½ Hours

Chang Hsueh-liang, leader of the
Sianfu coup was sentenced by
court-martial yesterday to 10 years'
imprisonment, according to a Cen-
tral News report last night. Cen-
tral News also reported that Gene-
ralissimo Chiang Kai-shek had
petitioned for clemency in regard to
the "Young Marshal."

At Kung Residence
NANKING, Dec. 31.—(Reuters).
—Chang is now under nominal
detention at the residence of Dr.
H. H. Kung, Minister of Finance,
whither he was accompanied by a
representative of the court-martial
on the conclusion of the trial.

The court-martial, a special
tribunal of the Military Affairs
Commission, opened at 10 o'clock
this morning. Chang Hsueh-liang
appeared promptly, escorted by
Mr. T. V. Soong, head of the
National Economic Council and
Governor of the Bank of China,
who had accompanied him to Nan-
king from Sianfu.

General Li Lieh-chun, who pre-
sided, questioned the "Young
Marshal" on eight points.

In reply, Chang Hsueh-liang ex-
plained that the motive of the
Sianfu coup was entirely based on
a desire to achieve freedom and
equality of the country and race in
the family of nations, and he him-
self must shoulder full re-
sponsibility.

He had always had the respect
for General Chiang Kai-shek
(President of the Executive Yuan
and Chairman of the Military
Affairs Commission, whom he had
detained at Sianfu for over 13 days)
and would support him to the end.

After a cross-examination last-
ing 1½ hours, the verdict was
pronounced, and Chang Hsueh-
liang, accompanied by a repre-
sentative of the tribunal, proceed-
ed to Dr. Kung's residence, where,
he will remain under nominal de-
tention.

The verdict of the court will be
announced in a mandate which is
being issued by the Government to-
night.

2 Assistant Judges
NANKING, Dec. 31.—(Kuomin).
—The presiding judge was General
Li Lieh-chun, with General Chu
Pei-teh and General Lu Chung-lin
as Assistant Judges:

The accused was tried on eight
counts. He accepted sole respon-
sibility for the Sian revolt and said
that he acted in the interests of
the State and the people. He affirm-
ed that he had no intention what-
ever of doing any harm to General-
issimo Chiang Kai-shek or anybody
else, and deeply regretted the loss
of life and injury which occurred.
"Whatever decision the Court
renders, I will cheerfully accept,"
the defendant said.

The Court sat from 10 a.m. until
11.30 a.m. but did not render its
decision until late this afternoon.

Pending announcement of the
judgment, the defendant was
ordered to stay at the residence of
Dr. H. H. Kung, Vice-President of
the Executive Yuan, under military
and police protection.

It is generally understood that
Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek
will appeal to the National Govern-
ment for clemency on behalf of
General Chiang Hsueh-liang.

（印：2 JAN 1937）

16205

判处十年监禁
张学良

西安事变首领
获建议从宽处理

宋子文护送
其受审

李将军主持
被告受审一个半小时

据昨晚中央社报道，西安事变首领张学良昨日被军事法庭判处十年监禁。中央社还报道，蒋委员长已为这位“少帅”请求宽恕。

在孔祥熙寓所
南京，12月31日。（路透社）。——张学良目前名义上被软禁在财政部长孔祥熙博士的寓所，审判结束后，由军事法庭代表陪同前往此处。

军事委员会特别法庭于今日上午10时开庭。张学良准时出庭，由全国经济委员会主席兼中国银行行长宋子文先生陪同护送，宋氏此前曾陪同他从西安来到南京。

主审法官李烈钧将军就八个问题讯问了这位“少帅”。

张学良回答说，西安事变的动机完全基于追求国家与民族在国际大家庭中的自由与平等，他本人愿承担全部责任。

他对蒋介石将军（行政院院长兼军事委员会委员长，他在西安将其扣押了13天以上）始终怀有敬意，并将支持到底。

经过一个半小时的交叉讯问后，宣判了判决结果，张学良在法庭代表的陪同下前往孔祥熙博士寓所，他将在那里继续接受名义上的软禁。

法院的判决将通过政府今晚发布的命令予以公布。

两名陪审法官
南京，12月31日。（《国民公报》）。——主审法官为李烈钧将军，陪审法官为朱培德将军和陆钟麟将军：

被告因八项罪名受审。他承认对西安叛乱负全部责任，并称其行为是为了国家和人民的利益。他肯定自己绝无意伤害蒋委员长或任何其他人，并对发生的伤亡深表遗憾。“无论法庭作出何种裁决，我都乐意接受，”被告说。

法庭从上午10时开庭至11时30分，但直到今天下午较晚时候才作出裁决。

在等待宣布判决期间，被告奉命留在行政院副院长孔祥熙博士的寓所，由军警保护。

据普遍了解，蒋委员长将代表张学良将军向国民政府请求宽恕。

（批注：3. 7675 37）
（印章：1937年1月2日）

January 2, 1937. Morning Translation No. 4937

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking telegram) -
GENERAL CHANG HSUEH LIANG SENTENCED TO TEN YEARS' IMPRISONMENT

General Chang Hsueh Liang was sentenced by court-martial on December 31, 1936 to ten years' imprisonment and deprivation of civil rights for five years in connection with the recent coup in Sianfu.
At 4 p.m. the same day he was removed in a prison van from Dr. H.H. Kung's residence to the Military Gaol where he will be confined until a special pardon is granted by the National Government.

Generalissimo Requests Pardon of General Chang Hsueh Liang

As soon as he learned of the sentence passed by the court-martial on General Chang Hsueh Liang, Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek at 2 p.m. on December 31 submitted a petition to the National Government requesting that in view of his voluntary surrender General Chang Hsueh Liang be granted a special pardon.

Generalissimo Flies to His Native Place

On the morning of January 1, Generalissimo and Madame Chiang Kai Shek left Nanking for Fenghua by aeroplane to attend to the funeral of his late brother. He is on one month's leave.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-
Martial Law in Shanghai Lifted

The Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters has issued the following notification :-
"Martial law was proclaimed in this locality shortly after the outbreak of the revolt in Sianfu. This Headquarters is now in receipt of a telegram from the Military Affairs Commission stating that the Sianfu revolt having been settled, the martial law should be lifted. Accordingly, this Headquarters hereby notifies the public that the martial law is cancelled from date."

Lih Pao published the following editorial on January 1 :-
"OUR NEW YEAR WISHES"

We wish the New Year will bring us the following two things :-
1. Real National Unification
With the settlement of the Kwangtung-Kwongsi problem, the nation appears to be unified. But remember that one-sixth of our territory comprising the Three Eastern Provinces, Jehol, the northern part of Chahar and a number of hsiens in North China, with a population of several tens of millions, are still under the control of our enemy. We wish that in 1937, the 26th year of the Republic, these territories will be replaced in the map of China. We wish that with the coming of 1937 the Hopei-Chahar Political Council and the Tangku Truce will become things of the past and Yang Ju Keng and other traitors will be executed one after another.

张学良将军被判十年监禁

同日下午4时，他被囚车从孔祥熙博士寓所移送至军事监狱，在国民政府给予特赦之前，他将在此关押。

委员长请求宽恕张学良将军

蒋介石委员长获悉军事法庭对张学良将军的判决后，于12月31日下午2日向国民政府提交请愿书，鉴于其自愿投案，请求对张学良将军给予特赦。

委员长飞回故乡

1月1日上午，蒋委员长及蒋夫人乘飞机离开南京前往奉化，参加其亡弟的葬礼。他休假一个月。

上海戒严令解除

淞沪卫戍司令总部发布如下通告：

《立报》于1月1日发表以下社论：
“我们的新年愿望”

我们希望新年能带来以下两件事：
1. 真正的国家统一
随着两广问题的解决，国家似乎已经统一。但请记住，我国六分之一的领土，包括东北三省、热河、察哈尔北部以及华北的若干县，拥有数千万人口，仍处在敌人的控制之下。我们希望在这民国二十六年（1937年），这些领土能重新出现在中国地图上。我们希望随着1937年的到来，冀察政务委员会和《塘沽协定》成为过去，殷汝耕及其他汉奸将被逐一处决。

张学良将军因近期西安事变，于1936年12月31日被军事法庭判处十年监禁，并剥夺公权五年。
同日下午4时，他被囚车从孔祥熙博士寓所移送至军事监狱，在国民政府给予特赦之前，他将在此关押。

委员长请求宽恕张学良将军

蒋介石委员长获悉军事法庭对张学良将军的判决后，于12月31日下午2日向国民政府提交请愿书，鉴于其自愿投案，请求对张学良将军给予特赦。

委员长飞回故乡

1月1日上午，蒋委员长及蒋夫人乘飞机离开南京前往奉化，参加其亡弟的葬礼。他休假一个月。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

上海戒严令解除

淞沪卫戍司令总部发布如下通告：
“西安事变爆发后不久，本地区宣布戒严。本总部现收到军事委员会电报，称西安事变已平息，应解除戒严。据此，本总部特此通知公众，自即日起取消戒严。”

《立报》于1月1日发表以下社论：

“我们的新年愿望”

我们希望新年能带来以下两件事：
1. 真正的国家统一
随着两广问题的解决，国家似乎已经统一。但请记住，我国六分之一的领土，包括东北三省、热河、察哈尔北部以及华北的若干县，拥有数千万人口，仍处在敌人的控制之下。我们希望在这民国二十六年（1937年），这些领土能重新出现在中国地图上。我们希望随着1937年的到来，冀察政务委员会和《塘沽协定》成为过去，殷汝耕及其他汉奸将被逐一处决。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 23, 1936
（批：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL S. D. REC... S. R. D. 7675 28 / 12 36）

BUDDHISTS, TAOISTS
PETITION HEAVEN

Praying for Safe Return of
Gen. Chiang Kai-shek

SPECIAL SERVICE HELD
AT SINZA TEMPLE

Three petitions for the safe return
of Gen. Chiang Kai-shek from Sian
are being sent to Heaven by hun-
dreds of Buddhists and Taoists in
a three-day service which began on
Monday night. Mr. Shao Lu-shing,
one of the sponsors of the prayer
meeting, told a representative of the
"North-China Daily News" yesterday
that since he had devoted himself to
the service, he had a feeling which
enabled him to predict the General-
issimo's freedom within the next three
days.

The Buddhists and Taoists are
gathering in two separate buildings
in Tsing Liang Temple, Sinza Road.
In front of each building are ex-
hibited a group of gorgeously em-
broidered umbrellas, while a huge
pallou made of yellow cloth was
erected at the entrance to the temple.
The two buildings are expected to
be filled to capacity to-day when the
second petition is to be sent, and a
still larger crowd is expected to wit-
ness the closing ceremony.

Sponsored by the World Peace
Meeting Preparations Committee, the
service is the second of its kind held
in Shanghai, the first taking place in
the Moore Memorial Church in Yu
Ya Ching Road on Sunday when over
600 Chinese Christians prayed for
Gen. Chiang. Similar prayer meet-
ings are being planned by adherents
of other religions.

Abbot Tsinghai Presides

Abbot Tsinghai, former chairman
of the National Buddhist Association,
presided over the service by Budd-
hists. Well-known abbots from Hang-
chow and Pootoo are also taking part
in the closing ceremony. Among the
sponsors are Messrs. Wen Lai-ting,
Wang In-ting, Yu Wei-chow, Hsu Kai-
ling, Loh Lien-kwei, Chao Yung-chao,
Yu Sheng-po, Tung Sing-yuan, Fong
King-chun, Chu Wei-sung, Chao Yu-
kwei, Chien Yo and Chen Kuan-tso.

Only vegetarians are admitted in
the two buildings where the cere-
monies take place. In addition to
monks and Taoists, scores of men and
women who follow the religions also
attended. Each petition, written on a
piece of yellow paper, is burnt after
a certain number of hymns have been
recited by the gathering.

Meanwhile meetings were held by
public bodies and university students
yesterday, urging the Government to
capture Chang Hsueh-liang and sup-
press the revolt at an early date.
Under the auspices of the Shanghai
Kuomintang Headquarters, a meeting
of representatives of public bodies
will be held at the Chinese Chamber
of Commerce to-morrow afternoon to
pledge local support to the punitive
expedition ordered by the Govern-
ment against the Sian rebels.

Mr. Chou Lu Due

Mr. Chou Lu, President of the
Chung Shan University at Canton,
is due in Shanghai on Christmas Day
in the Empress of Asia en route
to Nanking to take part in the discus-
sions on the Sian revolt.

Mr. Chou made a dramatic exit
from Canton last summer just be-
fore the open rift between the South-
west and Nanking, and spent several
months visiting various institutions
in Europe. He returned to Canton
late in the fall but owing to poor
health he was unable to come to
Nanking.

BUDDHISTS PETITION HEAVEN
N.C.D.N. Photos.

Hundreds of Buddhists are gathering at Tsing Liang Temple, Sinza Road,
for a three-day special service to pray for the safe return of Gen. Chiang
Kai-shek. Pictures above show those who took part in the prayer meeting
yesterday. The ceremony consists of the recitation of hymns and the burning
of three petitions to Heaven.

佛教徒、道教徒
祈天

祈求蒋介石将军
平安归来

在新闸寺庙举行
特别法会

数百名佛教徒和道教徒正在举行为期三天的法会，始于周一晚间，他们将三份祈求蒋介石将军从西安平安归来的表文上达天听。祈祷会的发起人之一邵鲁生（Shao Lu-shing，音译）先生昨日告诉《字林西报》记者，自从他投身于此次法会以来，他有一种感觉，使他能预测委员长将在未来三天内获得自由。

佛教徒和道教徒聚集在新闸路清凉寺内的两座独立建筑中。每座建筑前都陈列着一组绣工华丽的伞盖，寺庙入口处竖起了一座巨大的黄色布制幡幢。预计今天发送第二份表文时，这两座建筑将座无虚席，而预计将有更多人群见证闭幕仪式。

此次法会由世界和平会议筹备委员会发起，是上海举行的第二次此类活动，第一次于周日在虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）的慕尔纪念堂（Moore Memorial Church）举行，当时有600多名中国基督徒为蒋介石将军祈祷。其他宗教的信徒也在策划类似的祈祷会。

静海法师主持

前中国佛教会理事长静海法师主持了佛教徒的法会。来自杭州和普陀山的知名方丈也将参加闭幕仪式。发起人包括：温来庭（Wen Lai-ting，音译）、王因庭（Wang In-ting，音译）、俞维周（Yu Wei-chow，音译）、徐开灵（Hsu Kai-ling，音译）、罗连贵（Loh Lien-kwei，音译）、赵永兆（Chao Yung-chao，音译）、俞盛波（Yu Sheng-po，音译）、董星元（Tung Sing-yuan，音译）、冯金春（Fong King-chun，音译）、朱维松（Chu Wei-sung，音译）、赵玉桂（Chao Yu-kwei，音译）、钱耀（Chien Yo，音译）和陈观佐（Chen Kuan-tso，音译）。

只有素食者才被允许进入举行仪式的两座建筑。除了僧侣和道士外，还有数十名信奉这些宗教的男女信徒参加。每份写在黄纸上的表文，在集会诵唱一定数量的赞美诗后被焚化。

与此同时，公共团体和大学生昨日举行会议，敦促政府尽快逮捕张学良并镇压叛乱。在上海国民党党部的支持下，各公共团体代表将于明日下午在总商会举行会议，宣誓支持政府下令对西安叛军进行的讨伐行动。

周陆先生抵沪

广州中山大学校长周陆（Chou Lu，音译）先生预计将于圣诞节当天乘坐“亚洲皇后”号（Empress of Asia）抵达上海，途经前往南京，参与关于西安事变的讨论。

去年夏天，就在西南派与南京方面公开决裂前夕，周先生戏剧性地离开了广州，并在欧洲访问了数月机构。他于深秋返回广州，但由于健康状况不佳，未能前往南京。

December 19, 1936. Morning Translation.

Organizations are being formed by youths in Tientsin to search for members of Chang's family in order to send them to Nanking to be held as hostages against the release of General Chiang Kai Shek by Chang Hsueh Liang.

Attitude of Former Officials of the North-East

General Chang Tso Siang, ex-Governor of Kirin Province, is in Tientsin. All the elder members of the North-East clique are highly indignant at the action of General Chang Hsueh Liang, and have warned their relatives and friends against having any social intercourse with the family of General Chang Hsueh Liang. A certain retired high official of the North-East clique on December 18 sent a private letter to General Chang Hsueh Liang advising him to repent before it is too late.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

Arrival of Mr. Elder, Economic Advisor to General Chang Hsueh Liang

On December 16, Mr. James Elder, economic advisor to General Chang Hsueh Liang, left Sian for Nanking by aeroplane. When passing through Pengpu, the plane alighted owing to heavy rain. Mr. Elder then took a train and arrived at Nanking on December 18.
Upon reaching the Capital, Mr. Elder kept his movements very secret. He called on Dr. H.H. Kung, but did not meet other high Government officials.
Mr. Elder arrived in Shanghai at 11 p.m. yesterday from Nanking by train. He travelled first class, but he alighted from a second class carriage. Lest his whereabouts should become known to the public, he took a ricsha to Zung Chi Road (亿济路) where he hired a motor car from the Ford Hire Service to take him to the residence of Dr. H.H. Kung on Route Herve de Sieyes, French Concession.
The public are paying much attention to the movements and activities of Mr. Elder.

Lih Pao :-

No Japanese at Sian

Following the revolt in Sian, the authorities of foreign countries in China are paying close attention to the safety of their residents in Sian.
Mr. Yatani of the Intelligence Section of the Japanese Embassy declares that there are no Japanese residents in Sian.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, December 24, 1936 18080
What Happened At Sian?
(In Two Parts-Part One)
PRECISELY what happened at Sian? There have been many rumors but little to substantiate their details. The following summary, based on reports received by foreign correspondents in Peiping from Taiyuan, where it was brought by delegates from Sian, has been checked in a variety of quarters and may be taken as representing the facts, though there are differences of interpretation which will be noted.

General Chang Hsueh-liang's Tungpei, or "Northeastern Army", has long been disaffected. Dispossessed of its Manchuria homeland and resentful against Japan, it objected to its role of opposing the Chinese Communists. As the Communist policy turned toward stress on "national resistance" at the expense of all other features of policy, some form of entente must have been easy enough to achieve—a development certain to annoy General Chiang Kai-shek exceedingly.

At once we come to conflicts of interpretation, which may be dismissed briefly. In some quarters to the northward there is an apparently full belief in the sincerity of the Tungpei officers. We have access to other quarters by no means unfriendly to 'the young Marshal' which take a considerably more cynical view, believing that the Tungpei aims less at the Japanese than at domination by Nanking, and finding the whole situation comparable to the 1933 "Foochow rebellion"—where, it will be recalled, there was a similar "marriage of convenience" with the Communists of interior Fukien and similar protestations of regard for the national weal.

These conflicts of interpretation come to a head on the issue of General Chiang's attitude. It seems to us feasible that the Generalissimo may have been at once annoyed by liaison between Tungpei and Communists, and still sincerely determined to resist Japan in his own way. But to those cynically disposed toward the Generalissimo's intentions as to Japan, his insistence upon a "fight-the-Communists" policy for the Tungpei would seem clear proof that he preferred civil war to the demanded war against Japan. And to many Chinese of all shades of thought, the notion of fighting an invader is explicably more congenial than the notion of fighting fellow-Chinese.

General Chang had been completely loyal toward the Generalissimo but he found himself increasingly torn between this and instinctive loyalty to his own men. Announcement of the Japan-German treaty raised fresh doubts as to Nanking's sincerity, for among the Tungpei it was said that no such open agreement could have been made without private assurances from General Chiang. Italian recognition of "Manchukuo" posed the same problem. Our own view is that all this is 100 per cent rot, but from the viewpoint of interior China it all seems to us to hang together very well and if Nanking has been misunderstood the fault has been Nanking's, in our opinion; unless, of course, one is so out of sympathy with any criticism of Nanking that it is felt the whole thing was cooked up by Sian politician-propagandists. Usually in such a tangled state of affairs there is some truth to every point of view, no matter how many!

The Suiyuan and Tsingtao crises provoked fresh discussion, and though General Chiang sent three divisions to Suiyuan, the Tungpei felt that this was done tardily and that they took no part in the fighting but occupied positions in the rear and flank of Fu Tso-yi in Suiyuan and Shansi. Nanking planes had been ordered to Suiyuan, said the reports; but not a single machine took part in offensive operations. In late October, General Chang is said to have sent urgent wires to General Chiang, urging a policy of flat resistance and a united front with the "Anti-Japanese Red Army"—only to meet flat refusal.

General Chiang visited Sian in the first week of October and the Young Marshal had hopes of persuading him to declare a new policy through personal interviews; but Chiang made a point of insisting in a lecture in the Sian military school that the Red Army was the real enemy, and the enemy close at hand, while Japan was a remote menace. This had immediate response in open and outspoken criticism of student-commanders. When these attacks were continued in the assembly, Chang out of loyalty to the Generalissimo dismissed three men from the schools. But at Loyang Chiang repeated these remarks in a lecture to the military academy, and showed no disposition to concede to the general mood.

When Chiang departed, there was an outburst of activity by local secret groups (in some quarters termed "Blue Shirts", but others recently from Sian question the accuracy of this designation) and General Chang wrote a letter to the Generalissimo appealing for "the right and opportunity to drive out the Japanese and recover our homeland" and concluding: "In any case, I must tell you that I cannot control my army much longer."

Subsequently there was a Loyang meeting; reports differ as to whether Chiang or Chang asked this. Chiang explained his failure to send strong forces to Shansi on a basis of objections by Yen Hsi-shan, governor of the province. The only real outcome of the interview was Chiang's promise to come to Sian and meet the Tungpei leaders in person—the fateful visit leading to the present crisis.

Behind the scenes at Sian the secret groups, led by Chiang's nephew Chiang Hsiao-hsien, had established centers with wireless communications. There are allegations that kidnappings of students and workers took place; finally early in October three student delegates from North China are said to have been seized and when General Chang phoned the Kuomintang office to make inquiries he was told nothing was known of their whereabouts. That night he moved swiftly, closed the city gates, conducted a raid on Kuomintang headquarters, and is said to have found the students, afterward deporting the agents while a protest was wired to the Generalissimo.

At the same General Hu Chung-nan with three of Chiang's best divisions renewed the campaign against the Communists but after getting 80 li into the Red area he took a severe beating and had to retreat.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年12月24日，星期四 18080
西安发生了什么事？
（分两部分——第一部分）
西安究竟发生了什么事？谣言虽多，但鲜有确凿细节佐证。以下摘要基于在北平的外国记者从太原收到的报告，这些报告由来自西安的代表带至太原，并已在多方核实，可视为反映了事实真相，尽管其中存在若干诠释上的差异，下文将予以注明。

张学良将军的东北军（即“东北军”）长期心怀不满。该部失去了满洲故土，对日本怀恨在心，因而反对自身充当对抗中国共产党人的角色。随着中共政策转向强调“民族抵抗”，而牺牲政策的其他所有方面，某种形式的默契必然不难达成——这一发展注定令蒋介石将军极为恼火。

我们随即遇到诠释上的冲突，对此可简要略过。在北方某些圈子里，人们显然完全相信东北军军官的诚意。我们也接触到其他对“少帅”绝非不友好的圈子，他们持相当愤世嫉俗的看法，认为东北军的目标与其说是针对日本，不如说是针对南京的统治，并将整个局势比作1933年的“福建事变”——回想起来，当时也与福建内地的共产党人形成了类似的“权宜联姻”，并同样宣称关心国家福祉。

这些诠释上的冲突在蒋介石将军的态度问题上达到顶点。在我们看来，委员长可能既因东北军与共产党人的联络而感到恼火，又仍真诚地决心以自己的方式抵抗日本。但对于那些对委员长对日意图持愤世嫉俗态度的人来说，他坚持要求东北军执行“剿共”政策，似乎清楚证明了他宁愿打内战，也不愿进行所要求的对日战争。而对于许多持有各种思想倾向的中国人来说，抗击侵略者的念头显然比抗击同胞的念头更令人乐意接受。

张将军一直对委员长完全忠诚，但他发现自己日益在这种忠诚与对自己部下的本能忠诚之间撕裂。《德日协定》的宣布引发了对南京诚意的新的怀疑，因为在东北军中流传的说法是，若无蒋将军的私下保证，不可能达成如此公开的协议。意大利承认“满洲国”也带来了同样的问题。我们自己的观点是，这一切百分之百是胡扯，但从中国内地的角度来看，这一切似乎都非常连贯；如果南京被误解了，依我们看，过错在于南京；当然，除非有人对任何批评南京的言论都极度反感，以至于认为整件事都是西安的政治宣传家们策划出来的。通常在这种错综复杂的局势中，无论有多少种观点，每种观点都包含一定的真实性。

绥远和青岛危机引发了新的讨论，尽管蒋介石将军向绥远派遣了三个师，但东北军认为此举迟缓，且他们并未参与战斗，而是占据了傅作义在绥远和山西部队的后方及侧翼阵地。据报道，南京的飞机已奉命调往绥远；但没有一架飞机参与进攻行动。据说在10月下旬，张将军曾向蒋将军发出急电，敦促采取坚决抵抗的政策，并与“抗日红军”建立统一战线——结果却遭到断然拒绝。

蒋介石于10月第一周访问西安，少帅曾希望通过个人会晤说服他宣布新政策；但蒋在西安军校的一次演讲中特意强调，红军是真正的敌人，是近在咫尺的敌人，而日本则是遥远的威胁。这立即引起了学生指挥官们公开且直言不讳的批评。当这些攻击在集会上继续进行时，张出于对委员长的忠诚，开除了三名学员。但在洛阳，蒋在向军校学员演讲时重复了这些言论，并表现出无意顺应普遍情绪的姿态。

蒋离开后，当地秘密团体（在某些圈子里称为“蓝衣社”，但其他最近来自西安的人质疑这一称呼的准确性）活动爆发，张将军致信委员长，恳求“驱逐日本人、收复故土的权利和机会”，并在结尾写道：“无论如何，我必须告诉您，我再也无法控制我的军队了。”

随后举行了一次洛阳会议；关于是蒋还是张要求举行此次会议，报道不一。蒋解释称，未能向山西派遣重兵是基于山西省主席阎锡山的反对。此次会晤的唯一实际成果是蒋承诺亲自前往西安，会见东北军领导人——这次命运攸关的访问导致了当前的危机。

在西安幕后，由蒋的侄子蒋孝先（音译）领导的秘密团体建立了配备无线通讯的中心。有指控称发生了绑架学生和工人的事件；最终，据说在10月初，三名来自华北的学生代表被抓获，当张将军致电国民党党部查询时，被告知不知其下落。当晚他迅速行动，关闭城门，突袭国民党总部，据说找到了那些学生，随后在致电委员长提出抗议的同时，驱逐了特工人员。

与此同时，胡宗南将军率领蒋的三个精锐师重新发起对共产党人的战役，但在进入红色区域80里后遭受重创，被迫撤退。
