The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, December 23 1936

What Happened At Sian?
(In Two Parts—Part Two)

EXISTING tension was increased by the events of the next day, December 9, in Sian. This was the anniversary of the new student movement that began last year, in resistance to the Japanese so-called Autonomous Movement in the north. Thousands of students marched through the streets of Sian in silent massed formation, with slogans demanding that armies be sent to the defense of Suiyuan and Shantung.

General Chiang ordered Hsiao Li-tze, civil governor of Shensi and controller of the police force, to break up the demonstration and not allow the students to march out to Lintung to his residence. And so, as the procession marched towards Lintung, the police fired, seriously wounding two schoolboys of twelve and thirteen years of age. The incident at once brought Marshal Chang and other leaders to Lintung in angry protest.

Another immediate issue was the question of the seven National Salvation Association leaders, six of whom were being held in prison in Shanghai. Chang Hsueh-liang and the Sian people demanded their release, in common with other student demonstrations all over the country. Chiang refused pointblank to consider their release; and stated finally, in the most definite terms, that he was entirely opposed to a People's Front. Here was another impasse.

By December 11 a very serious and critical situation had developed in Sian. The crisis was precipitated by further activities on the part of the secret groups, who had been quietly armed, and were preparing for a violent coup. Chiang Kai-shek was rumored to have approved a blacklist for immediate arrest, and counter-measures of some sort were bound to be provoked.

On the night of the 11th there was held a conference of all the commanders of the Tungpei army, and of Yang Hu-cheng. The decision taken then is declared in some quarters to have been only on anticipation of action their men would have taken, perhaps, without them.

The coup was swiftly planned, and as swiftly executed. At 6 a.m. next morning, December 12, Chiang Kai-shek's headquarters at Lintung was surrounded. The first man captured was General Chiang's nephew, Chiang Hsiao-hsien, leader of the Blue Shirt gendarmerie. When the soldiers learned who he was, they stood him up and shot him dead on the spot.

Chiang Kai-shek escaped in his night-shirt, accompanied by one member of his bodyguard. But the guard went only a short distance, and on second thought turned back and told the Tungpei men where Chiang was. The Generalissimo was captured with his entire staff.

In Sianfu, the Sian Guest-house was occupied by Yang Hu-cheng's troops, and none of Chiang's men escaped. Hsiao Li-tze, who had ordered the firing on the students, was captured with most of his officials. The Bureaus of Public Safety under his control were all occupied and their chiefs taken prisoner.

The secret groups centers were rapidly invested, and captured with their staffs and many documents. One of Chiang's airplanes, landing to investigate, was captured immediately, and added to the main squadron of Government bombers that had already changed hands.

At the same time, similar action was taking place in Kansu. The Tungpei troops attacked Hu Chung-nan, capturing an entire brigade outright in Lanchow. With the Chinese Anti-Japanese Red Army (Communists) there was open fraternisation on the part of the Tungpei troops. Martial law was proclaimed in Sianfu for one day only; after which shops were opened and life went on as before.

A new administration was set up in Sianfu. It issued an eight-point program as follows:

1. Reorganization of the Nanking Government to include all anti-Japanese representatives from all parties, groups and organizations throughout the country.
2. Stop all civil war.
3. Immediate release of National Salvation Association leaders in Shanghai.
4. Release of all political prisoners throughout the whole country.
5. Remove all laws and restrictions upon the patriotic movement.
6. Protection of civil rights of the people—free speech, press and assembly. Full political freedom.
7. The immediate realization of the last will and testament of Sun Yat-sen, which calls for an alliance between China and all countries that believe in its freedom and independence.
8. The immediate convocation of a National Salvation Congress.

With this proclamation appeared many other manifestoes, guaranteeing all civil rights to the people. Mass demonstrations were held in the streets.

The "provisional government" also issued a long project of the People's Anti-Japanese National Salvation, urging and outlining establishment of People's United Front. On December 14 a United Chinese Anti-Japanese Military Affairs Council was organized, including all military leaders on a collective basis. It was made clear that General Chang wanted no personal leadership or control, and it was stated that the "Anti-Japanese Red Armies" will be represented on the Council together with any and all armies "willing to fight the Japanese."

General Chang has been making daily radio broadcasts from Sian, outlining the new program; on December 15 he gave a long story of his efforts to induce General Chiang to fight the Japanese, and one sympathizer declares: "These broadcasts, if they could only reach the whole nation, would make clear enough to all the struggle that has been going on for at least a year between the two leaders. The essential point is, of course, that General Chang continually obeyed the orders of the Generalissimo until he was threatened by the united action of his entire army. This is the mass basis of a movement that has been so widely described as the wanton action of a discontented individual."

Finally it is declared by this same source: "Peace or war rests with Nanking. The Northwest will not fire the first shot against a Chinese army."

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年12月23日，星期三

西安发生了什么？
（分两部分——第二部分）

12月9日，即次日在西安发生的事件，加剧了既有的紧张局势。这一天是去年开始的、旨在抵抗日本在北方所谓的“自治运动”的新学生运动的周年纪念日。成千上万的学生在西安街头以沉默的密集队形游行，高呼要求派兵保卫绥远和山东的口号。

蒋介石命令陕西省主席兼警察总监肖自忠（音译）驱散示威活动，并不允许学生游行至临潼他的住所。因此，当游行队伍向临潼进发时，警察开枪射击，严重打伤了两名分别为十二岁和十三岁的学童。这一事件立即促使张元帅和其他领导人愤怒地前往临塘提出抗议。

另一个紧迫的问题是七位全国救国会领导人的问题，其中六人被关押在上海的监狱中。张学良和西安方面与全国各地的其他学生示威活动一道，要求释放他们。蒋介石断然拒绝考虑释放他们；并最终以最明确的措辞表示，他完全反对人民阵线。这又造成了一个僵局。

到12月11日，西安的局势已变得非常严峻和危急。这场危机是由秘密团体的进一步活动引发的，这些团体一直暗中武装，并正准备发动暴力政变。有传言称蒋介石批准了一份立即逮捕的黑名单，而某种形式的反制措施势必会被激起。

11日晚，东北军所有指挥官以及杨虎城举行了一次会议。据某些方面宣称，当时做出的决定仅仅是基于对其部下可能会在没有他们指挥的情况下采取行动的预判。

政变计划迅速制定，并同样迅速地执行。第二天早上，即12月6时，蒋介石在临潼的总部被包围。第一个被俘的是蒋介石的侄子、蓝衣社宪兵领袖蒋孝先。士兵们得知他是谁后，让他站好并当场将其枪决。

蒋介石身穿睡衣逃跑，身边仅有一名保镖陪同。但这名保镖没走多远，转念一想又折返回来，告诉东北军人员蒋介石的下落。委员长及其全体幕僚被俘。

在西安府，杨虎城的部队占领了西京招待所，蒋介石的手下无人逃脱。曾下令向学生开枪的肖自忠（音译）与其大多数官员一同被俘。受其控制的公安局全部被占领，局长们均成为俘虏。

秘密团体的中心据点被迅速包围，其工作人员和许多文件被缴获。蒋介石的一架飞机降落进行调查时，立即被俘获，并被加入已经易手的政府轰炸机主力中队。

与此同时，甘肃也发生了类似的行动。东北军攻击胡宗南，在兰州直接俘获了整个旅。东北军与中国抗日红军（共产党）公开亲善。西安府仅宣布戒严一天；之后商店开门营业，生活如常进行。

西安府成立了一个新政府。它发布了如下八点纲领：

1. 改组南京政府，以容纳来自全国各党派、团体和组织的抗日代表。
2. 停止一切内战。
3. 立即释放上海的全国救国会领导人。
4. 释放全国所有政治犯。
5. 废除对爱国运动的所有法律和限制。
6. 保护人民的公民权利——言论、新闻和集会自由。充分的政治自由。
7. 立即实现孙中山遗嘱，该遗嘱呼吁中国与所有信仰其自由和独立的国家结盟。
8. 立即召开国民救国大会。

随着这一宣言的发布，还出现了许多其他保证人民所有公民权利的 manifesto（宣言/告示）。街头举行了大规模示威活动。

“临时政府”还发布了一项长长的《人民抗日救国方案》，敦促并概述建立人民统一战线。12月14日，成立了中华抗日军事委员会，集体纳入所有军事领导人。明确表示张将军不寻求个人领导或控制，并声明“抗日红军”将与任何及所有“愿意抗击日本”的军队一起在委员会中拥有代表权。

张将军一直在西安通过无线电广播每日讲话，概述新纲领；12月15日，他长篇讲述了自己努力劝说蒋介石将军抗日的经过，一位同情者宣称：“如果这些广播能够传遍全国，就足以向所有人阐明这两位领导人之间至少持续了一年的斗争。关键点当然在于，张将军一直服从委员长的命令，直到他受到其整个军队联合行动的威胁。这是一场被广泛描述为不满个人的鲁莽行动的运动，而这正是其群众基础。”

最后，同一消息源宣称：“和平还是战争取决于南京。西北方面不会向中国军队开第一枪。”

18983.

Deliberate suppression of the facts is charged by some northern quarters and it is strongly asserted that Sian represents “a popular movement that can only be compared with similar movements in Western countries for a united front against Fascist aggression.”
Here, again, we come to a divergence of view which stretches in more than two directions. It is not easy to represent such events in sharp black and white, the powers of evil against those of good (with the respective roles assigned in accordance with one’s own ideas).
To assign to Nanking nothing but the purest of acts and motives would obviously be an incredibly naive attitude, for Nanking has its full quota of politicians and politicians are politicians—the world over. But we must confess to a feeling that anyone who tries to assign to the Tungpei a similar purity of act and motive proves himself at least equally naive if not more so, for certainly our information (and some of it comes very direct) is that those about General Chang number their full proportion of hypocrites and self-seekers, willing to capitalize a “fight the Japanese” slogan or any other slogan to prevent Nanking and its Generalissimo from gaining complete domination.
And Nanking has on its side, as has been quite clearly shown by the widespread rallying behind the National Government, a basis of accomplishment which no rebel group can have in the very nature of things. Again and again we have heard Chinese and foreigners alike express themselves as convinced, against their earlier judgment, by the things the National Government has been able to do in the way of unification, reconstruction, establishment of peace and order, and general conduct of a modern government as opposed to the warlordism of old.
Perhaps Sian does not stand for warlordism; perhaps the words of the Sian ‘provisional government’ are to be taken at full face value; but we doubt if there is any national majority taking such a view. While the country has been increasingly pressing for a stronger and stronger attitude against Japan, it is our judgment that Nanking’s handling of events both at home and with reference to Japan has met with general support even though there has been plenty of criticism in detail. The important thing to us has been that Nanking seemed to be constantly doing better—strengthening its policy, abandoning some of the misguided tactics (including terrorism against its enemies) which smirched its earlier record. And the country seems to feel this, which may well turn the issue in this crisis.

But we regard some of the wild talk which has drifted down from Nanking as harmful and mischievous. This is not a situation to be handled with violence and abandon. Firmness must be unflinchingly the course—but not hysteria. Above all, it seems to us necessary if in any way possible to prevent the outbreak of civil warfare which might well be disastrous to every national cause at this juncture.
Madam Chiang’s trip has afforded a breathing-spell. It would be idle optimism to say that the situation gives grounds for optimism. But at least it gives time for an all-around cooling-down. Nanking must understand such grievances as Sian may put forward, but Sian for its part must realize that it cannot be permitted to strike in outlaw style at the National Government either direct or through its leaders. Sian is quite right in pointing to the nation’s crisis; it is now for Sian to see that it is accentuating that crisis, not in any way leading toward solution.

18983.

北方某些方面指责故意掩盖事实，并强烈主张西安代表着“一场民众运动，只能与西方国家为建立反对法西斯侵略的统一战线而进行的类似运动相提并论。”
在此，我们再次遇到一种不止两个方向的分歧观点。很难用鲜明的黑白来表现此类事件，即邪恶势力对抗善良势力（各自的角色根据一个人的想法分配）。
认为南京方面只有最纯洁的行为和动机，显然是一种令人难以置信的天真态度，因为南京也有其足额的政客，而政客就是政客——全世界皆然。但我们必须承认这样一种感觉：任何试图赋予东北军同样纯洁的行为和动机的人，证明其至少同样天真，甚至更甚，因为毫无疑问，我们的信息（其中一些非常直接）表明，张将军周围的人中不乏伪君子和利己主义者，他们愿意利用“抗日”口号或任何其他口号，以防止南京及其委员长获得完全的控制权。
而南京方面，正如在全国范围内 rallying（集结/支持）国民政府所清楚显示的那样，拥有叛乱团体在事物本质层面上无法具备的成就基础。我们一再听到中国人和外国人都表示，尽管早先持有不同判断，但他们对国民政府在统一、重建、建立和平与秩序以及现代政府的一般运作方面所能做到的事情感到信服，这与旧的军阀主义形成对比。
也许西安并不代表军阀主义；也许西安“临时政府”的话应该完全按字面意思理解；但我们怀疑是否有全国多数派持这种观点。虽然全国日益迫切要求对日本采取越来越强硬的态度，但我们的判断是，南京在处理国内事务及对日关系方面的做法获得了普遍支持，尽管细节上不乏批评。对我们来说重要的是，南京似乎一直在不断改进——加强其政策，放弃一些损害其早期记录的错误策略（包括对其敌人的恐怖主义）。国家似乎也感受到了这一点，这很可能扭转此次危机的局面。

但我们认为从南京流传下来的一些荒谬言论是有害且恶意的。这种情况不能用暴力和放纵来处理。坚定必须是毫不退缩的方针——但不是歇斯底里。最重要的是，在我们看来，如有可能，必须防止内战爆发，因为在此关头，内战很可能对每一项民族事业都是灾难性的。
蒋夫人的行程提供了一个喘息之机。如果说局势提供了乐观的理由，那是徒劳的乐观。但它至少为全面的冷静下来提供了时间。南京必须理解西安可能提出的不满，但西安方面也必须认识到，不允许它以不法方式直接或间接通过其领导人打击国民政府。西安指出国家危机是完全正确的；现在西安需要看到的是，它正在加剧这一危机，而不是以任何方式导向解决。

December 26, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers (dated Dec.25):
Processions, Demonstrations, Strikes Etc. Prohibited

On December 24, the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison
Commissioner's Headquarters issued the following proclamations:-
"Since the Sian coup, martial law has been
enforced in this locality. In order to prevent undesirable
elements from resorting to illegal activities, the Woosung-
Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters hereby issues
this proclamation notifying that military law will be employed
to deal with any person who spreads rumours, disturbs the
peace and order, impairs the national currency, harms foreign
nationals, calls illegal meetings, forms societies, holds
processions, stages demonstrations, instigates strikes or
incites a suspension of studies."

National Herald and other local newspapers:

The Shanghai Tangpu and City Government yesterday
jointly issued the following notices:-
"At the present time when our nation is facing
a crisis, the maintenance of peace and order is a matter
of first importance. Employers and employees in industries
and commercial undertakings should realize this and refrain
from doing anything that is liable to give rise to disputes.
"With a view to obviating labour troubles, we
hereby advise employers not to reduce staff or wages, while
employees should refrain from going on strike. Both sides
should work in a spirit of co-operation so that all causes
for dispute might be eliminated. Any person who instigates
labour disputes with the intention of disturbing the peace
and order will be severely punished."

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

THE QUESTION OF FACTORY INSPECTION

When interviewed yesterday by our representative
on the question of factory inspection in the International
Settlement, Mr. Wei Yung Hsi (  ), a special
delegate from the Ministry of Industry, stated that the
Chinese authorities are determined to resume the negotiations
over this question in order to uphold our administrative
rights and the Central Factory Law. A satisfactory
solution of the subject may be expected before long.

《大公报》及其他本地报纸（12月25日刊）：
禁止游行、示威、罢工等

12月24日，淞沪警备司令部发布以下公告：-
“鉴于西安事变，本地区已实行戒严。为防止不良分子从事非法活动，淞沪警备司令部特此发布公告通知，将对任何散布谣言、扰乱治安、破坏法币、伤害外籍人士、召集非法会议、组建社团、举行游行、进行示威、煽动罢工或鼓动停课的人员，依据军法处置。”

上海党部和市政府昨日联合发布以下通知：-
“在当前我国面临危机之际，维持治安至关重要。工商业界的雇主和雇员应认识到这一点，避免做任何可能引起纠纷的事情。
“为避免劳资纠纷，我们建议雇主不要裁员或减薪，而雇员应避免罢工。双方应以合作精神工作，以便消除所有争端原因。任何意图扰乱治安而煽动劳资纠纷的人将受到严厉惩罚。”

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

工厂检查问题

December 24, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Hwa Tung Yen Pao dated December 23 :-

CHANG HSUEH LIANG DEMANDS $30,000,000

Rumours are rife in Nanking to the effect
that General Chang Hsueh Liang, the leader of the Sian
revolt, is demanding from the National Government a sum
of $30,000,000 for the release of General Chiang Kai
Shek after which he (Chang Hsueh Liang) will retire.
This news cannot be confirmed.

Chin Pao (本报) publishes the following article on Dec. 24:-

THE CASE OF A ROAD REPAIRING COOLIE

(Continued from this morning)

Why did not the XX lords pull Siao Sz Tse
(小狮子) to their headquarters to torture him, to take
out his heart and lungs, to cut off his genital organ,
to remove his eyes or to have his body dissolved by
sulphuric acid? (These are the customary practices of the
XX devils when dealing with Chinese.) The reason why they
treated the coolie so leniently is because they saw he
was wearing the uniform of a certain Council.
I wonder why this Council has not disclosed
this incident, but has quietly endured this insult.
Probably this Council wants to win favour of the XX people;
furthermore, the victim is not a man with "yellow hair
and blue eyes". The Council may yet blame Siao Sz Tse
for not having got out of the way quickly enough.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers (Hangchow
telegram) :-

BANDITS ATTACK CITY IN CHEKIANG PROVINCE

On December 23, Mr. Chiang Chao Hsiung
(蒋超雄), Chief of the Peace Preservation Headquarters
of the Chekiang Provincial Government, made the following
statement on the disturbances created by bandits in the
city of Chong Hua Hsien (崇化县), Chekiang Province, on
the afternoon of December 21 :-
"Chong Hua Hsien borders on Anhwei Province.
A small party of the Peace Preservation Corps is stationed
in that city. At 4 p.m. December 21, some 60 bandits
entered the city. As the Magistrate was absent at the
time, no resistance was offered. The bandits wounded or
killed a number of officials of the Hsien Tangpu. A
report of the trouble soon reached the Peace Preservation
Corps stationed at Yui Zien (於潜) and a large force was
detailed to the city to suppress the bandits.
"Upon learning of the arrival of reinforcements
the bandits immediately withdrew. The Provincial
Government the same evening also detailed a large body of
troops to the city. Many bandits were killed".

张学良索要三千万元

南京谣言四起，称西安事变首领张学良将军向国民政府索要三千万元，以释放蒋介石将军，此后他（张学良）将引退。此消息无法证实。

《金报》（本报）于12月24日刊登如下文章：-

修路苦力案

（续今晨版）

为何那些XX老爷不把小狮子（Siao Sz Tse）抓到他们的总部去折磨他，挖出他的心肺，割掉他的生殖器，剜去他的双眼，或用硫酸溶解他的身体？（这些是XX鬼子对待中国人时的惯常做法。）他们之所以如此宽待这名苦力，是因为看到他身穿某公局的制服。
不知该公局为何不披露此事，而是默默忍受这一侮辱。或许该公局是想讨好XX人士；此外，受害者并非“黄发蓝眼”之人。该公局甚至可能责怪小狮子未能及时避让。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸（杭州电）：-

浙江省匪徒攻城

12月23日，浙江省政府保安司令部司令蒋超雄先生就12月21日下午浙江省崇化县发生的匪徒骚乱发表如下声明：-
“崇化县与安徽省接壤。该县驻有一小队保安团。12月21日下午4时，约60名匪徒进入县城。因县长当时不在，未作抵抗。匪徒杀伤了县党部多名职员。骚乱消息很快传至驻於潜的保安团，当局随即调派大批部队进城剿匪。
“匪徒得知援军到达后立即撤退。省政府当晚也调派大批军队进城。多名匪徒被击毙”。

MAINICHI

RED BANDITS APPEAR IN CENTRAL CHINA

    A telegram from Hangchow
reports that at 4 p.m. December 21 red troops occupied
Chang Hwa Prefecture in Chekiang Province about 200
Chinese li west of Hangchow.    The office of the
Prefectural Government and the District Kuomintang
were destroyed.    Mr. Chang Pang Van, a member of the
District Kuomintang, was killed and Mr. Ching Lih Ming,
a Prefect, was detained by the Reds.
    The Provincial Government has
dispatched soldiers to the place to suppress the outlaws.

BRITISH AND AMERICAN AMBASSADORS TO MEDIATE IN
SIAN AFFAIR

    A Daito telegram from Tientsin
reports that the mediation by Mr. Donald, advisor to
General Chiang Kai Shek, and Mr. T. V. Soong in the
Sian incident has failed.    General Yu Yu Jen, Pacification
Commissioner, and General Yen Hsi Shan's representative
left for Sian on December 23.    It is reported that
British and American diplomats are endeavouring to
mediate between Sian and Nanking; they are persuading
General Chang Hsueh Liang and General Yang Hu Chung to
go abroad.

JAPANESE MARINES WITHDRAW FROM TSINGTAO

    A Domei telegram from Tokyo
reports that on December 23 the Japanese marines landed
at Tsingtao on December 3 to protect Japanese residents
during the mill strike have been completely withdrawn to
the Japanese warships because the strike situation has
become normal.

December 24, 1936.    2    Morning Translation.

Lih Pao publishes the following telegram from Nanking .-

THE COUP IN SIAN

According to a certain high Government official, the recent revolt of the rebel General Chang Hsueh Liang was a pre-arranged plot. After Mr. Siao Nai Hwa, Personal Secretary of the Generalissimo, was killed, the code book was seized by the rebels. Using the code Chang Hsueh Liang at once sent telegrams in the name of General Chiang Kai Shek to Generals Liu Shih, Ho Chen Chin, Ho Ying Ching, Chen Chi, Chu Pei Teh, T'ung Sung Tse and others, instructing them to proceed immediately to Sian to receive confidential instructions verbally from the Generalissimo. Chang Hsueh Liang's object was to do away with all the military leaders of the National Government at one stroke.

Upon receipt of this false telegram, General Ho Ying Ching and others at once made arrangements to fly to Sian.

General Feng Yu Hsiang, however, said to them: "Why should we all be required to proceed to Sian at one time. The matter requires careful consideration."

The proposed trip was postponed for about two hours. In the meantime news of the Sian uprising was received from the railway authorities.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers .-

To-Day's General Meeting of Representatives of Shanghai Various Circles to Support the Central Government

At 2 p.m. to-day, the local Kuomintang headquarters will call a "General Meeting of Representatives of Shanghai Various Circles in Support of the Central Government to Send an Expedition against the Rebels" in the auditorium of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Soochow Road. A notification is published by the Tangpu in the advertisement columns of local newspapers to-day inviting Party and government organs, public bodies and schools to send three delegates each to attend the meeting.

The following will compose the presidium of the meeting:- Mayor Wu Teh Chen, General Yang Fu, General Tsai Chin Chun, Messrs. Pan Kung Chan, Dong Ying Bah, Wong Shao Lai, Tu Yuet Seng, Tsu Hsueh Van, Chang Shou Yung, Pang Kung Pih, Yue Chung Hwei and Huang Chao Yung.

The Bureau of Public Safety will detail policemen to maintain order at the meeting.

The programme of the meeting will be as follows :-
(1) Opening of the meeting.
(2) Music by the Band of the Public Safety Bureau.
(3) Respect to the National and Party Flags as well as to the portrait of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen.
(4) The reading of Dr. Sun's will.
(5) Three-minute silence in memory of the martyrs who fell during the Sian incident.
(6) Chairman's report.
(7) Speeches
(8) Discussion of proposals
(9) Shouting of slogans
(10) Music
(11) Meeting ends.

1936年12月24日。    2    上午译件。

《立报》刊登如下南京电报：-

西安事变

据某政府高官称，叛逆将领张学良最近的叛变是一场预谋的阴谋。在委座私人秘书萧乃华先生遇害后，密码本被叛军缴获。张学良利用密码，立即以蒋介石将军的名义向刘峙、何成浚、何应钦、陈济棠、朱培德、宋哲元等将军发出电报，指示他们立即前往西安，当面接受委座的机密指令。张学良的目的是企图一举消灭国民政府的所有军事领袖。

收到这封假电报后，何应钦将军等人立即安排飞往西安。

然而，冯玉祥将军对他们说：“为何要求我们所有人同时前往西安。此事需慎重考虑。”

拟议的行程推迟了约两小时。在此期间，铁路当局传来了西安起义的消息。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

今日上海各界代表拥护中央出兵讨逆大会

今日下午2时，本地国民党党部将在北苏州路商会礼堂召开“上海各界代表拥护中央出兵讨逆大会”。公安局今日在本地报纸广告栏发布通知，邀请党政机构、公共团体及学校各派三名代表出席会议。

会议主席团由以下人员组成：- 市长吴铁城、杨虎将军、蔡劲军将军、潘公展先生、董英拔先生、黄绍竑先生、杜月笙先生、褚学范先生、张寿镛先生、庞京周先生、岳钟辉先生及黄朝庸先生。

公安局将派遣警察维持会场秩序。

会议议程如下：-
(1) 开会。
(2) 公安局乐队奏乐。
(3) 向国旗、党旗及已故孙中山博士遗像致敬。
(4) 宣读孙中山博士遗嘱。
(5) 为西安事变中牺牲的烈士默哀三分钟。
(6) 主席报告。
(7) 演讲
(8) 讨论提案
(9) 呼口号
(10) 奏乐
(11) 散会。

December 24, 1936.
Morning Translation

With a view to making the local community acquainted with the rebellious acts of Chang Hsueh Liang, the local Tangpu has prepared a large quantity of coloured paper slips bearing slogans denouncing Chang Hsueh Liang, supporting an expedition against the rebels and urging the rescue of General Chiang Kai Shek. It has arranged to have these paper slips distributed this afternoon by an aeroplane.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

Death of a German Dentist

During the trouble in Sian, a German dentist named Dr. Herr Wunsch was killed by the rebels. This tragic news was confirmed yesterday by our representative at various sources.

Dr. Wunsch in the early part of this year was in practice in Shanghai at No. 1191 Bubbling Well Road, but owing to bad business he went to Sian where he had been doing very good business owing to the fact that he was the only German dentist in that place.

During the revolt on December 12, a group of rebel troops arrived at his place and owing to language difficulties, a misunderstanding arose as a result of which the rebels opened fire. The German dentist died instantaneously.

At about the same time, another German named Mr. Friese, advisor to General Chang Hsueh Liang, was likewise assaulted by the rebels, but fortunately he did not sustain serious injury. With the exception of these two incidents, no harm has befallen any foreign resident in Shensi.

According to information secured from the Eurasian Aviation Corporation, Mr. "Rots", a German pilot, and Mr. "Fisu", assistant pilot, of the Corporation are still being detained in Sian by the rebel Chang Hsueh Liang.

It is also learned that recently Chang Hsueh Liang sent a telegram to the Eurasian Aviation Corporation stating that if the Corporation would despatch an aeroplane to Sian, the two aviators would be released, but the offer was ignored because the Corporation regards Chang Hsueh Liang as a man who is insincere and cannot be trusted.

Lih Pao :-

JAPANESE MOTOR CYCLIST KNOCKS DOWN HAWKER

At about 9 a.m. yesterday, a certain Japanese, whilst passing near the corner of Gordon Road and Penang Road on a motor cycle, knocked down a Chinese hawker named Chu Sin Dah ( 朱新大 ) who was selling fried puffed flour balls. The Japanese cyclist decamped at a high speed in a northerly direction.

The accident was witnessed by several pedestrians who at once reported the matter to the Police. The injured hawker was removed to a hospital for treatment. A slight injury to his leg was treated and he was able to leave the hospital immediately.

为使本地社区了解张学良的叛逆行径，本地公安局准备了大量印有谴责张学良、支持出兵讨逆及呼吁营救蒋介石将军标语的彩色传单。该局安排于今日下午由飞机散发这些传单。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：-

一名德国牙医身亡

在西安骚乱期间，一名名为温施（Wunsch）博士的德国牙医被叛军杀害。昨日，本报记者从多方渠道证实了这一悲惨消息。

温施博士今年早些时候在上海静安寺路1191号执业，但因生意不佳前往西安，由于他是当地唯一的德国牙医，生意一直很好。

在12月12日的叛乱期间，一群叛军士兵来到他的住所，由于语言障碍产生误会，导致叛军开火。这名德国牙医当场死亡。

大约在同一时间，另一名名为弗里泽（Friese）先生的德国人，即张学良将军的顾问，也遭到叛军袭击，但幸运的是未受重伤。除这两起事件外，陕西的外国居民未受任何伤害。

据从欧亚航空公司获得的消息，该公司的德国飞行员“罗茨”（Rots，音译）先生和副驾驶员“菲苏”（Fisu，音译）先生仍被叛军张学良扣押在西安。

另获悉，张学良最近向欧亚航空公司发送电报称，如果公司派遣飞机前往西安，将释放这两名飞行员，但该提议被忽视，因为公司认为张学良是一个不真诚、不可信任的人。

《立报》：-

日本骑摩托车者撞倒小贩

昨日上午9时许，一名日本人骑摩托车经过戈登路与槟榔路拐角附近时，撞倒了一名名叫朱新大的中国小贩，该小贩当时正在售卖油炸膨化面粉球。这名日本骑车者迅速向北逃逸。

几名行人目睹了事故，并立即向警方报告。受伤的小贩被送往医院治疗。其腿部轻伤经处理后，随即出院。

Hwa Tung Yen Pao dated December 23 :-

CHANG HSUEH LIANG DEMANDS $30,000,000

Rumours are rife in Nanking to the effect that General Chang Hsueh Liang, the leader of the Sian revolt, is demanding from the National Government a sum of $30,000,000 for the release of General Chiang Kai Shek after which he (Chang Hsueh Liang) will retire. This news cannot be confirmed.

Chin Pao (申报) publishes the following article on Dec. 24:-

THE CASE OF A ROAD REPAIRING COOLIE

(Continued from this morning)

Why did not the XX lords pull Siao Sz Tse (小柿子) to their headquarters to torture him, to take out his heart and lungs, to cut off his genital organ, to remove his eyes or to have his body dissolved by sulphuric acid? (These are the customary practices of the XX devils when dealing with Chinese.) The reason why they treated the coolie so leniently is because they saw he was wearing the uniform of a certain Council.
I wonder why this Council has not disclosed this incident, but has quietly endured this insult. Probably this Council wants to win favour of the XX people; furthermore, the victim is not a man with "yellow hair and blue eyes". The Council may yet blame Siao Sz Tse for not having got out of the way quickly enough.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers (Hangchow telegram) :-

BANDITS ATTACK CITY IN CHEKIANG PROVINCE

On December 23, Mr. Chiang Chao Hsiung (蒋兆熊), Chief of the Peace Preservation Headquarters of the Chekiang Provincial Government, made the following statement on the disturbances created by bandits in the city of Chong Hua Hsien (崇化县), Chekiang Province, on the afternoon of December 21 :-
"Chong Hua Hsien borders on Anhwei Province. A small party of the Peace Preservation Corps is stationed in that city. At 4 p.m. December 21, some 60 bandits entered the city. As the Magistrate was absent at the time, no resistance was offered. The bandits wounded or killed a number of officials of the Hsien Tangpu. A report of the trouble soon reached the Peace Preservation Corps stationed at Yui Zien (于潜) and a large force was detailed to the city to suppress the bandits.
"Upon learning of the arrival of reinforcements the bandits immediately withdrew. The Provincial Government the same evening also detailed a large body of troops to the city. Many bandits were killed".

1936 年 12 月 24 日。下午译件。

《华通日报》12 月 23 日讯：-

张学良索款三千万元

南京谣言四起，称西安事变首领张学良将军向国民政府索要三千万元，以释放蒋介石将军，此后他（张学良）将引退。此消息无法证实。

《申报》于 12 月 24 日刊登如下文章：-

修路苦力案

（续今晨报道）

为何那些 XX 老爷不把小柿子拉到他们的总部去折磨他，挖出他的心肺，割掉他的生殖器，剜去他的双眼，或用硫酸溶解他的身体？（这些是 XX 鬼子对待中国人时的惯常做法。）他们之所以如此宽待这名苦力，是因为看到他穿着某公局的制服。
我不禁要问，该公局为何不披露此事，而是默默忍受这一侮辱。或许该公局是想博取 XX 人的欢心；此外，受害者并非“黄发蓝眼”之人。该公局甚至可能责怪小柿子未能及时避让。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸（杭州电）：-

匪徒袭击浙江省县城

12 月 23 日，浙江省政府保安司令部司令蒋兆熊先生就 12 月 21 日下午浙江省崇化县发生的匪徒骚乱事件发表如下声明：-
“崇化县与安徽省接壤。该县驻有一小队保安团。12 月 21 日下午 4 时，约 60 名匪徒进入县城。由于县长当时不在，未作抵抗。匪徒杀伤了县党部多名职员。骚乱消息很快传至于潜驻防的保安团，当局随即调派大批部队进城剿匪。
“匪徒得知援军到达后立即撤退。省政府当晚也调派大批军队进城。多名匪徒被击毙”。

December 24, 1936.
2
Morning Translation.
No. D 2675.
Date 24/12/36

Lih Pao publishes the following telegram from Nanking :-

THE COUP IN SIAN

According to a certain high Government official, the recent revolt of the rebel General Chang Hsueh Liang was a pre-arranged plot. After Mr. Siao Nai Hwa, Personal Secretary of the Generalissimo, was killed, the code book was seized by the rebels. Using the code Chang Hsueh Liang at once sent telegrams in the name of General Chiang Kai Shek to Generals Liu Shih, Ho Chen Chin, Ho Ying Ching, Chen Chi, Chu Pei Teh, Tang Sung Tse and others, instructing them to proceed immediately to Sian to receive confidential instructions verbally from the Generalissimo. Chang Hsueh Liang's object was to do away with all the military leaders of the National Government at one stroke.

Upon receipt of this false telegram, General Ho Ying Ching and others at once made arrangements to fly to Sian.

General Feng Yu Hsiang, however, said to them: "Why should we all be required to proceed to Sian at one time. The matter requires careful consideration."

The proposed trip was postponed for about two hours. In the meantime news of the Sian uprising was received from the railway authorities.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

To-Day's General Meeting of Representatives of Shanghai Various Circles to Support the Central Government

At 2 p.m. to-day, the local Kuomintang headquarters will call a "General Meeting of Representatives of Shanghai Various Circles in Support of the Central Government to Send an Expedition against the Rebels" in the auditorium of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Soochow Road. A notification is published by the Tangpu in the advertisement columns of local newspapers to-day inviting Party and government organs, public bodies and schools to send three delegates each to attend the meeting.

The following will compose the presidium of the meeting:- Mayor Wu Teh Chen, General Yang Fu, General Tsai Chin Chun, Messrs. Pan Kung Chan, Dong Ying Bah, Wong Shao Lai, Tu Yuet Seng, Tsu Hsueh Van, Chang Shou Yung, Pang Kung Pih, Yue Chung Hwei and Huang Chao Yung.

The Bureau of Public Safety will detail policemen to maintain order at the meeting.

The programme of the meeting will be as follows :-
(1) Opening of the meeting.
(2) Music by the Band of the Public Safety Bureau.
(3) Respect to the National and Party Flags as well as to the portrait of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen.
(4) The reading of Dr. Sun's will.
(5) Three-minute silence in memory of the martyrs who fell during the Sian incident.
(6) Chairman's report.
(7) Speeches
(8) Discussion of proposals
(9) Shouting of slogans
(10) Music
(11) Meeting ends.

日期 36 年 12 月 24 日

《立报》刊登如下南京电文：-

西安事变

据某政府高官称，叛逆将领张学良近期的叛变是一场预谋的阴谋。在委员长私人秘书萧乃华先生遇害后，密码本被叛军缴获。张学良利用密码，立即以蒋介石将军的名义向刘峙、何成浚、何应钦、陈济棠、朱培德、唐生智等将军发送电报，指示他们立即前往西安，当面接受委员长的机密指令。张学良的目的是企图一举消灭国民政府的所有军事领袖。

收到这封假电报后，何应钦将军等人立即安排飞往西安。

然而，冯玉祥将军对他们说：“为何要求我们所有人同时前往西安。此事需要慎重考虑。”

拟议的行程推迟了约两小时。在此期间，从铁路当局收到了西安起义的消息。

《顺报》及其他本地报纸：-

今日上海各界代表举行大会支持中央政府

今日下午 2 时，当地国民党总部将在北苏州路上海总商会礼堂召开“上海各界代表拥护中央讨逆大会”。公安局今日在本地报纸广告栏发布通知，邀请党政机关、公共团体和学校各派三名代表出席会议。

会议主席团由以下人员组成：- 市长吴铁城、杨虎将军、蔡劲军将军、潘公展先生、董英拔先生、王少莱先生、杜月笙先生、褚学范先生、张寿镛先生、庞公璧先生、岳钟辉先生及黄朝庸先生。

公共安全局将派遣警察维持会议秩序。

会议议程如下：-
(1) 开会。
(2) 公共安全局乐队演奏音乐。
(3) 向国旗、党旗及孙中山先生遗像致敬。
(4) 宣读孙中山先生遗嘱。
(5) 为西安事变中牺牲的烈士默哀三分钟。
(6) 主席报告。
(7) 演讲
(8) 讨论提案
(9) 呼口号
(10) 奏乐
(11) 散会。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. E. REGISTRY.
No. D
Date / /

December 24, 1936.    3    Morning Translation

With a view to making the local community
acquainted with the rebellious acts of Chang Hsueh Liang,
the local fangpu has prepared a large quantity of coloured
paper slips bearing slogans denouncing Chang Hsueh Liang,
supporting an expedition against the rebels and urging the
rescue of General Chiang Kai Shek. It has arranged to have
these paper slips distributed this afternoon by an aeroplane.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

Death of a German Dentist

During the trouble in Sian, a German dentist
named Dr. Herr Wunsch was killed by the rebels. This tragic
news was confirmed yesterday by our representative at various
sources.

Dr. Wunsch in the early part of this year
was in practice in Shanghai at No. 1191 Bubbling Well Road,
but owing to bad business he went to Sian where he had been
doing very good business owing to the fact that he was the
only German dentist in that place.

During the revolt on December 12, a group
of rebel troops arrived at his place and owing to language
difficulties, a misunderstanding arose as a result of which
the rebels opened fire. The German dentist died
instantaneously.

At about the same time, another German
named Mr. Friese, advisor to General Chang Hsueh Liang, was
likewise assaulted by the rebels, but fortunately he did
not sustain serious injury. With the exception of these
two incidents, no harm has befallen any foreign resident
in Shensi.

According to information secured from the
Eurasian Aviation Corporation, Mr. "Rots", a German pilot,
and Mr. "Fisu", assistant pilot, of the Corporation are
still being detained in Sian by the rebel Chang Hsueh Liang.
It is also learned that recently Chang
Hsueh Liang sent a telegram to the Eurasian Aviation
Corporation stating that if the Corporation would despatch
an aeroplane to Sian, the two aviators would be released,
but the offer was ignored because the Corporation regards
Chang Hsueh Liang as a man who is insincere and cannot be
trusted.

Lih Pao :-

JAPANESE MOTOR CYCLIST KNOCKS DOWN HAWKER

At about 9 a.m. yesterday, a certain Japanese,
whilst passing near the corner of Gordon Road and Penang Road
on a motor cycle, knocked down a Chinese hawker named Chu Sin
Dah (朱新达) who was selling fried puffed flour balls. The
Japanese cyclist decamped at a high speed in a northerly
direction.

The accident was witnessed by several
pedestrians who at once reported the matter to the Police.
The injured hawker was removed to a hospital for treatment.
A slight injury to his leg was treated and he was able to
leave the hospital immediately.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
东南区登记处。
第 D 号
日期 / /

1936 年 12 月 24 日。    3    上午译件

为使本地社区了解张学良的叛逆行径，
本地房铺（注：此处原文为 fangpu，疑指警方或相关宣传机构，按音译保留或依语境理解为当局宣传部门，鉴于前文有 Tangpu/党部，此处可能指 Fangpu/分局或特定机构，暂按字面译为房铺，但结合语境更可能是“当局”或“警方”的误植，若指 Police Station 则为巡捕房。考虑到上下文是散发传单，且前文有 Public Safety Bureau，此处 fangpu 极可能是“分局”或“党部”的拼音误写，但根据规则不确定保留原文加音译。然而，结合“coloured paper slips”和 slogans，这通常是政治宣传。若参照前文 Chin Pao 文章中的 "XX lords" 和 "Council"，此处 fangpu 可能指代某种官方机构。为严谨起见，若无法确定具体对应中文机构名，按规则处理。但在民国档案语境下，fangpu 极大概率是“分局” (Fen Ju) 或 “党部” (Dang Bu) 的 OCR 错误或拼写错误。鉴于前文有 Tangpu (党部)，此处可能是 Fenpu (分局)。但若严格按规则“不确定的保留原文并加括号注明(音译)”，则应写作 fangpu (音译)。不过，通常此类传单由警方或党部发放。让我们看下文 Lih Pao 的内容。这里暂按规则处理，若认为是明显错误可标注。但“fangpu”并非标准拼音。可能是“Fanpu”？或者就是“Party Headquarters”的误写？再看前文“Tangpu”即党部。此处“fangpu”可能是“分局” (Fenju) 的误拼。为了安全，我将译为“当局（原文为 fangpu，音译）”或直接根据语境推测为警方/党部。但规则4说“明显是 OCR 遗留的乱码...不要脑补”。fangpu 看起来像是一个词的拼音。如果是“分局”，拼音是 Fenju。如果是“党部”，是 Dangbu。如果是“防务”，是 Fangwu。这里可能是“方铺”？不通。考虑到这是 SMP 档案，可能是 Chinese Section 的报告。通常会说“本局”或“分局”。我将保守地译为“本地当局（原文 fangpu，音译）”或者如果确信是“分局”的误写，可以标注。但为了严格遵守规则3和4，我将保留原文注音或译为最接近的通用词。在此语境下，散发谴责传单通常是政府或党部行为。前文提到“Tangpu” (党部) 发通知。这里可能是“Fenju” (分局) 的误写。我将译为“本地分局（原文 fangpu，音译）”以示谨慎，或者直接译为“本地当局”。
*修正思考*：规则3说“能确定的用当时通行的中文...不确定的保留原文并加括号注明(音译)”。fangpu 不是一个标准的地名或人名。它很可能是“分局” (Fen Ju) 或 “党部” (Dang Bu) 的打字错误。鉴于前文刚提到 Tangpu，这里可能是指另一个机构。在 SMP 档案中，Chinese Section 常引用中文报纸。报纸原文可能是“分局”或“市府”。由于无法 100% 确定，我将按规则处理为：本地 fangpu (音译)。但这样阅读体验不好。再看一眼，有没有可能是“防共”？不像。
让我们看回译文策略。如果我不确定，我必须保留原文。
译文：本地 fangpu (音译) 已准备大量彩色纸条...
或者，考虑到这是翻译任务，且上下文是“making the local community acquainted”，这通常是宣传行为。
我将译为：本地当局（原文 fangpu，音译）

准备了大量印有谴责张学良、
支持讨伐叛逆并呼吁营救蒋介石将军口号的彩色
纸条。已安排于今日下午由飞机
投放这些纸条。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：-

一名德国牙医死亡

在西安骚乱期间，一名名为
Wunsch (音译) 博士的德国牙医
被叛军杀害。这一悲惨
消息昨日经我方代表从多方
消息源证实。

Wunsch 博士今年早些时候
在上海静安寺路 1191 号执业，
但因生意不佳前往西安，在那里
他的生意非常好，因为他是
当地唯一的德国牙医。

在 12 月 12 日的叛乱期间，一群
叛军士兵来到他的住所，由于
语言障碍，产生了误会，导致
叛军开火。这名德国牙医当场
死亡。

大约在同一时间，另一名名为
Friese (音译) 先生的德国人，张学良将军的顾问，
也遭到叛军袭击，但幸运的是他
未受重伤。除这两起
事件外，陕西的外国居民未受
任何伤害。

据从欧亚航空公司获得的消息，
该公司的德国飞行员 "Rots" (音译) 先生
和副驾驶员 "Fisu" (音译) 先生
仍被叛逆的张学良扣押在西安。
另获悉，张学良
最近向欧亚航空公司发送电报称，
如果该公司派遣一架飞机到西安，
两名飞行员将被释放，
但这一提议被忽视，因为该公司认为
张学良是一个不真诚、不可信的人。

《立报》：-

日本骑摩托车者撞倒小贩

昨日上午 9 时许，一名日本人
骑摩托车经过戈登路与槟榔路
拐角附近时，撞倒了一名正在
售卖炸膨化面粉球的中国小贩，
名叫朱新达。该日本骑车人
高速向北逃逸。

几名行人目睹了这起
事故，并立即向警方报告。
受伤的小贩被送往医院治疗。
其腿部轻伤经处理后，他随即
出院。

December 24, 1936.    Morning Translation    7675
                                            24 / 12 / 36

MAINICHI

RED BANDITS APPEAR IN CENTRAL CHINA

    A telegram from Hangchow
reports that at 4 p.m. December 21 red troops occupied
Chang Hwa Prefecture in Chekiang Province about 200
Chinese li west of Hangchow.    The office of the
Prefectural Government and the District Kuomintang
were destroyed.    Mr. Chang Pang Van, a member of the
District Kuomintang, was killed and Mr. Ching Lih Ming,
a Prefect, was detained by the Reds.
    The Provincial Government has
dispatched soldiers to the place to suppress the outlaws.

BRITISH AND AMERICAN AMBASSADORS TO MEDIATE IN
SIAN AFFAIR

    A Daito telegram from Tientsin
reports that the mediation by Mr. Donald, advisor to
General Chiang Kai Shek, and Mr. T. V. Soong in the
Sian incident has failed.    General Yu Yu Jen, Pacification
Commissioner, and General Yen Hsi Shan's representative
left for Sian on December 23.    It is reported that
British and American diplomats are endeavouring to
mediate between Sian and Nanking; they are persuading
General Chang Hsueh Liang and General Yang Hu Chung to
go abroad.

JAPANESE MARINES WITHDRAW FROM TSINGTAO

    A Domei telegram from Tokyo
reports that on December 23 the Japanese marines landed
at Tsingtao on December 3 to protect Japanese residents
during the mill strikes have been completely withdrawn to
the Japanese warships because the strike situation has
become normal.

1936 年 12 月 24 日。    上午译件    7675
                                            36 年 12 月 24 日

《每日新闻》

赤匪出现在华中

    杭州电报
报道，12 月 21 日下午 4 时，赤色部队占领了
浙江省金华府（注：原文 Chang Hwa，通常指金华，但前文有 Chong Hua 崇化，此处 Chang Hwa 可能是金华 Jinhua 或长兴 Changxing 等的误拼，或者是“昌化”？Changhua 可能是昌化。昌化县在浙江西部。前文崇化县可能是笔误或旧称。此处 Chang Hwa 按音译为昌化或保留。考虑到“west of Hangchow 200 li”，昌化符合地理位置。金华较远。故译为昌化），位于杭州以西约 200
华里处。    府
政府办公室和区国民党
部被毁。    区国民党
党员张邦范（音译）先生被杀，知事
程立明（音译）先生被赤匪扣押。
    省政府已
派遣士兵前往该地平定匪患。

英美大使调解
西安事变

    天津大东电报
报道，蒋介石将军的顾问唐纳德先生
和宋子文先生在西安
事变中的调解已失败。    安抚
专员于右任将军和阎锡山将军的代表
于 12 月 23 日启程前往西安。    据报道，
英国和美国外交官正努力
在西安和南京之间进行调解；他们正在劝说
张学良将军和杨虎城将军
出国。

日本海军陆战队从青岛撤离

    东京同盟社电报
报道，12 月 23 日，日本海军陆战队
于 12 月 3 日登陆青岛以保护日本居民
免受纱厂罢工影响，现因
罢工局势恢复正常，已完全撤回
日本军舰。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 24, 1936

Reported Death Of
German Unconfirmed

Inquiries made at the German
Consulate and other German
sources here yesterday failed to
elicit any further news or confir-
mation of the alleged death of one
Herr Wunach, German dentist, who
is reported to have been killed in
Sian during the coup on Dec. 12.

德国人死亡消息
未经证实

昨日向德国
领事馆及其他在沪德国
方面进行的查询，未能
获取任何进一步消息或确
认关于一名名为

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 24, 1936
18872
7675
24 12 36

American Is
Prisoner Of
Chang At Sian

Chief Hangchow School
Air Mechanic Held
By Insurrectos
— Reg to Ira Gk

Mr. Edward Weingart, American
and chief mechanic of the National
Aviation Academy at Hangchow, is
being held a prisoner at Sian by
General Chang Hsueh-liang, accord-
ing to information obtained from
authentic sources by THE CHINA
PRESS last night.

Made a prisoner on December 12,
the same day Generalissimo Chiang
was seized by General Chang, Mr.
Weingart is in no danger, the re-
ports continued. It stated that he
has been informed by his captor
that he will be released as soon as
the present trouble has been clear-
ed up. He also has been warned
against trying to escape.

Weingart left Hangchow a few
days before the seizure of the Gen-
eralissimo and arrived in Sian on
the morning of December 12. He
was asked to make the journey to
Sian by aviation authorities at
Nanking, the purpose of his trip
being to make some repairs on
Government planes stationed at the
Sian field.

Picked Up In Street

At the time of his arrival, THE
CHINA PRESS informant stated, Sian
was in turmoil due to the fact that
Generalissimo Chiang's bodyguards,
rather than lay down their arms as
requested by General Chang, elected
to fight. Weingart was picked up
on the street and taken to General
Chang where he was informed of
his detention. No reasons for his
being held have been revealed.

THE CHINA PRESS also learned that
Mr. Royal Leonard, American, who
is General Chang Hsueh-liang's
pilot, has been elected to the task
of keeping watch over Weingart. In
other words, Leonard is really the
mechanic's jailor and responsible if
the man gets away until General
Chang is ready to release him.

Besides the two European pilots and
Weingart, one other foreigner is
being held prisoner by General
Chang, THE CHINA PRESS learned.
This man is Captain Norman
Gill, British subject, who is captain
of the Chinese Air Force's heavy
bombers.

guards. THE CHINA PRESS informant
learned reports that the captain of
the guards had been killed or fail-
ed stated that Weingart was being
held in a house together with the
three other foreigners.

Quartered In Same House

The foreign pilots whenever made
trips to Sian and met with Mr. T. V.
Soong, Mr. W. H. Donald and others,
were quarters in the same house
where they are located. They are not
permitted to communicate with the for-
eign prisoners.

Mr. Weingart, it is learned, has
a wife and two children, and has
been stationed at Hangchow as chief
mechanic of the aviation school for
many months. His wife and two
children in China with him. They
are reported to be in Hangchow at
the present time.

美国人成为
张在西安的

杭州航校
首席机械师
被叛军扣押
— 致 Ira Gk（音译）

据《大美晚报》昨晚从可靠渠道获得的消息，美国人爱德华·温加特（Edward Weingart）先生，杭州国立航空学院首席机械师，正被张学良将军扣留在西安作为人质。

报道继续称，温加特先生于12月12日被捕，即蒋介石总司令被张将军扣押的同一天，但他并无危险。消息称，扣押者已告知他，一旦当前事态平息，他将被释放。他还受到警告，不得试图逃跑。

温加特在总司令被扣押前几天离开杭州，于12月12日上午抵达西安。他是应南京航空当局的要求前往西安的，此行目的是对停放在西安机场的政府飞机进行一些维修。

街头被捕

据《大美晚报》的消息人士称，在他抵达时，西安正处于混乱之中，因为蒋介石总司令的卫队没有按照张将军的要求放下武器，而是选择战斗。温加特在街上被带走，并被带到张将军处，被告知已被拘留。目前尚未透露扣留他的原因。

《大美晚报》还获悉，美国人罗亚尔·伦纳德（Royal Leonard）先生，即张学良将军的飞行员，已被指派负责看守温加特。换言之，伦纳德实际上是这名机械师的狱卒，如果此人在张将军准备释放他之前逃脱，伦纳德将承担责任。

《大美晚报》获悉，除了两名欧洲飞行员和温加特外，还有一名外国人被张将军扣押。此人是英国籍诺曼·吉尔（Norman Gill）上尉，中国空军重型轰炸机大队队长。

卫队。《大美晚报》的消息人士得知有报告称卫队队长已被杀或未能（原文不清），并指出温加特正与其他三名外国人一起被关押在一所房子里。

同住一处

据悉，外国飞行员每当前往西安并与宋子文先生、W. H. 唐纳德（W. H. Donald）先生等人会面时，都寄宿在他们目前所在的同一所房子里。他们不被允许与外国囚犯联系。

据悉，温加特先生有一位妻子和两个孩子，他已在杭州担任航校首席机械师数月。他的妻子和两个孩子与他一同在中国。据报道，他们目前身在杭州。

S. I. B.
J R

December 23, 1936.    2    Afternoon Translation.

Eastern Times and other local newspapers publish the following
reports:

MADAME CHIANG KAI SHEK TO FLY TO SIAN

At 10 a.m. December 22, Mr. T.V. Soong went with
Madame Chiang Kai Shek and Mr. Donald to Sianfu by aeroplane.
They were expected at the rebel city by 3 p.m.

A refugee from Shensi gives the following account
of the rebellion at Sians-
On the morning of December 12, the rebel troops
surrounded the Railway Station and General Chiang Kai Shek's
Field Headquarters. Under the leadership of Generals
Chien Ta Chang and Chiang Shao Sien, the 200 bodyguards
of the Generalissimo put up a brave resistance. The Chief
Bodyguard Chien was wounded, while General Chiang Shao Sien
was killed. Most of the bodyguards were either wounded
or killed. Some of the bodyguards escorted the
Generalissimo to a cave on a hill. Pah Feng Hsiang,
a battalion commander under the rebel leader, pursued them
to the cave. The bodyguards resisted, but were ordered
by the Generalissimo to desist. General Chiang Kai Shek
told Pah to kill them all if he liked, but the latter
replied that he had no wish to do this and that he had been
instructed to protect him to the city.
After the incident, the railway stations at Ling-
chun and Weinen were destroyed by fire. The Stationmasters
together with some 10 other officials were killed. Rebel
soldiers and ruffians then started looting the houses of
the dead. The food supplies in the city are running
short and the people are panic stricken.

46 Followers of Generalissimo Killed

When General Chiang Kai Shek proceeded to Shensi,
he had 52 attendants. After the rebellion, only six of
the guards were alive.

Chinese edition of the Shanghai Nichi Nichi:

Mr. Chiang Meng Ling, Principal of the Peiping
University, together with the principals of other universities
recently sent a telegram to Chang Hsueh Liang requesting him
to protect General Chiang.
In reply, General Chang stated as follows:-
"I guarantee the safety of General Chiang Kai Shek. The
incident of December 12 was inevitable and was carried out
in the hope that General Chiang Kai Shek would change his
policy and resist the enemy immediately. My movement will
end when this object has been attained. After that I shall
submit myself for punishment."

Lih Pao:

BROADCASTING PROGRAMMES TO BE CENSORED BY CENTRAL
BROADCASTING AFFAIRS CONTROL BUREAU

Commencing from next month, the programmes of
local radio broadcasting stations will be censored by the
Central Broadcasting Affairs Control Bureau.

1936年12月23日。    2    下午译文。

《申报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下报道：

蒋夫人将飞往西安

12月22日上午10时，宋子文先生偕蒋夫人及唐纳德先生乘飞机前往西安府。预计他们将于下午3时抵达这座叛军控制的城市。

一名来自陕西的难民对西安叛乱情况叙述如下：
12月12日上午，叛军包围了火车站和蒋介石总司令的行营总部。在钱大钧将军和蒋孝先将军的率领下，总司令的200名卫队进行了英勇抵抗。卫队长钱大钧受伤，蒋孝先将军阵亡。大多数卫队成员非伤即亡。部分卫队成员护送总司令至山上的一处洞穴。叛军首领麾下的营长鲍凤翔（音译）追至洞穴。卫队进行抵抗，但奉总司令之命停止抵抗。蒋介石将军告诉鲍，若他愿意可将他们全部杀死，但后者回答说他不希望这样做，且他已受命保护总司令进城。
事件发生后，临潼和渭南的火车站被焚毁。站长及其他约10名官员遇害。随后，叛军士兵和流氓开始洗劫死者住宅。城内粮食供应短缺，民众惊慌失措。

46名总司令随从遇害

蒋介石总司令前往陕西时，共有52名随从。叛乱发生后，仅有六名卫兵幸存。

《上海日日新闻》中文版：

北京大学校长蒋梦麟先生联合其他大学校长近日致电张学良，请求其保护蒋将军。
张将军回复如下：“我保证蒋介石总司令的安全。12月12日之事变实属不可避免，此举旨在希望蒋介石总司令改变政策，立即抗日。一旦达到此目的，我的行动即将结束。此后我将听候惩处。”

《立报》：

广播节目将由中央广播事业管理处审查

自下月起，本地无线电台的节目将由中央广播事业管理处进行审查。

MAINICHI

TIENTSIN STUDENTS SUPPORT GENERAL CHANG HSUEH LIANG

A Daito telegram from Tientsin
reports that at 7 p.m. December 21 the Tientsin Students
Federation held a meeting to discuss the Sian incident.
The meeting decided to support
General Chang Hsueh Liang and to hold a demonstration on
December 22.
The Bureau of Public Safety,
as a precautionary measure, ordered the various schools
in Tientsin not to allow their students to leave school.

The Shanghai Kuomintang Headquarters has sent

西安政变：拥政府大会将于12月24日举行

国民党上海市党部已向各公共团体、学校及各区分部发出通知，要求各方派代表三人参加上海各界代表会议，以支持政府并镇压陕西叛军，会议定于12月24日下午2时在苏州路北路的上海总商会举行。

December 22, 1936. Morning Translation.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

THE SIAN COUP: COMMUNISTS SEEKING ALLIANCE WITH
GENERAL CHANG HSUEH LIANG

Taking advantage of the coup in Sian, Chow Heng
Lai (周恩來), one of the leaders of the Chinese Communist
Party, is reported to have gone to Sian and is arranging
an alliance with General Chang Hsueh Liang and General Yang
Fu Chen.
In the meantime the Nanking Government is
intensifying its operations in the punitive expedition
against the rebels.

Formation of Group of Representatives of Shanghai
People to Rescue General Chiang Kai Shek

At 2 p.m. yesterday people from all walks of
life held a meeting at No.692 Newchwang Road and formed
a Group of Representatives of Shanghai People to Rescue
General Chiang Kai Shek.

China Times and other local newspapers publish the following
telegraphic reports:

Mr. T.V. Soong Sees Generalissimo

Mr. T.V. Soong flew from Nanking to Loyang
on the afternoon of December 19. At 8 a.m. December 20
he left Loyang by plane for Sian. He was met at the
aerodrome at Sian by Generals Chang Hsueh Liang and Yang
Fu Chen. After a short rest Mr. T.V. Soong accompanied
by General Chang Hsueh Liang saw General Chiang Kai Shek.
Mr. Soong returned to Nanking by the same aeroplane at
4.25 p.m. December 21 and made a report to Madame Chiang
Kai Shek, Dr. H.H. Kung and General Ho Ying Ching. He
may go to Sian again on December 22.
It is said that Madame Chiang Kai Shek has
decided to fly to Sian.
Acting in a private capacity, Mr. T.V. Soong
left Nanking on December 19 to see General Chiang Kai Shek
in Sian. He returned to Nanking at 4.30 p.m. December 21.
It is said that Mr. Soong has returned in order to accompany
Madame Chiang Kai Shek to Sian.

The Chinese Edition of the Shanghai Nichi Nichi, a Japanese
newspaper, publishes the following telegraphic reports:

A certain committeeman of the Shensi Provincial
Kuomintang who managed to escape from Sian on December 20
disguised as a merchant gave the following account of
conditions in Sian prior to December 16:-
"General Chiang Kai Shek is being held in the
New City Building and cooks his own food. On December 16
Sian was thrown into confusion, but order was restored
soon afterwards. It is not true that red flags have
been flown in Sian. A North-West Military Commission
has been formed with General Chang Hsueh Liang as Chairman.

1936年12月22日。上午译文。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

西安政变：共产党寻求与张学良将军结盟

据悉，中国共产党领导人之一周恩来利用西安政变之机，已前往西安，正安排与张学良将军和杨虎城将军结成联盟。
与此同时，南京政府正在加强针对叛军的讨伐行动。

成立上海市民营救蒋委员长代表团

昨日下午2时，各界人士在新闸路692号举行会议，成立上海市民营救蒋委员长代表团。

《时报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下电讯报道：

宋子文先生会见总司令

宋子文先生于12月19日下午从南京飞抵洛阳。12月20日上午8时，他由洛阳乘飞机前往西安。张学良将军和杨虎城将军在西安机场迎接了他。短暂休息后，宋子文先生在张学良将军陪同下会见了蒋介石总司令。宋先生于12月21日下午4时25分乘同一架飞机返回南京，并向蒋夫人、孔祥熙博士及何应钦将军作了汇报。他可能于12月22日再次前往西安。
据悉，蒋夫人已决定飞往西安。
宋子文先生以私人身份于12月19日离开南京，前往西安会见蒋介石总司令。他于12月21日下午4时30分返回南京。据悉，宋先生返回是为了陪同蒋夫人前往西安。

日本报纸《上海日日新闻》中文版刊登如下电讯报道：

陕西省国民党某委员于12月20日化装成商人从西安逃出，他对12月16日之前西安的情况叙述如下：
“蒋介石总司令被关押在新城大楼，自行做饭。12月16日西安曾陷入混乱，但不久后秩序恢复。西安悬挂红旗之说并不属实。已成立西北军事委员会，由张学良将军任主席。

December 22, 1936. Morning Translation.

NICHI-NICHI

GENERAL CHANG HSUEH LIANG ADVISES ALL MILITARY
LEADERS TO FORM ANTI-JAPANESE MILITARY
COMMITTEE

A Daito telegram reports that
General Chang Hsueh Liang has abolished the North-West
Anti-Communist Commander's Headquarters and has organized
an Anti-Japanese United Military Committee of which he
is the chairman. General Chang Hsueh Liang is reported
to be advising all Chinese military leaders throughout
China to join the Committee. The authorities of the
Chahar-Hopei Political Council are believed to have
received General Chiang's advice but they have not yet
decided upon their attitude.

NIPPO

CHINESE COMMUNIST LEADER ENDEAVOURING TO WIN OVER
GENERAL YEN HSI SHAN

A telegram from Taiyuan reports
that owing to the Sian incident, General Yen Hsi Shan
now holds the key to a solution of the incident. The
Nanking Government is reported to be endeavouring to
induce General Yen Hsi Shan to help Nanking and has detailed
General Whang Hsiao Soong, Chairman of the Hupeh Provincial
Government to call on him.
Attaching great importance to
the position held by General Yen Hsi Shan, the Chinese
Communist Party on December 17 sent Chow Hung Iri, a
leader of the Party, to Taiyuan to secure an interview
with General Yen Hsi Shan through an introduction of one
of General Yen's pro-communist officers.
In the course of the interview
the following suggestions are said to have been made to
General Yen Hsi Shan:-
I. That a telegram be issued supporting General
Chang Hsueh Liang.
2. That a manifesto be issued announcing co-operation
with the Communist Party and resistance to Japan; that
the Nanking Government be urged to enforce this policy.
The communist leader is believed
to have gone to Sianfu.
Upon receipt of this information,
the Nanking Government is reported to be actively engaged
in discussing an adequate policy to deal with this
situation.
Judging by the above reports, an
understanding seems to have been reached between General
Yen Hsi Shan's troops, General Chang Hsueh Liang's troops
and the Red Army.

1936年12月22日。上午译文。

《日日新闻》

张学良将军劝告各军事领袖组建抗日军事委员会

大同社电报称，张学良将军已撤销西北剿共总司令部，并组织抗日联军军事委员会，由其担任主席。据悉，张学良将军正劝告全中国各地的军事领袖加入该委员会。察冀政务委员会当局据信已收到张将军的建议，但尚未决定其态度。

《尼波报》（Nippo）

中共领导人努力争取阎锡山将军

太原来电称，由于西安事变，阎锡山将军现在掌握了解决事变的关键。据悉，南京政府正努力促使阎锡山将军协助南京方面，并已派遣湖北省政府主席黄绍竑将军前去拜访他。
鉴于阎锡山将军所处地位的重要性，中国共产党于12月17日派遣该党领导人周洪毅（音译，注：此处原文为Chow Hung Iri，疑为周恩来或其他人的误拼或特定指代，按音译处理）前往太原，通过阎将军麾下的一名亲共军官引荐，以求得与阎锡山将军会晤。
据悉，在会晤过程中向阎锡山将军提出了以下建议：
1. 发表通电支持张学良将军。
2. 发表宣言，宣布与共产党合作并抵抗日本；敦促南京政府执行此政策。
据悉，这位共产党领导人已前往西安府。
据悉，南京政府在收到此消息后，正积极讨论应对这一局势的适当政策。
根据上述报道判断，阎锡山将军的部队、张学良将军的部队与红军之间似乎已达成谅解。

December 20, 1936. Morning Translation

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

THE COUP IN SIAN : GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK STILL DETAINED.

Up to the evening of December 19, no information was secured regarding the liberation of General Chiang Kai Shek or of his coming to Nanking. The Headquarters of the Commander-in-Chief to direct the punitive expedition against the rebel troops has sent an urgent telegram to the front instructing that bombardment of Sian be resumed on December 20.

Mr. Shao Yuan Chung, Madame Shao Lih Ts and two others dead

During the revolt in Sian that took place on December 12, Mr. Shao Yuan Chung, a member of the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang, Mr. Chiang Shiao Sien, Chief of the Bodyguards of General Chiang Kai Shek, Mr. Siao Nai Hwa, a clerk, and Madame Shao Lih Ts were wounded. They have since succumbed to their wounds.
In the meantime, many bodyguards of General Chiang Kai Shek were killed during the revolt for they resisted bravely.

Mr. T.V. Soong Flies to Sian

At 1 p.m. yesterday, Mr. T.V. Soong left Nanking for Sian by aeroplane for the purpose of interviewing General Chiang Kai Shek. The plane was forced to alight at Loyang owing to bad weather. If weather permits, Mr. Soong will fly to Sian on December 20.

Activities of Mr. J. Elder

Mr. James Elder, economic advisor to General Chang Hsueh Liang, arrived in Nanking on December 18 acting on instructions from the young Marshal. On the evening of that day, he came to Shanghai and sojourned at the Metropole Hotel, Kiangse Road.
On the morning of December 19, Mr. Elder was very busy in approaching the various sources interested. He will return to Nanking to-day whence he will proceed to Sian to call on General Chang Hsueh Liang.

Deposits of General Chang Hsueh Liang in Local Foreign Bank Drawn Out

According to reliable information secured from the banking circles, a deputy who was sent to Shanghai by General Chang Hsueh Liang drew large deposits on the morning of December 19 from a certain foreign bank on the Bund on behalf of the General. A part of the deposits will be remitted to England, while the other part was taken by this deputy to Sian for the use of General Chang.

1936年12月20日。晨间译稿

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下电讯报道：-

西安事变：蒋介石将军仍被扣押。

截至12月19日晚，尚未获得关于蒋介石将军获释或抵达南京的消息。讨逆军总司令部已向火线发出急电，指示于12月20日恢复对西安的轰炸。

邵元冲先生、邵力子夫人等二人身亡

在12月12日发生的西安事变中，国民党中央执行委员邵元冲先生、蒋介石将军的侍卫长蒋孝先先生、职员萧乃华先生以及邵力子夫人受伤。他们随后因伤重不治身亡。
与此同时，蒋介石将军的许多侍卫在事变中遇害，因为他们进行了英勇抵抗。

宋子文先生飞往西安

昨日下午1时，宋子文先生离开南京乘飞机前往西安，目的是面见蒋介石将军。由于天气恶劣，飞机被迫降落在洛阳。如果天气允许，宋先生将于12月20日飞往西安。

詹姆士·埃尔德先生的活动

张学良将军的经济顾问詹姆士·埃尔德（James Elder）先生奉少帅之命，于12月18日抵达南京。当晚，他来到上海，寓居江西路大都会酒店（Metropole Hotel）。
12月19日上午，埃尔德先生忙于接触各方有关人士。他将于今日返回南京，随后前往西安拜访张学良将军。

张学良将军在当地外资银行的存款被提取

据从银行界获得的可靠消息，张学良将军派往上海的一名副手于12月19日上午代表张将军从外滩某家外资银行提取了大量存款。部分存款将汇往英国，另一部分则由该副手带往西安，供张将军使用。

December 13, 1936.    Morning Translation

Shun Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

THE COUP IN SIAN : GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK EXPECTED TO RETURN TO NANKING TO-DAY.

General Chiang Ting Wen, Commander of the Second Army, arrived at Loyang on the afternoon of December 17 and left for Nanking by aeroplane on the morning of December 18. He landed at the Ming Palace Aerodrome at 11.50 a.m. December 18 and was met by Madame Chiang Kai Shek, Mr. T.V. Soong, General Feng Yu Hsiang and members of the families of the other high officials detained in Sian. In reply to inquiries put by Mr. T.V. Soong and General Feng Yu Hsiang regarding General Chiang Kai shek's health, he said that General Chiang is safe and sound.

General Ho Ying Ching's Statement

In an interview with a newspaper reporter, General Ho Ying Ching, Minister of War, said :- "Since my appointment as Commander-in-Chief of the Punitive Campaign, I have already directed the Government troops to push on to Sian in accordance with the instructions of the National Government. I am now in receipt of the following letter dated December 17 addressed to me by General Chiang Kai Shek at Sian and handed to me by General Chiang Ting Wen :-
'I have learned that the air force started bombing Weinan yesterday. I wish you to order the operations to cease immediately. According to my observation of recent events, I may return to Nanking before Saturday this week. Therefore, fighting should be avoided before Saturday, particularly the bombing by aeroplanes must cease'.
"As soon as I received the letter, I sent telegrams to the front directing a cessation of the bombing until 6 p.m. December 19. If rebel Chang Hsueh Liang fails to escort General Chiang Kai Shek to Nanking by that time, I shall have to carry out the original plans to the full so as to stamp out the rebellion".

General Chiang Ting Wen's statement

Interviewed by newspaper reporters following his arrival at Nanking, General Chiang Ting Wen gave the following account of the coup in Sian :-
"Immediately after the outbreak of the revolt, General Chiang Kai Shek and a number of other high political and military officials and myself were detained and held separately. Chang Hsueh Liang frequently visited us. He said that at every visit he had paid to General Chiang Kai Shek he was scoffed. At the first visit he was severely reprimanded by General Chiang Kai Shek who said: 'Since you address me as Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission, this means that you are my subordinate. To-day you have only one way to deal with me: if you recognise me as your superior officer, you must immediately send me back to Loyang, otherwise you are a rebel. In that case, since I am in the hands of you rebels, you can kill me. There is nothing else to say.'

1936年12月13日。晨间译稿

《申报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下电讯报道：-

西安事变：预计蒋介石将军今日返回南京。

第二军军长蒋鼎文将军于12月17日下午抵达洛阳，并于12月18日上午乘飞机离开前往南京。他于12月18日上午11时50分降落在明故宫机场，受到蒋介石夫人、宋子文先生、冯玉祥将军以及其他在西安被扣高官家属的迎接。在回答宋子文先生和冯玉祥将军关于蒋介石将军健康状况的询问时，他表示蒋介石将军安然无恙。

何应钦将军的声明

陆军部长何应钦将军在接受报社记者采访时说：- “自我就任讨逆军总司令以来，我已遵照国民政府的指令，指挥政府军向西安推进。我现已收到蒋介石将军于12月17日从西安写给我、并由蒋鼎文将军转交的信函，内容如下：
‘获悉空军昨日开始轰炸渭南。望你立即命令停止行动。根据我对近期事态的观察，我可能在本周六之前返回南京。因此，在周六之前应避免战斗，特别是必须停止飞机轰炸’。
“我一收到此信，便向前线发出电报，指示停止轰炸直至12月19日下午6时。如果叛将张学良届时未能护送蒋介石将军抵达南京，我将不得不全面实施原定计划，以彻底平定叛乱”。

蒋鼎文将军的声明

蒋鼎文将军抵达南京后接受报社记者采访，就西安事变作了如下陈述：-
“事变爆发后，蒋介石将军和其他多位党政军高官以及我本人立即被扣押，并分别关押。张学良经常来看望我们。他说，每次探望蒋介石将军时都遭到斥责。第一次探望时，他受到蒋介石将军的严厉训斥，蒋说：‘既然你称我为军事委员会委员长，这就意味着你是我的部下。今天你只有一条路可以对待我：如果你承认我是你的上级军官，你必须立即送我回洛阳，否则你就是叛逆。既然如此，既然我落在你们这些叛逆手中，你可以杀了我。无话可说。’

December 19, 1936. Morning Translation.

"During the past few days, the Government troops have been pushing on and detailed aeroplanes to drop bombs. Chang Hsueh Liang asked me to call on General Chiang Kai Shek. I saw General Chiang Kai Shek at 9 a.m. December 17 in company with Chang Hsueh Liang for the latter did not permit me to converse alone with General Chiang. The Generalissimo was calm. He wrote two letters and ordered me to hand one to General Ho Ying Ching and the other to Madame Chiang Kai Shek. He then said to me: 'You can go back and tell the public that even Chang Hsueh Liang and his followers must now have an understanding of my views about national affairs. The rest is explained in detail in my letter to General Ho Ying Ching. According to my observation of recent events, I may return to Nanking in a few days.' After my interview with General Chiang Kai Shek, I left Sian by a military aeroplane at noon December 17 for Loyang."

In reply to further questions put by newspaper reporters regarding the situation in Sian, General Chiang Ting Wen said that as he had been entirely removed from touch with the outside world, he knew nothing of what was going on there.

Mr. Yu Yu Jen On Way to Loyang

On December 18 the Control Yuan received a telegram from Kaifeng stating that Mr. Yu Yu Jen, President of the Control Yuan who had been detailed by the Government to Sian to appease the troops and people, arrived there on the morning of December 18. Mr. Yu interviewed General Shang Chen, Chairman of the Honan Provincial Government, and other officials. Mr. Yu's special train was expected at Loyang on the afternoon of December 18.

Mr. Yu Yu Jen passed through Chengchow at 11 a.m. December 18. On arrival at Loyang he will get into touch with General Chang Hsueh Liang by telegram before proceeding to Shensi.

Return of Mr. Wang Ching Wei

In response to a summons from the National Government, Mr. Wang Ching Wei is now on his way back to China and is due in Shanghai in the latter part of January.

Chang Hsueh Liang's Mother Going to Nanking

It is reported that General Chang Hsueh Liang's mother, who is now staying at Tientsin, is leaving for Nanking on the afternoon of December 18.

Search For General Chang's Family

Chang Hsueh Chen and Chang Hsueh Ming, the brothers of General Chang Hsueh Liang, who reside on 32nd Street, French Concession, Tientsin, and Hongkong Road, British Concession, Tientsin, respectively, escaped with their families on the night of December 17. Their homes are being looked after by the British and French authorities.

1936年12月19日。晨间译稿。

“过去几天，政府军不断推进，并派遣飞机投掷炸弹。张学良要求我去拜访蒋介石将军。12月17日上午9时，我在张学良的陪同下见到了蒋介石将军，因为后者不允许我与蒋介石将军单独交谈。委员长神情镇定。他写了两封信，命令我将其中一封交给何应钦将军，另一封交给蒋介石夫人。然后他对我说：‘你可以回去告诉公众，即使是张学良及其追随者，现在也必须理解我对国家事务的看法。其余细节在我给何应钦将军的信中已有详细说明。根据我对近期事态的观察，我可能在几天内返回南京。’在与蒋介石将军会面后，我于12月17日中午乘军用飞机离开西安前往洛阳。”

在回答报社记者关于西安局势的进一步提问时，蒋鼎文将军表示，由于他与外界完全隔绝，他对那里发生的情况一无所知。

于右任先生正在前往洛阳途中

12月18日，监察院收到来自开封的电报，称受政府委派前往西安安抚军民的监察院院长于右任先生已于12月18日上午抵达该地。于先生会见了河南省政府主席商震将军及其他官员。于先生的专列预计于12月18日下午抵达洛阳。

于右任先生于12月18日上午11时途经郑州。抵达洛阳后，他将在前往陕西之前通过电报与张学良将军取得联系。

汪精卫先生回国

应国民政府召唤，汪精卫先生目前正在返回中国途中，预计将于1月下旬抵达上海。

张学良之母前往南京

据报道，目前居住在天津的张学良将军之母将于12月18日下午启程前往南京。

搜寻张氏家属

居住在天津法租界三十二号街和天津英租界香港路的张学良将军之弟张学曾和张学铭，于12月17日晚携家眷出逃。他们的住所正由英法当局照看。

December 19, 1936. Morning Translation.

Organizations are being formed by youths in Tientsin to search for members of Chang's family in order to send them to Nanking to be held as hostages against the release of General Chiang Kai Shek by Chang Hsueh Liang.

Attitude of Former Officials of the North-East

General Chang Tso Siang, ex-Governor of Kirin Province, is in Tientsin. All the elder members of the North-East clique are highly indignant at the action of General Chang Hsueh Liang, and have warned their relatives and friends against having any social intercourse with the family of General Chang Hsueh Liang. A certain retired high official of the North-East clique on December 18 sent a private letter to General Chang Hsueh Liang advising him to repent before it is too late.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

Arrival of Mr. Elder, Economic Advisor to General Chang Hsueh Liang

On December 16, Mr. James Elder, economic advisor to General Chang Hsueh Liang, left Sian for Nanking by aeroplane. When passing through Pengpu, the plane alighted owing to heavy rain. Mr. Elder then took a train and arrived at Nanking on December 18.
Upon reaching the Capital, Mr. Elder kept his movements very secret. He called on Dr. H.H. Kung, but did not meet other high Government officials.
Mr. Elder arrived in Shanghai at 11 p.m. yesterday from Nanking by train. He travelled first class, but he alighted from a second class carriage. Lest his whereabouts should become known to the public, he took a ricsha to Zung Chi Road (众义路) where he hired a motor car from the Ford Hire Service to take him to the residence of Dr. H.H. Kung on Route Herve de Sieyes, French Concession.
The public are paying much attention to the movements and activities of Mr. Elder.

Lih Pao :-

No Japanese at Sian

Following the revolt in Sian, the authorities of foreign countries in China are paying close attention to the safety of their residents in Sian.
Mr. Yatani of the Intelligence Section of the Japanese Embassy declares that there are no Japanese residents in Sian.

1936年12月19日。晨间译稿。

天津的青年正在组建组织，搜寻张氏家族成员，以便将他们送往南京作为人质，以换取张学良释放蒋介石将军。

东北前官员的态度

前吉林省主席张作相将军目前在天津。东北系的所有元老成员对张学良将军的行为感到极度愤慨，并警告亲友不要与张学良将军的家族有任何社交往来。东北系的一位退休高官于12月18日向张学良将军发出一封私信，劝其趁早悔悟。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：-

张学良将军经济顾问埃尔德先生抵达

12月16日，张学良将军的经济顾问詹姆士·埃尔德（James Elder）先生乘飞机离开西安前往南京。途经蚌埠时，因大雨飞机降落。埃尔德先生随后改乘火车，于12月18日抵达南京。
抵达首都后，埃尔德先生的行踪非常隐秘。他拜访了孔祥熙博士，但未会见其他政府高官。
埃尔德先生于昨晚11时乘火车从南京抵达上海。他购买的是一等座车票，但从二等车厢下车。为了避免行踪被公众知晓，他乘坐人力车前往众义路，在那里从福特租车行（Ford Hire Service）租用了一辆汽车，将他送往法租界赫维德西斯路（Route Herve de Sieyes）孔祥熙博士的寓所。
公众非常关注埃尔德先生的行踪和活动。

《立报》：-

西安无日本人

西安事变发生后，在华各国当局密切关注其驻西安居民的安全。
日本大使馆情报部的谷谷尼（Yatani，音译）先生宣称，西安没有日本居民。

December 19, 1936. Morning Translation

upholding the nation's prestige, issued an official mandate for a punitive expedition against the rebels. General Ho Ying Ching was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the operations against the rebels.
Yesterday General Wu Teh Chen, Mayor of Shanghai, sent a telegram to the Military Affairs Commission, the various Yuans and Ministries and other military and government organs, newspapers, etc., throughout the country pledging his heartfelt support to the punitive expedition. Mayor Wu denounces Chang Hsueh Liang whom he accuses with having committed an unpardonable act not only against the Government but also the Kuomintang and in this connection he deserves to be put to death by any person who can get at him.
Mayor Wu Teh Chen has also sent a telegram to Generals Ho Ying Ching, Liu Shih and Koo Tsoh Dong wishing success for the punitive expedition.

Action Condemned By Nation

Yesterday Mr. Yu Ya Ching expressed the following views on the coup at Sian:-
"Just as political conditions have become more stabilized and unified, the national defences consolidated and the suppression of the communists nearing its completion, the people received a rude shock through the revolt at Sian, a revolt which has aroused the highest indignation and resulted in a strong denunciation by the public throughout the country. Due to the painstaking and fearless efforts on the part of our leader, General Chiang Kai Shek, both internal and diplomatic affairs have triumphed over a series of crises and have taken a turn for the better, thereby enabling China to become a united nation and be in a position to resist invasion. The meritorious service done by General Chiang Kai Shek is unprecedented in Chinese history and this fact is also recognized by foreigners. The sudden detention of General Chiang Kai Shek as a hostage in Sian will do great harm to the nation and people. I am unaware of the motive of the leader of the Sian revolt but he will, no doubt, be condemned by the whole Chinese nation. I hope that he will quickly repent and at once liberate General Chiang; he should also resume the operations against the communists so as to make atonement for his terrible mistake."

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

ENTERTAINMENT IN AID OF SUIYUAN

With a view to raising contributions in aid of the bandit suppression forces in Suiyuan, many local dramatic bodies arranged a general broadcasting programme to be given on December 20 from 8 a.m. to 2 a.m. the next day, from the broadcasting station of the Great China Dispensary, Foochow Road.
Yesterday the Broadcasting Programme Committee of the dramatic bodies issued a notice announcing the cancellation of the admission tickets already sold and stating that these tickets may be contributed towards the purchase of ambulances.

1936年12月19日。晨间译稿

为维护国家威望，发布讨伐叛逆的正式命令。何应钦将军被任命为讨逆行动总司令。
昨日，上海市市长吴铁城向全国各地的军事委员会、各院部及其他军政机关、报纸等发出电报，誓言衷心支持讨逆行动。吴市长谴责张学良，指控其犯下了不仅针对政府，而且针对国民党的不可饶恕的罪行，在此情况下，任何能抓到他的人都可将其处死。
吴铁城市长还向何应钦、刘峙和顾祝同（音译）将军发出电报，祝愿讨逆行动取得成功。

全国谴责该行动

昨日，虞洽卿先生就西安事变发表如下观点：
“正当政治局势趋于稳定统一，国防得到巩固，剿共接近完成之际，民众因西安叛乱而受到强烈冲击，这一叛乱激起了极大的愤慨，并导致全国公众的强烈谴责。由于我们的领袖蒋介石将军不辞辛劳、无畏的努力，内政和外交事务均战胜了一系列危机并出现好转，从而使中国成为一个团结的国家，并有能力抵抗侵略。蒋介石将军的功绩在中国历史上是空前的，这一事实也为外国人所认可。蒋介石将军在西安突然被扣为人质，将对国家和人民造成巨大危害。我不清楚西安叛乱领导者的动机，但他无疑将受到全中国人的谴责。我希望他能迅速悔悟，立即释放蒋将军；他还应恢复剿共行动，以弥补其可怕的错误。”

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

绥远助赈游艺会

为筹集捐款援助绥远剿匪部队，许多本地戏剧团体安排于12月20日上午8时至次日凌晨2时，在福州路的大中华制药厂广播电台举行联合广播节目。
昨日，各戏剧团体的广播节目委员会发布公告，宣布取消已售出的入场券，并声明这些票款可捐赠用于购买救护车。

12月18日，在河南路452号和505号房屋的墙壁上发现张贴了两份谴责张学良将军并支持蒋介石将军的小册子。

December 18, 1936.    3.    Morning Translation.
(印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE ... No. D 2675 Date 18/12/36)

China Times and other local newspapers :-

Mr. Yu Yu Jen Appointed Pacification Commissioner To
Appease Troops and People of the North-West

Mr. Yu Yu Jen, President of the Control Yuan,
has been appointed Pacification Commissioner to Appease the
Troops and People of the North-West in accordance with a
resolution passed at the Central Political Council on
December 16.
Mr. Yu left for Tung Kwan (潼關) on December 17
and will establish his office at Loyang. Whether he will
proceed to Sian to interview Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek
will depend on circumstances.

Messrs. Wong Shiao Lai, Tu Yuet Sen and Zien
Sing Ts Offer Themselves As Hostages

Mr. Wong Shiao Lai (王曉), Chairman of the
Shanghai Chamber of Commerce, and Messrs Tu Yuet Sen (杜月笙)
and Zien Sing Ts (錢新之), Chairman and Vice-Chairman
respectively of the Shanghai District Association, yesterday
sent the following telegram to General Chang Hsueh Liang:-
"The uneasiness caused throughout the
country by the events at Sian has become unbearable.
We love our country and are ready to come to Sian as
hostages for the release of the Generalissimo. All
discussions of policy can be made after Generalissimo
Chiang's return to Nanking."

Lih Pao (Nanking telegram):

General Chang Hsueh Liang and General Yang
Fu Chen have not yet given any sign of their sincerity to
repent. On December 14 they abolished the Headquarters
of the Commander-in-Chief of the North-west Bandit
Suppression Forces and inaugurated a bogus Provisional
North-west Military Commission. On December 17 they
issued a circular telegram announcing their assumption of
posts of Chairman and Vice Chairman respectively of the
Commission.

Soviet Official Interviewed

Interviewed by our reporter yesterday,
Mr. "Salatoff-Kas", Officer-in-Charge of the Intelligence
Office of the U.S.S.R. Embassy in China, made the following
statements:-
"Since the Sian incident, some misunderstanding
about the position of the U.S.S.R. appears to have arisen
among foreign circles, especially the Japanese newspapers;
it is being stated that two cliques; one pro-Japanese
and the other pro-Soviet, will come into existence in China.
Such a report is only propaganda on the part of Japan,
for the U.S.S.R. has no advance knowledge whatever of the
Sian incident. At present, there is not a single citizen
of Soviet Russia in either Kansu or Shensi. The report
that the U.S.S.R. is taking advantage of the incident and is
secretly aiding General Chang Hsueh Liang is absolutely
untrue. The attitude of Soviet Russia has always been to support
the National Government and to respect its independence."

《时事新报》及其他本地报纸：

于右任被任命为西北安抚专员以慰抚军民

根据12月16日中央政治会议通过的决议，监察院院长于右任先生被任命为西北安抚专员，以慰抚军队和民众。
于先生于12月17日前往潼关，并将在洛阳设立办事处。他是否会前往西安会见蒋介石委员长，将视情况而定。

王晓籁、杜月笙和钱新之先生自愿充当人质

上海总商会主席王晓籁先生，以及上海地方协会会长杜月笙先生和副会长钱新之先生，昨日向张学良将军发出如下电报：
“西安事件在全国引起的不安已令人难以忍受。我们爱国，愿意前往西安充当人质，以换取委员长的释放。所有政策讨论均可在蒋介石委员长返回南京后进行。”

《立报》（南京电）：

张学良将军和杨虎城将军尚未表现出任何悔过的诚意。12月14日，他们撤销了西北剿匪总司令部，并成立了一个虚假的临时西北军事委员会。12月17日，他们发出通电解职，宣布分别担任该委员会的正副委员长。

采访苏联官员

本报记者昨日采访了苏联驻华大使馆情报处负责人“Salatoff-Kas”（音译）先生，他发表了以下声明：
“自西安事变以来，外国界别，尤其是日本报纸，似乎对苏联的立场产生了一些误解；有人声称中国将出现两个派系，一个亲日，另一个亲苏。这种报道只是日本的宣传，因为苏联对西安事变事先毫不知情。目前，甘肃或陕西没有一名苏联公民。关于苏联利用此次事件并秘密援助张学良将军的报道绝对不实。苏联的态度一直是支持国民政府并尊重其独立。”

December 18, 1936. Morning Translation.

MAINICHI

NANKING GOVERNMENT INSTRUCTS BANKS IN TIENTSIN
TO SEND SILVER TO SHANGHAI

A Daito telegram from Tientsin
dated December 17 reports that, owing to the unrest in
the money market since the Sian incident, the Nanking
Government on December 16 ordered the Bank of China, the
Central Bank of China and the Bank of Communications at
Tientsin to send their silver stocks(about $50,000,000)
to Shanghai immediately.

The representatives of the
three banks held a conference to discuss the matter.
The amount of silver held by the banks is less than
$50,000,000. The financial situation in the North
will become serious should the instructions be carried
out.

REDS PLAN TO ESTABLISH INDEPENDENT STATE AT SIAN

A Daito telegram from Hongkong
dated December 17 reports that local Chinese newspapers
are publishing reports received by Europeans to the effect
that General Chang Hsueh Liang's action in detaining
General Chiang Kai Shek was done at the instigation of
communists.

Chu Mao and Mo Tse Tung,
leaders of the Chinese communist party , are co-operating
with General Chang Hsueh Liang to establish an independent
state at Sian.

NICHI-NICHI

General Chang Hsueh Liang's secret connection
with the Reds

It has been ascertained that
General Chang Hsueh Liang is in a close co-operation with
the red army and the popular front because a red flag was
hoisted in Sian and a joint headquarters of the Kuomintang
and the Communist Party has been established by the
General.

When General Chang Hsueh Liang
was in command of the anti-communist campaign, he reached
an understanding with the red army.

A young American aviator named
"Hazavy", who was detained at Dihwa, Sinkiang Province,
for violation of aviation regulations, states that he saw
many trucks transporting war materials from Outer Mongolia
or Soviet Russia to China.

General Chang Hsueh Liang has
sent money to Shanghai to assist the activities of the
popular front and to demand the release of Chang Nan Chi
and other leaders of the popular front. Since last summer
General Chang Hsueh Liang has been in close touch with
Sheng Shih Sai in Sinkiang.

1936年12月18日。晨间译稿。

《每日新闻》

南京政府指令天津银行将白银运往上海

据12月17日从天津发出的大东电报报道，由于西安事变后货币市场动荡，南京政府于12月16日命令中国银行、中央银行和交通银行在天津的分行立即将其白银储备（约5,000万美元）运往上海。

三家银行的代表举行了会议讨论此事。银行持有的白银金额少于5,000万美元。如果执行该指令，北方的金融局势将变得严峻。

赤色分子计划在西安建立独立国家

据12月17日从香港发出的大东电报报道，当地中文报纸刊登了欧洲人收到的消息，称张学良将军扣押蒋介石将军的行动是在共产党的唆使下进行的。

中国共产党领导人朱毛（原文如此，指朱德与毛泽东）和张学良将军合作，计划在西安建立一个独立国家。

《日日新闻》

张学良将军与赤色分子的秘密联系

经查实，张学良将军与红军及人民阵线密切合作，因为西安升起了红旗，并且张将军建立了国共联合总部。

当张学良将军指挥剿共战役时，他与红军达成了谅解。

一位名叫“Hazavy”（音译）的美国年轻飞行员因违反航空法规在新疆迪化被拘留，他声称看到许多卡车从外蒙古或苏联向中国运输战争物资。

张学良将军已向上海汇款，以资助人民阵线的活动，并要求释放章乃器（音译）及其他人民阵线领导人。自去年夏天以来，张学良将军一直与新疆的盛世才保持密切联系。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / S. B. REGISTRY. / No. D 2625. / Date 18 / 12 / 36）

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

CENSORSHIP OF BROADCASTING PROGRAMMES

Recently the Shanghai Radio Station
Owners Association received a notification from the
Central Radio Broadcasting Affairs Control Bureau of the
Central Propaganda Department stating that commencing from
December 15 all broadcasting programmes of local radio
stations must be submitted for censorship by the Bureau
and that commencing from that date the Shanghai Telegraph
Administration of the Ministry of Communications and the
Shanghai Bureau of Social Affairs will cease censoring
radio broadcasting programmes. The Association has also
received a set of measures governing the control of
radio broadcasting programmes.
Members of the Executive Committee of
the association held a meeting at its office on Kiangse
Road yesterday, when it was resolved that the Central
Control Bureau be requested to modify some of the measures
drawn up by the Bureau; that in case of necessity, delegates
be detailed to Nanking to make a verbal explanation of
their request.

Hua Mei Wen Pao dated December 17 :-

GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK STOPS PROPOSED BOMBING OF
SIAN BY 400 AEROPLANES

While on his way back to Nanking, on the
night of December 16, Mr. Donald sent a message to Madame
Chiang Kai Shek stating that on his arrival at Sian he
occupied the same residence as the Generalissimo and the
latter instructed him to accompany Mr. T.V. Soong and
General Koo Tsoh Dong to Sian as soon as possible. The
message further stated that Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek
had given an order stopping the proposed bombing of Sian
by aeroplanes.
General Chiang Ting Wen, one of the high
officers held at Sian, has sent a telegram to Generals
Ho Ying Ching, Liu Shih and Koo Tsoh Dong stating that,
in compliance with an autograph order from the Generalissimo,
he will fly to Loyang on December 17 and that the proposed
bombing must be abandoned.
A serious panic was caused in the City
of Sian by the report that 400 aeroplanes of the Central
Airforce were about to bomb the city.

On the morning of December 17 Mr. Donald
flew from Loyang to Pengpu where he boarded the night train
for Nanking to make a report on his mission. Mr. Donald
will fly to Sian again at 7 a.m. December 17. It is said
that he will remain with the Generalissimo.

On the morning of December 17 the
Central Authorities received a telegram from General Chiang
Ting Wen from Sian stating that he would fly to Loyang
shortly. In the afternoon a telegram was received from
Loyang reporting that General Chiang Ting Wen had arrived
at 11 a.m. by plane. No information was received as to
whether General Chiang Ting Wen had escaped from Sian or had
left with the permission of General Chang Hsueh Liang.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

广播节目审查

近日，上海广播电台业主协会收到国民党中央宣传部中央广播事业指导委员会的通知，称自12月15日起，本地各电台的所有广播节目必须送交该委员会审查；并自该日起，交通部上海电政管理局及上海市社会局将停止对广播节目的审查工作。该协会还收到了一套关于管制广播节目的措施办法。
协会执行委员会委员昨日在江西路会所举行会议，决议请求中央指导委员会修改其制定之部分措施；如有必要，将指派代表前往南京，口头说明其请求。

12月17日《华美晚报》：-

蒋介石将军制止拟议中由400架飞机轰炸西安

唐纳德先生（Mr. Donald）于12月16日晚在返回南京途中，向蒋夫人发去电报，称他抵达西安后，与委员长同住一处，委员长指示他尽快陪同宋子文先生和郭佐东将军（General Koo Tsoh Dong，音译）前往西安。电报又称，蒋介石委员长已下令停止拟议中对西安的飞机轰炸。
被扣留在西安的高级将领之一陈调元将军（General Chiang Ting Wen，音译）致电何应钦将军、刘峙将军和郭佐东将军，称遵照委员长手令，他将于12月17日飞往洛阳，必须放弃拟议中的轰炸行动。
有关中央空军400架飞机即将轰炸该市的消息，在西安市内引起了严重恐慌。

12月17日上午，唐纳德先生从洛阳飞抵蚌埠，随后搭乘夜间列车前往南京汇报使命。据悉，唐纳德先生将于12月17日上午7时再次飞往西安。据说他将陪伴在委员长身边。

12月17日上午，中央当局收到陈调元将军从西安发来的电报，称他即将飞往洛阳。下午收到来自洛阳的电报，报告陈调元将军已于上午11时乘飞机抵达。目前尚未收到有关陈调元将军是从西安逃脱，还是经张学良将军许可离开的消息。
