Date January 12, 1937.
Subject Interruption on Lunghai Railway.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

According to information from the Railway
Administration, west bound trains of the Lunghai Railway are
going as far as Tung Kwan only. Buses to Sian are still
available.
It appears that General Yang Hu Cheng is the most
obstinate and stubborn person amongst the rebel ranks. He
has not only ignored Nanking's orders to quit his post but
has styled himself chairman of the Shensi Provincial Government.
General Yang was formerly a bandit leader and has little
knowledge of political organizations. Being busily engaged
in military preparations for defence, he has thus given
communists an opportunity to check the activities of the
Kuomintang.
It is reported that the attitude of General Yu
Hsueh Chung, the military leader of Kansu has become milder
and is still in communication with Nanking politicians.
Nanking still hopes of effecting a peaceful
settlement of the situation through General Chang Hsueh Liang
and General Yen Si San.

Some 700 persons claiming to represent various
circles in Shanghai held a meeting in the Chinese Chamber

3.45 p.m. December 24 in support of the Central Government
to send a punitive expedition to subdue Marshal Chang Hsueh
Liang. Pan Kung Chai, Chief of the Bureau of Social Affairs,
presided and made a report on the revolt organized by
General Chang. He also urged the people throughout the
country to support the Central Government in the campaign
against the rebels in Shensi. Similar speeches were
delivered by Tsai Ching Chun, Chief of the Bureau of Public
Safety, Chang Shou Yung, ex-Vice Minister of Finance,
Dung Ying Pah, a committee member of the local Kuomintang
Headquarters. The following resolutions were discussed
and passed :-
1. That a manifesto be issued in the name of the Meeting.
2. That the Central Government be requested to send a
punitive expedition to suppress Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang.
3. That the people throughout the country be requested to
support the expedition.
4. That telegrams be despatched to the North-eastern
generals requesting them to surrender to the Central
Government.

Messrs. Doo Yueh-sung, Wong Shiao-lai, Zien Sing-tse,
Chu Hsueh Fan, Loh Ching Dz, and Dung Ying Pah be
organized and sent to Sian or Nanking to welcome
General Chiang Kai Shek.
6. That the troops in Suiyuan be requested to continue

Subject Terms for the Surrender of Rebel Leader, and the Release of
Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek.

Made By and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

It is reported from well informed sources that
Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek is insisting that General Chang
Hsueh Liang and the rebel officers should surrender unconditionally
and submit themselves to whatever punishment that may be meted
out to them by the Nanking Government. This resulted in a
deadlock in the negotiations and hastened the departure of
Madame Chiang to Sianfu to endeavour to persuade her husband
and General Chang Hsueh Liang to come to terms.

It would appear that after the coup in Sianfu, General
Chang Hsueh Liang made the following demands in a circular
telegram to Nanking:-
(1) The re-organization of the Nanking Government.
(2) The dismissal of Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek.
(3) The immediate declaration of war against Japan.
(4) The cessation of hostilities with the Reds.
(5) The treatment accorded to his troops in the North-West
to be improved and his troops to be equipped like other
Nationalist troops (or Government troops under Nanking.)

Nanking ignored the demands, dismissed General Chang
Hsueh Liang from all his posts and ordered a punitive expedition.
Two or three days later, the attitude of General Chang Hsueh
Liang became milder. It was said that he had abandoned the
demands for the dismissal of Chiang Kai Shek and the re-
organization of the Government but insisted that war be declared
on Japan and that his troops be sent to Suiyuan to fight with
better equipment. He himself will resign on payment of an
allowance and will hand over military control to General Yu
Hsueh Chung, the Defence Commissioner of Kansu who is one of
his subordinate officers. These demands are reported to

制作及呈报人：谭绍良督察。

据可靠消息来源报道，蒋介石委员长坚持要求张学良将军及叛军军官无条件投降，并接受南京政府可能给予的任何惩罚。这导致谈判陷入僵局，并促使宋美龄夫人加速前往西安府，试图说服其丈夫和张学良将军达成妥协。

看来在西安府发生兵变后，张学良将军在向南京发出的通电中提出了以下要求：
(1) 改组南京政府。
(2) 罢免蒋介石委员长。
(3) 立即对日宣战。
(4) 停止与红军的敌对行动。
(5) 改善其西北部队所受的待遇，并像其他国军（或南京政府军）一样装备其部队。

南京方面无视这些要求，罢免了张学良将军的所有职务，并下令进行讨伐。两三天后，张学良将军的态度变得温和。据说他已放弃罢免蒋介石和改组政府的要求，但坚持要对日宣战，并将其部队派往绥远，配备更好的装备进行作战。他自己将在领取津贴的情况下辞职，并将军事指挥权移交给其部下之一、甘肃绥靖主任于学忠将军。据报道，这些要求已

among local labour and cultural circles and the Chinese
Y.M.C.A. at 599 Szechuen Road and 123 Boulevard de Montigny

various newspaper offices in an envelope and that there were
no indications as to the source of origin.

Group of Representatives of Shanghai Citizens to Rescue
and Welcome General Chiang Kai-shek" (上海市民救迎委員長代表團)

propaganda in favour of General Chiang Kai-shek addressed
to the people and soldiers in Sian.
3. That the pamphlets be sent to the Garrison Commissioner
of Loyang for distribution at Sian by aeroplane.

December 20, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Poo and other local newspapers :-

Inaugural Meeting of the "Association of Comrades to Rescue
the Leader"

The inauguration of the "Association of Comrades
to Rescue the Leader" took place at the Chinese Y.M.C.A.
Building (address not mentioned) at 5 p.m. yesterday. About
70 representatives of the labour, cultural and various other
bodies were in attendance.
After 21 persons had been appointed members to
the Executive and Supervisory Committees of the Association,
the following proposals were passed:-
1) That a telegram be despatched to the National Government
requesting it to immediately issue an order for a
punitive expedition against the rebel troops and to
besiege the Sian city; that a circular telegram be issued
to the people throughout the country to render support.
2) That representatives be appointed to form a "Group to
Rescue the Leader" which is to leave for Sian to welcome
the return of the leader.
3) That picketing groups be formed to assist the military
and police authorities in preventing the activities of
Chinese traitors and reactionary elements.

56 persons, including Messrs. Chang Shih Ying
(張世英) and Tsai Yi (蔡琦), of the cultural, educational,
medical and legal practitioners circles have taken the
initiative to form a "Group of Representatives of the
People throughout the Country to Rescue and Welcome General
Chiang Kai Shek."
Yesterday Mr. Chang Shih Ying and others held a
meeting at which the following resolutions were passed:-
1) That representatives from various bodies be requested
to attend a meeting to be held by the Preparatory
Committee of the Group in question on 2nd floor, No.692
Newchwang Road, at 3 p.m. December 21.
2) That Mr. Wong Shao Lai be requested by letter to immediately
leave for Loyang and to devise ways and means for the
departure for Sian to rescue and administer consolation
to General Chiang Kai Shek.
3) That a telegram be despatched to General Chang Hsueh
Liang asking him to accompany the Generalissimo back to
Nanking.

1936年12月20日。晨间译稿。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：-

“救领袖同志会”成立大会

“救领袖同志会”的成立大会于昨日下午5时在华人基督教青年会大楼（未提及地址）举行。约有70名来自劳工、文化界及各团体的代表出席。
在任命21人为该会执行委员会和监察委员会成员后，通过了以下提案：-
1) 向国民政府发送电报，请求其立即发布命令，对叛军进行讨伐并包围西安城；向全国民众发出通电，请求支持。
2) 指派代表组成“救领袖团”，前往西安欢迎领袖归来。
3) 组建纠察队，协助军警当局防止汉奸和反动分子的活动。

来自文化、教育、医疗和法律从业界的56人，包括张世英（Chang Shih Ying）先生和蔡琦（Tsai Yi）先生，发起成立了“全国各界救迎蒋介石将军代表团”。
昨日，张世英先生等人举行会议，通过了以下决议：-
1) 请各团体代表参加有关团体筹备委员会于12月21日下午3时在新闸路692号二楼举行的会议。
2) 致函黄绍竑（Wong Shao Lai）先生，请其立即前往洛阳，并策划前往西安营救和慰问蒋介石将军的方法。
3) 向张学良将军发电报，请其陪同委员长返回南京。

Subject Local Buddhist and Taoist Services held for the
early return to Nanking of Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek
and for World Peace.

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by R.E. Moore, Pol. Adviser.

A religious service petitioning Heaven
for the early return to Nanking of Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek
and for World Peace is now being held by over 40 male
and 30 female Buddhist devotees under the leadership of
some 11 monks in the Tzuyun Temple (慈雲寺),
Sikwe Road. The service, which consists of prayer only,
commenced at 5 a.m. December 22, 1936, and will terminate
at 5 p.m. to-day. The service will again commence at
7 a.m. December 23, 1936, under the leadership of 11 monks
and will continue right through the day and night until
7 p.m. December 24, 1936.

The principal promoter is one Fan Chi-chuan
(范積川), who is a Taoist and Buddhist although he is the
owner and Manager of the 7th King (七王) Restaurant, 306,
Nanking Road, Rue Eugene Bard. He has invited the following
to be sponsors of the services:-

Weng Ih-ding (翁一亭), a well-known philanthropist
and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the
Shanghai Tientsin Stock Exchange.

Vung Lai-ding (馮來庭), Manager of Mr. Vung's
Management of the Chinese Overseas Trust
Exchange.

Zi Tien-ling (紫田林), a member of the Board of
Directors of the Great Wall Tobacco Company.

Fay Tsia-tsao (費家造), Manager of the Far East
Life Insurance Company, Ltd.

No mention of any donation was made by
Chang Hsueh-liang or others. The services
were held without any political significance.
Services being conducted.

Made by D.S.I. Shields Forwarded by [Signature] E.D.C.

Sir,

C.D.S. 133 reports that between 2.25 p.m. and 3.50 p.m.
24/12/36, about 700 representatives of the Shanghai Municipality
Various Public Bodies to Support the Central Government and
Exterminate Rebel, held a meeting in the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce Building, North Soochow Road, and Messrs. Pan Kong Tsen
(潘公展), Yue Hong Chuen (俞鴻鈞), Loh Ching Zu (陸京士),
Dong Ying Bah (董行) presided. The following resolutions
were passed:-

1. That telegrams be despatched to the Central Government
asking them to exterminate the rebel Chang Hsueh Liang
(張學良).

2. To Woo Ying Ching (何應欽) asking him to give instruc-
tions to all officers to exterminate the rebel Chang
Hsueh Liang.

3. To the people of the whole nation to exterminate the
rebel Chang Hsueh Liang and free Chiang Kai Shek the
Minister of the Executive Yuan.

4. To Sian and advise the rebel army to refrain from
rebellion and free Chiang Kai Shek.

5. To Yang Ho Zung (楊虎城) asking him to protect Chiang
Kai Shek and free him.

6. To the officers in Suiyuan asking them to object to the
attitude of Chang Hsueh Liang.

60 Chinese policemen unarmed under the command of Liang
Foo Tso (梁扶初) officer in charge of the North Station Branch
Bureau and S. P. S. Bureau band attended.

No untoward incident occurred.

General Meeting of Representatives of Shanghai Various
Circles to discuss the Sian incident and to support the
Central Government, to be held in the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce on December 24, 1936

A general meeting styled "General Meeting of Representa-
tives of Shanghai Various Circles in Support of the Central
Government to Send an Expedition against Rebels," will be held
under the auspices of the local Tangpu in the Chinese Chamber
of Commerce, North Soochow Road, at 2 p.m. December 24, 1936
for the purpose of discussing the Sian incident and measures
to be adopted to deal with General Chang Hsueh-liang. Circulars
inviting local public bodies to send delegates to attend the
meeting have been issued.

It is learned that the chairmen will be Mayor Wu who has
approved the holding of this meeting, and Mr. Pan Kung-chai,
Chief of the Bureau of Social Affairs, and that speeches
appropriate to the occasion will be delivered by prominent
Chinese including Tao Pah-chuen, committee member of the local
Tangpu, and Wong Shiao-lai, chairman of the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce.

The agenda of the meeting is as follows:-

1) Respects to the National and Party Flags as well as to the
portrait of Dr. Sun Yat-sen.

2) The reading of Dr. Sun's will by the chairman.

3) The chairman will make a report outlining the present
political situation.

4) Speeches will be delivered by prominent persons.

Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by [Signature]

A meeting entitled "General meeting of representatives
of Shanghai Various Circles in support of the Central Government
to send an expedition against rebels" sponsored by the local
Tangpu will be held in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North
Soochow Road, at 2 p.m. December 24, 1936. The programme of
the meeting is as follows :-
1) Opening ceremony. Respects will be paid to the National
and Party Flags as well as to the portrait of Dr. Sun
Yat-sen.
2) The chairman of the meeting will read Dr. Sun's Will.
3) The chairman will make a report on the present political
situation.
4) Prominent persons will deliver speeches.
5) Proposals, if any, will be moved by the attendance.
6) The suggestion to send circular telegrams and manifestoes
will be put to the meeting for approval.
7) Meeting will close with the shouting of pro-government
slogans.
It is learned that the chairman will be Mayor Wu and
Mr. Pan Kung-chai, Chief of the Bureau of Social Affairs, and
that the persons who will deliver speeches will include Mr.
Tao Pah-chuen (陶百川), committee member of the local Tangpu,
and Mr. Wong Shiao-lai (王曉籟), chairman of the Chinese
Chamber of Commerce.
A circular, inviting local public bodies to send
delegates to attend the meeting, has been issued by the local
Tangpu.

Date Dec. 21, 19 36.

Subject Plan to celebrate General Chiang Kai-shek's return
from Sian.

Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by [Signature]

Reports are to hand which indicate that local
residents are preparing to fire crackers when news is
received of General Chiang Kai-shek's restoration to
freedom. Although enquiries at the majority of Chinese
candle and fire cracker shops show that so far there has
been no large sales of fire crackers during the past few
days, it is reported that the Office of the Chief of the
Membership Canvassing Group of the China Aviation Society,
Chinese Y.M.C.A. Building, Boulevard de Montigny, has
already purchased fire crackers to the value of $10 for
use when required. It is also learnt that workers of the
Yee Tsoong Tobacco Factory, 674 Thorburn Road, have
contributed 10 cents each to a fund raised for the purchase
of firecrackers, and that a total of about $100 has been
raised.

It is to be noted that on March 4, 1932, during
the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Chapei, a rumour was current
that General Shirakawa, commander of the Japanese forces,
had been killed in action. Following the circulation of
this rumour, many Chinese residents resorted to the firing
of crackers which procedure resulted in a mass demonstration
in the Settlement.

General Chiang is at present respected by the
majority of Chinese, and there is every reason to believe
that his safe return to Nanking from Sian will be celebrated.

主题：庆祝蒋介石将军从西安返回的计划。

由督察 Sih Tse-liang 制作，经 [签名] 转呈

收到的报告显示，当地居民正准备在收到蒋介石将军恢复自由的消息时燃放鞭炮。虽然对大多数中国蜡烛和鞭炮店的查询显示，过去几天内鞭炮销量并未大幅增加，但据报道，蒙太尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）中华基督教青年会大楼内的中国航空协会征募组成员办事处已购买了价值10美元的鞭炮，以备不时之需。还获悉，韬朋路674号颐中烟草公司的工人每人捐款10角，筹集资金购买鞭炮，目前已筹集约100美元。

值得注意的是，1932年3月4日，在闸北中日冲突期间，曾流传日军指挥官白川将军战死的谣言。随着这一谣言的传播，许多中国居民开始燃放鞭炮，导致租界内发生大规模示威。

蒋介石目前受到大多数中国人的尊敬，有充分理由相信，他从西安安全返回南京将会受到庆祝。

Date......Dec. 18.......1936.

Subject.........Arrival of General Chiang Ting Wen at Nanking.

Made by....................and........................Forwarded by...........Supt. Tan Shao Liang.

Dr. Hung Chi telephoned this afternoon conveying
the following information which he has received from an
authentic source:-
General Chiang Ting Wen, Pacification Commander of
Fokien, who was one of the prisoners detained at Sianfu as
a result of the coup, arrived at Nanking at 1 p.m. to-day.
General Chiang Ting Wen's release was evidently ordered by
General Chang Hsueh Liang to convey messages from Generalissimo
Chiang Kai Shek to the Nanking officials who had ordered the
punitive expedition.
It appears that General Chang Hsueh Liang had
appealed to Nanking to send an important official to discuss
the situation but Nanking refused stating that if General
Chang Hsueh Liang had anything to say he could say it to the
officials detained there.
General Chiang Ting Wen is reported to have carried
the following message from General Chiang Kai Shek:-
"So long as I am alive, I have no desire to see war
and bloodshed amongst our own people."
This means that he does not approve of the punitive
expedition ordered by Nanking and prefers an amicable solution
of the crisis.
General Chiang Ting Wen was recently summoned by
Generalissimo Chiang to a conference at Sian to discuss the
transfer of his troops to that area for the suppression of
Communists to replace the troops of General Chang Hsueh Liang
forces which were to have been removed to Fokien.

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent,
D.C. (Special Branch).

主题.........蒋鼎文将军抵达南京。

由....................和........................制作，经...........谭绍良警司转呈。

Hung Chi 博士今天下午打电话传达了以下他从可靠来源获得的信息：
福建绥靖主任蒋鼎文将军是西安事变中被扣押在西安府的人质之一，他于今天下午1时抵达南京。蒋鼎文将军的释放显然是张学良将军下令的，目的是向下令进行讨伐的南京官员传达蒋介石委员长的口信。
看来张学良将军曾呼吁南京派遣重要官员讨论局势，但南京方面拒绝，称如果张学良将军有话要说，可以对被扣留在当地的官员说。
据报道，蒋鼎文将军携带了蒋介石委员长的如下口信：
“只要我还活着，我就不希望看到同胞之间的战争和流血。”
这意味着他不赞成南京下令进行的讨伐，更倾向于和平解决危机。
蒋鼎文将军最近被委员长召至西安开会，讨论将其部队调往该地区以镇压共产党，以替换原本要撤往福建的张学良将军的部队。

used as a wireless station under instructions of Marshal Chang
Hsueh Liang. A watch was kept on the premises. Later in
the evening Mr. C. C. Keng, Secretary to Mayor Wu, acting on
instructions from Dr. H. H. Kung, went to the French Police
and requested not to take any action. This request was
complied with and the Police were withdrawn.

This is another instance tending to show that the
Nanking Government is at present very nervous and is exercising
much care when dealing with political opponents.

December 17, 1936.    2    'Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated December 16 :-

Raid on General Chang Hsueh Liang's Radio Station in
Shanghai

On December 15 the radio station
established by General Chang Hsueh Liang in Shanghai was
raided by members of the Bureau of Public Safety with
the assistance of the French Police. The aerials were
cut and all the important accessories were removed. The
responsible persons of the station were interrogated.
Later, on the suggestion of a certain high Government
official, everything was restored to its proper place.
The French Municipal Police have detailed officials to
guard the premises.
The radio station is located in House
No. 28 Hwa Yuan Fong alley off Rue Pere Robert. Its
aerials extend to the roofs of Houses Nos. 26 and 27.
The place was generally known as the Shanghai Communications
Office of the North-eastern Army prior to the revolt of
General Chang Hsueh Liang. The place was raided because
it was still in touch with General Chang after the Sian
uprising.
When our representative called on the
morning of December 16, there was only one person named
Chiang ( 蒋 ) on the premises. He stated that all
telegrams received by the radio station during the past
few days were identical with those published in the
newspapers. The man further stated that when a certain
high Government official arrived in Shanghai, he instructed
him to get into touch with Sian as usual so as to be able
to secure news from that place. Owing to the raid, the
station has ceased operating.

Lih Pao :-

Precautions Against Students Movements

The other day, the Ministry of Education
sent telegrams to universities and education authorities
through the country, instructing them to exert their
utmost to guard against illegal movements by students
and to submit reports from time to time regarding the
situation in schools.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

SHANGHAI HSIEN TANGPU TO HOLD PROPAGANDA MEETING

In order to draw the attention of the
people to the importance of the campaign for the suppression
of bandits, the extermination of traitors and resistance
to insults, the Shanghai Hsien Tangpu will hold a propaganda
meeting on December 21 in the Dr. Sun Yat Sen Memorial
Hall of the Tangpu. Theatrical performances will be
given during the meeting.
The "Min Chung Pao" ( 民衆報 ) of
Shanghai Hsien will publish an extra issue to be presented
gratis to the public.

1936年12月17日。    2    晨间译件。

《华美晚报》12月16日讯：

突袭上海张学良将军电台

12月15日，由张学良将军在上海设立的电台遭到公安局成员在法租界巡捕房协助下的突袭。天线被切断，所有重要配件被拆除。电台负责人受到讯问。随后，根据某位政府高官的建议，一切物品均恢复原状。法租界公董局巡捕房已派遣官员守卫该处所。
该电台位于罗伯特神父路（Rue Pere Robert）华园坊28号。其天线延伸至26号和27号的屋顶。在张学良将军发动事变之前，该处通常被称为东北军上海通讯处。此次突袭是因为该处在西安事变后仍与张学良将军保持联系。
当我方代表于12月16日上午前往该处时，现场只有一名姓蒋（蒋）的人。他称，过去几天电台收到的所有电报均与报纸上刊登的内容相同。此人还称，当某位政府高官抵达上海时，指示他像往常一样与西安方面取得联系，以便获取那里的消息。由于遭到突袭，该电台已停止运作。

《立报》：

防范学生运动

日前，教育部向全国各大学及教育当局发出电报，指示他们竭尽全力防范学生的非法活动，并随时提交关于学校局势的报告。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

上海县党部将举行宣传大会

为引起民众对剿匪、除奸及抗侮运动重要性的关注，上海县党部将于12月21日在汤浦中山纪念堂举行宣传大会。会议期间将有戏剧演出。
上海县《民众报》将出版增刊，免费向公众发放。

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated December 15 :-

GENERAL CHANG HSUEH LIANG'S HOUSE IN FRENCH CONCESSION
WELL GUARDED

Following the shocking news of the revolt
of General Chang Hsueh Liang, developments in the situation
are being watched closely. Definite information is lacking
owing to interruption of telegraphic communication between
Shanghai and Sian.
It is known that General Chang Hsueh Liang
has a residence in Shanghai at No. 2 Rue Corneille, French
Concession. After the outbreak of the Sian uprising, the
place received great attention. General Chang has a
5-year old child for whom he has great affection and whom
he used to leave at Shanghai under the care of an Italian
amah. With a view to ascertaining whether General Chang's
child is still in Shanghai, our reporter called at the
address on the afternoon of December 15. The house was well
guarded by a party of Chinese, French, Russian and Annamite
detectives and uniformed officers from the French Municipal
Police. Similar strict precautions were adopted on the
premises. There were a number of servants in the house,
but they all stated that there was no responsible person
present who could reply to questions put by a reporter.
They also stated that the youngest son of General Chang
had left the place long ago.
The reporter noticed that all the windows and
doors were securely fastened.
pages.zh:
《华美晚报》12月15日讯：

法租界内张学良将军寓所戒备森严

继张学良将军发动事变的惊人消息之后，各方正密切关注局势发展。由于上海与西安之间的电报通信中断，缺乏确切消息。
据悉，张学良将军在法租界高乃依路（Rue Corneille）2号有一处寓所。西安事变爆发后，该处受到极大关注。张将军有一名5岁的幼子，他非常疼爱，以往将其留在上海，由一名意大利保姆照顾。为了查明张将军的孩子是否仍在上海，本报记者于12月15日下午前往该地址探访。该住宅由一队中、法、俄及安南籍侦探以及法租界公董局巡捕房的制服警员严密把守。该处所采取了类似的严格预防措施。屋内有多名仆人，但他们均表示，现场没有负责人可以回答记者的提问。他们还表示，张将军的小儿子早已离开该处。
记者注意到，所有门窗均已牢固锁闭。

pages.en:
TRANSLATION

(The first few sentences containing information regarding
Japanese invasion and the hostilities in the North-East,
at Shanghai and Shanhaikwan are missing.)

The North-East volunteers and national troops have
been engaged in resisting foreign aggression for some time.
The sacrifices made by these men are supreme and glorious.
Owing to the ignorance of Chairman Chiang on public opinion
and the situation in the country, and on account of his
vain talks on war preparations, the resistance put up by
the volunteers has been of no avail. Although they have
gained victories, yet a final triumph cannot as yet be
achieved.

Following the outbreak of war in Suiyuan, the
people of the country have demanded that the army be
immediately mobilized and the invasion resisted, and that
the lost territory be recovered. Chiang, however, has
ignored these demands with the intention of concluding
the hostilities in Suiyuan as early as possible. He
continues to send troops to Shensi and Kansu to suppress
communists.

General Chang Hsueh-liang and General Yang Hu-chen
and other North-Eastern generals who have been guarding
the frontier of China became alarmed at the unfavourable
development in the situation and advised Chiang to repent
and to order all the national troops to resist the enemy in
order to pacify the people. But Chiang rejected the advice
and rebuked Generals Chang and Yang. As Chiang's attitude
concerns the safety of the country, the two generals on
December 12 detained him at Sian in order to make him repent,
while the people and troops in the North-West submitted the
following demands :-

1) That the Nanking Government be reorganized in order to
enable all parties and factions to take part in national
salvation.

2) That civil war be stopped.

3) That the leaders of the national salvation movement who
were recently arrested in Shanghai be released.

4) That all political prisoners be pardoned.

5) That freedom to conduct patriotic movements be granted.

6) That freedom of assembly and organization and other
political privileges be granted.

7) That the bequeathed teachings of the late Party Leader, Dr.
Sun Yat-sen, be put into effect.

8) That a congress to discuss national salvation be convened.
pages.zh:
译文

（开头几句关于日本入侵以及东北、上海和山海关战事的信息缺失。）

东北义勇军和国军抗击外来侵略已有时日。这些人的牺牲是至高无上且光荣的。由于蒋主席无视舆论和国内局势，且空谈备战，致使义勇军的抵抗未能奏效。虽然他们取得了一些胜利，但最终胜利尚无法实现。

绥远战争爆发后，全国人民要求立即动员军队，抵抗侵略，收复失地。然而，蒋无视这些要求，意图尽早结束绥远战事。他继续向陕西和甘肃派兵镇压共产党。

负责守卫中国边疆的张学良将军、杨虎城将军及其他东北将领对局势的不利发展感到震惊，劝告蒋悔悟，并命令所有国军抵抗敌人以安抚民心。但蒋拒绝了建议，并斥责了张、杨两位将军。由于蒋的态度关乎国家安危，两位将军于12月12日在西安将其扣留，以迫使其悔悟，同时西北民众和军队提出了以下要求：

1) 改组南京政府，使各党派参与救国。

2) 停止内战。

3) 释放近期在上海被捕的救国运动领袖。

4) 赦免所有政治犯。

5) 给予开展爱国运动的自由。

6) 给予集会、结社自由及其他政治权利。

7) 实行已故党总理孙中山先生的遗教。

8) 召开救国会议。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. S. B. D. 2675
Special Branch Reg. 36
Date December 15, 1936.

REPORT

Subject Situation created by Sian Rebellion.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

General Yang Hu, the Woosung-Shanghai Defence
Commissioner, on instructions from General Ho Ying Ching, the
Minister of War, issued a proclamation yesterday (December 14)
declaring Martial Law in Shanghai.

The enforcement of Martial Law is intended to put
a stop to mass meetings etc.

It is also reported that Mr. T. V. Soong has offered
the Government to negotiate for the release of Generalissimo
Chiang as he (Mr. T.V.Soong) is on good terms with Chang
years ago but in view of the complicated situation in Sianfu
and the risk of travelling there by aeroplane, the offer was
not accepted. There is no definite news regarding Generalissimo
Chiang Kai Shek; the report that he has been shot cannot be
confirmed.

It is reported that only one Division (the 105th) of
Chang Hsueh Liang's soldiers took part in the mutiny, the
other Divisions are indifferent. Thus, it will not be
difficult for the Government forces to suppress the rebels.

另有消息称，宋子文先生已向政府提出愿为释放蒋介石总司令进行斡旋，因为他（宋子文先生）与张（学良）早年交好；但鉴于西安府局势复杂，且乘飞机前往该地存在风险，该提议未被接受。关于蒋介石总司令尚无确切消息；其被枪击的说法无法证实。

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, DECEMBER 14, 1936
B. D. 7675
14 12 36

Most Of 18 Names Signed To
Chang Declaration Forged

NANKING, Dec. 13.—(Central).—It was now revealed that of the eighteen persons whose names appeared together with that of Chang Hsueh-liang in the telegram from Sian yesterday, at least thirteen could not possibly have participated in the revolt and the appearance of their names was nothing more than a farce concocted by the real conspirators.

To say such men as Gen. Chien Ta-chuh, Chief Aide-de-Camp of the Generalissimo, Mr. Shao Li-tse, Chairman of the Kansu Provincial Government, and Gen. Yang Hu-cheng, Pacification Commissioner for Shensi, have joined an open rebellion against the Government is to insult the credulity of anybody, it was stated.

The inclusion in the telegram names of Gens. Chen Tiao-yuan, Chen Cheng, Chu Shao-liang, Chiang Ting-wen, Wei Li-huan, Wan Yao-huan, Chen Chi-cheng, and Ma Chan-shan was also farcical. All these eight political and military leaders summoned to Sian by Gen. Chiang Kai-shek, it was pointed out.

The names of Gens. Feng Ching-tsai and Sung Wei-ju, it was further pointed out, were also among the co-signatories of Chang Hsueh-liang's telegram. A report from Sian, however, stated that both of them are now under surveillance by the rebels, and directly disproved their alleged complication.

The remaining five signatures to the telegram included Gens. Ho Chu-kuo, Wang I-chih, Miao Cheng-liu, Tung Ying and Yu Hsueh-chung. Even in the case of these five men, it was problematical if they actually placed their signatures on the telegram out of their free will, it was said.

（批：8e OK）

《字林西报》，1936年12月14日，星期一
B. D. 7675
14 12 36

张学良宣言签署的18个名字中
大部分系伪造

南京，12月13日.—（中央通讯社）.—现已查明，昨日西安发来的电报中与张学良名字并列的十八人中，至少有十三人不可能参与叛乱，他们的名字出现纯属真正阴谋者策划的一场闹剧。

据称，如果说像总司令首席侍从室主任钱大钧将军、甘肃省主席邵力子先生以及陕西绥靖公署主任杨虎城将军这样的人加入了公开反政府的叛乱，那简直是对任何人轻信程度的侮辱。

电报中列入陈调元、陈诚、朱绍良、蒋鼎文、卫立煌、万耀煌、陈继承和马占山等将军的名字也同样荒谬可笑。指出这八位军政领袖均是受蒋介石总司令召见前往西安的。

进一步指出，冯钦哉和孙蔚如两位将军的名字也出现在张学良电报的联署人中。然而，来自西安的一份报告称，他们二人目前均处于叛军的监视之下，直接驳斥了他们涉嫌参与的传言。

电报上剩余的五个签名包括何柱国、王以哲、缪澄流、董英和于学忠五位将军。据说，即便对于这五人而言，他们是否出于自愿在电报上签字也成问题。

（批注：8e OK）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, DECEMBER 14, 1936
LOYALIST TROOPS CONVERGE
ON SHENSI; TRAFFIC UPON
RAILWAYS NOW DISLOCATED
SHANGHAI YM. 7957
S. B. RLG.
S. B. D. 2625
14 12 36

General Chiang Kai-shek
And Other Army Leaders
Definitely Held Captive

MME. CHIANG STOPPED FROM FLYING TO
LOYANG IN AN EFFORT TO SAVE
HUSBAND FROM CAPTORS

MARTIAL LAW DECLARED IN VARIOUS
PARTS OF CHINA; NANKING TENSE

Generalissimo's Grave Differences With Ex-Warlord
At Mukden; Reasons Behind Revolt; Soldiers'
Friendliness With Red Forces

NANKING, Dec. 13.—Thousands of Central Government troops were on their way to Shensi to-day in full war-kit in an attempt to quell the revolt of Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang's forces, who are holding General Chiang Kai-shek and several other notables prisoner.

General Chiang Kai-shek was dramatically seized yesterday morning by troops belonging to Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang, commander-in-chief of the anti-Communist forces in Northwest China, who had given an order for his arrest. In this manner the "Young Marshal," who had been lifted from disgrace by the Generalissimo after he had lost Manchuria, rewarded the man who had saved him from total eclipse.

It is learnt that the rebellion broke out when General Chiang Kai-shek expressed dissatisfaction with the progress of the anti-Communist campaign and indicated his intention to transfer some of the Young Marshal's troops, who had fraternized with the Reds instead of fighting them, to Fukien province.

Besides General Chiang Kai-shek, several other military leaders are reported to be in the hands of the mutineers:—

General Chiang Tse-pin, Minister of the Interior and former Ambassador to Tokyo;
General Chen Ting-wen, Pacification Commissioner for Fukien;
General Chen Chi-chen, Pacification Commissioner for the Honan, Hupeh and Shensi borders;
General Chen Cheng, Vice-Minister for War; and
General Yu Hsueh-chung, formerly a staunch supporter of Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang, who opposed the suggestion of a revolt.

Heavy Troop Movements

So heavy were the movements of Central Government troops today that freight traffic on the Lunghai and Tientsin-Pukow Railways had to be suspended and the passenger services severely curtailed.

The Lunghai Railway authorities have placed 100 trains at the disposal of the military and the Tientsin-Pukow Railway 60.

Martial law has been declared, as a precautionary measure, in Nanking, Hankow and many other cities in various parts of China. At Hankow, curfew is being imposed for the entire population, including foreigners, at midnight.

Two divisions of troops have arrived in Nanking to reinforce the local garrison.

Large-scale fighting is considered inevitable in Shensi.

The Central Government was gratified to-day to receive telegrams pledging allegiance and support from various military leaders, including General Sung Cheh-yuan, chairman of the Hopei and Chahar Political Council, General Yen Hsi-shan, Pacification Commissioner for Shansi and Suiyuan, and General Yu Han-mou, Pacification Commissioner for Kwangtung.

Anxiety Over Safety

Although the Government authorities are confident that the revolt will be suppressed quickly, anxiety is felt in all quarters over the personal safety of General Chiang Kai-shek.

Among the loyalist troops in the neighbourhood of Sianfu are several thousand men under General Chu Min-tao, formerly commander of the Public Safety Corps in Chekiang.

Mr. W. H. Donald, who is a close friend of both General Chiang Kai-shek and Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang, is trying to make arrangements to fly to Sianfu to ascertain the precise position and, if possible, to secure the liberation of the Gen-eralissimo. Mr. Donald, who was in Hankow when news of the rebellion was received there, is reported to have left to-day for Loyang.

Dramatic Scene

A dramatic scene was witnessed at the Nanking aerodrome this morning when friends succeeded, at the last minute and only after persistent entreaties, in dissuading Madame Chiang Kai-shek from leaving by air for Loyang, from which city she planned to conduct negotiations for the release of her husband.

It was feared that Madame Chiang might have flown direct to Sianfu, thereby endangering her own life, in an attempt to be at her husband's side in his hour of trial.

Red flags were flown at Sianfu this morning, but when Central Government planes flew over the city they were hastily removed.

Reliable information reaching Nanking shows that the revolt started at 8.30 on Saturday morning, when rifle fire was audible in all parts of Sianfu. The previous night General Chiang Kai-shek had given orders for a special train to be held in readiness for him the next morning, for he intended to leave Sianfu after delivering an address before Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang's officers.

When the Generalissimo failed to arrive at the appointed hour, the railway officials were worried, and their anxiety increased when firing broke out and sections of the railway track were torn up.

After an all-night sitting a special meeting of the Central Political Council, hastily summoned to discuss the emergency, this morning dismissed Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang from his post as acting commander-in-chief of the anti-Communist forces in north-west China and all other appointments, and ordered the Military Affairs Commission to take disciplinary action against him.

General Ho Ying-chin, Minister of War and one of the Vice-Chairmen of the Commission, has been placed in charge of military operations against the rebels.

Strongly-Worded Mandate

The office of the National Government to-day issued a vigorously-worded mandate denouncing Marshal Chang as a traitor to his country for his part in the rebellion.

"Although the Government gave him an opportunity to make up for his past mistakes," declares the mandate, "at a time of national crisis he chooses to adopt the role of a bandit and kidnap the Generalissimo."

Marshal Chang, on his part, has sent a circular telegram to leading civil and military leaders throughout the country bitterly assailing the Government, which he demands should be reorganised, and calling for a national war against Japan in co-operation with the Communists.

On receiving the news of the rebellion, Dr. H. H. Kung, Minister of Finance and Vice-President of the Executive Yuan, and Madame Chiang Kai-shek, hurried to Nanking from Shanghai last night, arriving here this morning.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年12月14日，星期一
效忠派军队向陕西集结；
铁路交通现已中断
SHANGHAI YM. 7957
S. B. RLG.
S. B. D. 2625
14 12 36

蒋介石总司令及其他军方领导人
确已被扣押

蒋夫人试图飞往洛阳营救丈夫
未获成功

中国各地宣布戒严；南京气氛紧张

总司令与前沈阳军阀存在严重分歧；
叛乱背后的原因；士兵与红军关系友好

南京，12月13日.—数千名中央政府军队今日全副武装开赴陕西，试图平息扣留蒋介石总司令及数位其他知名人士的张学良元帅部队的叛乱。

蒋介石总司令于昨日早晨戏剧性地被隶属于中国西北剿共总司令张学良元帅的部队逮捕，张已下达逮捕令。就这样，这位在丢失满洲后由总司令提拔从而摆脱耻辱的“少帅”，以此回报了那位使他免于彻底失势的人。

据悉，当蒋介石总司令对剿共战役的进展表示不满，并暗示打算将部分已与红军 fraternized（原文如此，意为交好/联谊）而非与之作战的少帅部队调往福建省时，叛乱爆发。

除蒋介石总司令外，据报道还有其他几位军事领导人身陷叛军之手：—

内政部长兼前驻东京大使蒋作宾将军；
福建绥靖公署主任陈廷文（音译）将军；
豫鄂陕边区绥靖公署主任陈继承将军；
军政部次长陈诚将军；以及
曾是张学良元帅坚定支持者、反对叛乱建议的于学忠将军。

大规模部队调动

今日中央政府军队的调动规模之大，致使陇海铁路和津浦铁路的货运交通不得不暂停，客运服务也大幅缩减。

陇海铁路当局已将100列火车交由军方支配，津浦铁路则为60列。

作为预防措施，南京、汉口及中国各地许多城市已宣布戒严。在汉口，午夜起对包括外国人在内的全体居民实施宵禁。

两个师的部队已抵达南京，以增援当地驻军。

陕西的大规模战斗被认为不可避免。

中央政府今日欣慰地收到各方军事领导人的效忠和支持电报，其中包括冀察政务委员会委员长宋哲元将军、晋绥绥靖公署主任阎锡山将军以及广东绥靖公署主任余汉谋将军。

对安全的担忧

尽管政府当局确信叛乱将迅速被镇压，但各界仍对蒋介石总司令的人身安全感到焦虑。

在西安府附近的效忠派部队中，有数千人由前浙江保安团指挥官朱民涛（音译）将军率领。

W. H. Donald（端纳）先生是蒋介石总司令和张学良元帅的密友，正试图安排飞往西安府，以查明确切情况，并尽可能争取释放总司令。据报道，当叛乱消息传到汉口时，Donald先生正在汉口，他今日已启程前往洛阳。

戏剧性场面

今晨在南京机场目睹了戏剧性的一幕：朋友们在最后关头，经过苦苦劝阻，成功说服蒋夫人放弃乘飞机前往洛阳的计划，她原计划从该地展开谈判以释放其丈夫。

人们担心蒋夫人可能会直接飞往西安府，试图在丈夫受难时刻陪伴在其身边，从而危及自身生命。

今晨西安府曾升起红旗，但当中央政府飞机飞越该市上空时，红旗被匆忙撤下。

传至南京的可靠消息显示，叛乱始于周六上午8时30分，当时西安府各处均可听到枪声。前一晚，蒋介石总司令已下令准备一列专供他次日清晨使用的火车，因为他计划在向张学良元帅的军官发表讲话后离开西安府。

当总司令未在预定时间到达时，铁路官员感到担忧；而当枪声爆发且部分铁轨被破坏时，他们的焦虑加剧。

中央政治委员会召开紧急特别会议通宵讨论此次危机，今晨会议决定撤销张学良元帅的中国西北剿共代理总司令及其他所有职务，并命令军事委员会对其采取纪律行动。

军政部长兼军事委员会副委员长之一何应钦将军，已负责指挥针对叛军的军事行动。

措辞严厉的命令

国民政府办公厅今日发布了一道措辞严厉的命令，谴责张元帅参与叛乱，卖国求荣。

命令宣称：“虽然政府曾给予他弥补过去错误的机会，但在国家危难关头，他却选择扮演匪徒角色，绑架总司令。”

张元帅方面则向全国文武要员发出通电，激烈抨击政府，要求改组政府，并呼吁与共产党合作，共同进行抗日民族战争。

财政部长兼行政院副院长孔祥熙博士和蒋夫人昨晚从上海匆匆赶至南京，今晨抵达此处。

pages.en:
Mme. Chiang To Rescue
Madame Chiang is flying immediately to Loyang personally to supervise measures to suppress the rebellion and secure the release of her husband.
In a telegram to her last night, Marshal Chiang guaranteed her husband's life.
Dr. Kung arrived too late for the meeting of the Central Political Council, but he presided at a session of the Executive Yuan this morning. Another meeting of the Council was held at the headquarters of the Kuomintang this afternoon.
Nanking yesterday was thrown into a flurry of alarm when the news of the rebellion reached the city during the afternoon. Trains on the Lunghai railway, it was learned, were unable to proceed westward of TungKuan, on the Shensi-Honan border, and railway officials there completely telegraphed what they knew of the situation to Nanking.

For several hours official telegrams to Sianfu remained unanswered.
When the rebellion broke out, General Chiang Kai-shek is stated to have been at Huachihgtze, a hot springs resort about 20 miles from Sianfu. On learning of the event, he immediately hurried back in an attempt to restore the situation, and was detained by the rebels. General Chiang flew to Sianfu from Loyang, Honan, a few days ago.
The troops under Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang are stated to number about 160,000, and are at present scattered through Shensi and Kansu, where they are supposed to have been engaged in operations against the Reds.

Reasons For Rebellion
It is understood that the immediate cause of the rebellion was an order issued by the Generalissimo transferring to Fukien certain troops suspected of fraternising with the Communist enemy.
The Central Political Council, at its meeting this morning, ordered the whole of Marshal Chang's forces, the old North-Western Army, to be placed under the direct command of the Military Affairs Commission.
Other decisions taken to ensure continuance of the Government in the absence of its leaders were—
1.—Dr. H. H. Kung to assume charge of the affairs of the Executive Yuan;
2.—Generals Ho Ying-chin, Ministers of War, Chen Chien, Li Lieh-chun, Chu Pei-teh and Tang Sheng-chih and Admiral Chan Shee-kwan appointed to the standing committee of the Military Affairs Commission;
3.—General Feng Yu-hsiang, Vice-Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission, to be in charge of the Commission in conjunction with the members of the standing committee;
4.—General Ho Ying-chin to be in charge of all troop movements and operations.

Rebels' Demands
In his message to Marshal Chiang Kai-shek, the rebels demanded:
1.—The adoption by the government of progressive measures to form a united front against Japan;
2.—An alliance with Soviet Russia;
3.—Reorganisation of the Kuomintang to admit Communists;
4.—Establishment of a coalition government in place of the dictatorship.
Marshal Chiang expressed himself as willing to accept these demands provided they were submitted to the Central Committee of the Kuomintang for consideration.—Reuter.

Reasons Behind Revolt
PEIPING, Dec. 13.—The dramatic news of the revolt at Sianfu came as a shock to most circles in Peiping today although telegrams received here from the Shensi capital two days ago had indicated that all was not well.
These messages had stated that General Chiang Ting-wen, Pacification Commissioner for Fukien, had been appointed Commander-in-Chief of the bandit suppression activities in the northwest. On the face of it, this step appeared to be a direct blow at Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang.
This appointment, it is also believed, precipitated the crisis which began over a difference of views between General Chiang Kai-shek, and Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang regarding action to be taken against the Communists.
The Generalissimo desired that firm action should be carried out against the Reds, and is reported to have stated that those who talked of action against the Japanese while Communists still remained on Chinese soil were traitors to their country.
It has been well known here for some months that the forces of Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang have been on friendly terms with the Reds and have done no fighting against them for at least nine months.
Anti-Japanese feeling and a common desire to unite the military forces against the Japanese appear to be the basis of agreement between the Communists and Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang's troops.
All eyes here are watching a number of military commanders in north and north-west China in order to observe their reactions to Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang's move.
The majority of the Marshal's troops are reported to be concentrated at TungKwan, on the Honan-Shensi border, where the railway line enters Shensi.
If the revolt at Sianfu proves to have been instigated jointly by Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang and the Communists, the Hopei and Chahar authorities here will make no exception in their anti-Communist policy, and will oppose the rebellion.
This statement was made by a spokesman of the Hopei Chahar authorities during an interview with the Chinese press here to-day.—Reuter.

Chang's Telegram A Farce
NANKING, Dec. 13.—It is revealed that of the eighteen persons whose names appeared together with that of Chang Hsueh-liang in the telegram from Sian yesterday, at least seven could not possibly have participated in the revolt.
Amongst these men as General Chen Tse-chun, Chief Aide-de-Camp of the Generalissimo, Mr. Wu Tieh-cheng, Chairman of the Kiangsu Provincial Government, and General Hsiung Shih-hui, Pacification Commissioner for Shensi, have refused in any situation to join the rebellion, it is stated.
The inclusion in the telegram names of General Chen Cheng, General Chen Chi-tang, Chen Shao-kuan, Wang Ching-wei, Tai Chi-tao, T. V. Soong, H. H. Kung, and Mr. Chang Chun is also denied. The names were added to give by General Peng Chia-sheng and others. It is further pointed out that among the signatories, it would seem that none are really current.
The remaining five signatures to the telegram are those of Chang Hsueh-liang, Yang Hu-cheng, Feng Yu-hsiang, and two others. It is understood that they actually signed their names on the telegram of their own will.—Central News.

Japanese Anxiety
TIENTSIN, Dec. 13. — Cutting short his tour of inspection, General Kenkichi Ueshiro, commander of the Japanese forces in North China, returned here at 4 o'clock this afternoon for a conference with staff officers on the Sian rebellion.
Japanese military circles show intense concern over the whirlwind developments of the last 24 hours. According to intelligence reports, sixteen Chinese divisions are concentrated along the Lunghai line. These forces would probably bear the brunt of any punitive campaign against Chang Hsueh-liang.
Involved at the outset of the possible civil war would be Shansi, with the likelihood that the turmoil may spread to Hopei and other provinces.—Domei.

Japanese Watching Sian Crisis
Fears that the possible repercussions of the Sian mutiny might affect Japanese communities in China were freely expressed last night by Japanese diplomatic and military officials stationed here. These officials said they were mystified by the conflicting reports of General Chiang Kai-shek's death, but expressed unwillingness to believe that General Chang Hsueh-liang would slay the Generalissimo.—Domei.
pages.zh:
蒋夫人前往营救
蒋夫人正立即亲自飞往洛阳，以督导镇压叛乱及确保其丈夫获释的措施。
在昨晚发给她的电报中，蒋委员长保证了她丈夫的生命安全。
孔博士未能赶上中央政治委员会的会议，但他于今早主持了行政院的一次会议。今天下午，中央政治委员会在国民党总部举行了另一次会议。
昨日午后，当叛乱消息传至南京时，全城陷入一片惊慌。据悉，陇海铁路上的列车无法继续向西越过位于陕豫边界的潼关，当地铁路官员将他们所知的局势完全电告南京。

发往西安府的官方电报在数小时内未获回复。
据称，叛乱爆发时，蒋介石将军正在华清池，那是距离西安府约20英里的一个温泉胜地。得知此事后，他立即赶回试图恢复局势，但被叛军扣留。蒋将军于数日前从河南洛阳飞抵西安府。
据称，张学良元帅麾下的部队人数约为16万，目前分散在陕西和甘肃两地，据说他们一直从事针对红军的作战行动。

叛乱原因
据悉，叛乱的直接原因是总司令发布的一道命令，将某些涉嫌与共产主义敌人勾结的部队调往福建。
中央政治委员会在今早的会议上命令，将张学良元帅的全部部队（即旧西北军）置于军事委员会的直接指挥之下。
为确保在领导人缺席期间政府继续运作而作出的其他决定包括——
1.——孔祥熙博士负责行政院事务；
2.——任命何应钦将军（军政部长）、陈诚、李烈钧、朱培德、唐生智将军以及陈绍宽海军上将为军事委员会常务委员；
3.——军事委员会副委员长冯玉祥将军会同常务委员负责委员会工作；
4.——何应钦将军负责所有部队调动及作战行动。

叛军要求
在其致蒋介石元帅的电文中，叛军要求：
1.——政府采取进步措施，建立抗日统一战线；
2.——与苏维埃俄国结盟；
3.——改组国民党以容纳共产党人；
4.——建立联合政府以取代独裁统治。
蒋元帅表示，如果将这些要求提交国民党中央委员会审议，他愿意接受。——路透社。

叛乱背后的原因
北平，12月13日。——尽管两天前从陕西省会收到的电报已暗示局势不稳，但西安府叛变的惊人消息今天仍让北平各界感到震惊。
这些电文指出，福建省绥靖主任蒋鼎文将军已被任命为西北剿匪总司令。表面上看，这一举措似乎是对张学良元帅的直接打击。
人们还认为，这一任命加剧了危机，危机的起因是蒋介石将军与张学良元帅在对待共产党人的行动问题上存在观点分歧。
总司令希望对红军采取强硬行动，据报道他曾表示，在共产党人仍留在中国领土上时谈论对日行动的人是国家的叛徒。
此处数月来众所周知的是，张学良元帅的部队与红军关系友好，且至少九个月未与其发生战斗。
反日情绪以及联合军事力量对抗日本的共同愿望，似乎是共产党人与张学良元帅部队达成协议的基础。
此处各方正密切关注中国华北及西北地区的多位军事指挥官，以观察他们对张学良元帅举动的反应。
据报道，张元帅的大部分部队集中在豫陕边界的潼关，即铁路线进入陕西之处。
如果西安府的叛变被证实是由张学良元帅与共产党人共同煽动，此处的河北察哈尔当局将在其反共政策上不做例外，并将反对此次叛乱。
河北察哈尔当局发言人在今天接受中文媒体采访时发表了上述声明。——路透社。

张之电报纯属闹剧
南京，12月13日。——据披露，在昨日西安发来的电报中与张学良名字并列出现的十八人中，至少有七人不可能参与叛乱。
据悉，其中包括总司令首席侍从室主任陈祖焜将军、江苏省政府主席吴铁城先生以及陕西绥靖主任熊式辉将军，他们在任何情况下都拒绝加入叛乱。
电报中列入陈诚将军、陈济棠将军、陈少宽、汪精卫、戴季陶、宋子文、孔祥熙和张群先生的名字也遭到否认。据说这些名字是由彭嘉生将军等人添加的。此外还指出，在签署人中，似乎没有一人是真正当前的（有效签署）。
电报上剩余的五个签名是张学良、杨虎城、冯玉祥以及另外两人的。据悉，他们是自愿在电报上签名的。——中央通讯社。

日本的焦虑
天津，12月13日。——日本华北驻屯军司令官梅津美治郎将军缩短了视察行程，于今天下午4时返回此处，就西安叛乱与参谋军官举行会议。
日本军方对过去24小时内的急剧变化表现出极度关切。根据情报报告，十六个中国师集中在陇海线沿线。这些部队可能会承担任何针对张学良的惩罚性战役的主要压力。
山西将被卷入可能的内战初期，动荡有可能蔓延至河北及其他省份。——同盟社。

日本关注西安危机
驻此地的日本外交和军事官员昨晚 freely 表达了对西安兵变可能产生的反响会影响在华日本侨民的担忧。这些官员表示，他们对关于蒋介石将军死亡的各种矛盾报道感到困惑，但表示不愿相信张学良将军会杀害总司令。——同盟社。

Date December 14, 1936.

Subject Situation in Shanghai created by the Shensi rebellion.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

As a result of a joint conference held yesterday by local military and civil officials on the Shensi trouble, Mayor Wu Teh Chen and General Yang Hu, the Defence Commissioner, despatched a circular telegram pledging their loyalty to the Nanking Government. Mayor Wu will broadcast a report at 10.30 a.m. to-day on the situation in Shensi.

A prominent official of the City Government states that it is fact that Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek and his staff officers have been held captive in Sian but it is doubtful whether Marshal Chang Hsueh Liang was acting with his free will or whether it was he who started the movement. His brother-in-law, General Yu Hsueh Chung, the Governor of Kansu, is one of the prisoners reported held by the mutineers; he went to Sian in response to a call from Generalissimo Chiang.

With the pouring of Government troops into Shensi from Honan, Kansu and Shansi and with the assistance of a portion of the loyal troops amongst the forces of Chang Hsueh Liang, the Government believes that the rebellion will be quickly quelled.

Meanwhile, the local Chinese Authorities have adopted measures to suppress all movements that may be fomented by radicals in the name of national salvation.

日期：1936年12月14日。

主题：陕西叛乱造成的上海局势。

由谭绍良警司制作并转发。

鉴于昨日地方军政官员就陕西事态举行联席会议，市长吴德桢和防卫专员杨虎将军发出通电信，宣誓效忠南京政府。吴市长将于今天上午10时30分广播关于陕西局势的报告。

市政府一位高级官员表示，蒋介石总司令及其参谋人员被扣留在西安确有其事，但张学良元帅是出于自由意志行事，还是由他发起了这一运动，则令人怀疑。据报道，他的妹夫、甘肃省主席于学忠将军也是被叛变者扣押的人质之一；他是响应蒋介石总司令的号召前往西安的。

随着政府军队从河南、甘肃和山西涌入陕西，并在张学良部队中部分忠诚军队的协助下，政府相信叛乱将很快被平息。

与此同时，中国地方当局已采取措施，镇压所有可能由激进分子以救国名义煽动的运动。

December 14, 1936. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:

THE COUP OF GENERAL CHANG HSUEH LIANG

Mr. Donald, advisor to General Chiang Kai Shek, arrived at Nanking from Shanghai in company with Dr.H.H. Kung, Vice President of the Executive Yuan. Later, Mr. Donald and General Huang Zung Ling left for Loyang by air on their way to Shensi to seek information about General Chiang Kai Shek. Prior to his departure, Mr. Donald received a telegram from General Chang Hsueh Liang in reply to a wire sent by him earlier in the day.

It is learned that General Chiang Kai Shek is still safe in Sian in the hands of the insurgent troops. Generals Chiang Ting Wen, Chen Cheng and Tsu Shao Liang have also been deprived of their freedom. Generals Chiang Kai Shek, Chiang Ting Wen, Chen Cheng, Tsu Shac Liang, Zien Dah Chuin and several guards were resting at Hua Ching Dz when the rebellion broke out; the suddenness of the movement took them completely by surprise. Generals Chiang Kai Shek, Chiang Ting Wen, Chen Cheng and Tsu Shao Liang were escorted by the insurgents to Sian, while General Zien Dah Chuin, who opened fire as soon as he became aware of the situation, was seriously wounded; one report states that he is dead.

The insurgents who seized the military leaders are reported to belong to the 105th Division under the command of General Liu Tou Chuen (劉多荃), General Chang Hsueh Liang's most trusted officer.

According to a report submitted by officials sent by aeroplanes to make an investigation in Sian, the city is quiet. A red flag has been hoisted on the city wall tower. Several sections of the rail way from Sian to Dong Kwan have been removed.

Up to the evening of December 13, communications between the Capital and Sian were still interrupted because the wireless stations have been placed under surveillance by the insurgent troops and the telegraph lines have been cut. Communication with the radio station of the Eurasia Aviation Corporation at Sian is also interrupted. The company's aeroplane, which left Chengtu, Szchuen Province, for Shanghai on December 13, did not land in Shensi; it arrived at Nanking at 4 p.m. and later left for Shanghai.

1936年12月14日。晨译。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

张学良将军之政变

蒋介石将军顾问端纳先生（Mr. Donald）与行政院副院长孔祥熙博士一同由上海抵达南京。随后，端纳先生与黄宗麟将军（General Huang Zung Ling）乘飞机前往洛阳，途中拟赴陕西以探听蒋介石将军的消息。在出发前，端纳先生收到张学良将军发来的复电，回复其当日早些时候发出的电报。

据悉，蒋介石将军目前仍在西安，处于叛军控制之下，但安然无恙。蒋鼎文将军、陈诚将军及朱绍良将军（Tsu Shao Liang）亦被剥夺自由。事变发生时，蒋介石、蒋鼎文、陈诚、朱绍良、钱大钧将军（Zien Dah Chuin）及数名卫士正在华清池休息；事出突然，他们完全措手不及。蒋介石、蒋鼎文、陈诚及朱绍良诸将军被叛军押送至西安，而钱大钧将军在察觉局势后立即开枪还击，身受重伤；有消息称其已死亡。

据报，扣押这些军事领袖的叛军隶属于刘多荃将军指挥的第105师，刘氏是张学良将军最信任的军官。

根据派往西安调查的官员乘飞机提交的报告，该市秩序平静。城墙上已升起一面红旗。西安至潼关（Dong Kwan）铁路的部分路段已被拆除。

截至12月13日晚，首都与西安之间的通讯仍然中断，因为无线电台已受到叛军监视，电报线路被切断。与欧亚航空公司在西安的电台的通讯也已中断。该公司一架于12月13日从四川成都飞往上海的飞机未在陕西降落；该飞机于下午4时抵达南京，随后飞往上海。

《上海日日新闻》（中文版）：

张学良将军发布的通电

Government should have declared war on Japan, but instead
it still adheres to a diplomatic policy of compromise.
The nation and people are in imminent danger.    We take
this opportunity to denounce the present National Government,
to reorganize the country, to drive away the foreign enemies
and to recover the Four North-Eastern Provinces and other
lost territories.*

Yesterday the Mayor of Shanghai and the Woosung-

to be held at 9.30 a.m. to-day.    The report will be broad-

Station (XGOI) (K.C.900).
The Shanghai Education Association, the Shanghai
Middle Schools Association and the Shanghai Agricultural
Association sent the following telegram to General Chang
Hsueh Liang yesterday:-

"We have learned from newspapers that you are holding
General Chiang Kai Shek by force at a time when a tense
situation exists in Suiyuan and when our soldiers are
gaining victories at the front.    Our country is now in
a dangerous and critical situation.    We will not be
able to resist foreign aggressions if the country does
not rise as one man; we cannot achieve national recovery
unless we pursue a unified course in accordance with the
national policy.    This unfortunate incident has occurred
at a time when the whole country has been unified and
the complete extermination of bandits is in sight.
Should the confidence of the army be shaken and the
downfall of our country result, who is to be blamed?    As a
militarist, your duty is to obey and to guard the country.
If your subordinates follow your example and act as they
like, how is discipline to be upheld?    The situation
is serious.    We anxiously hope that you will "pull up
your horse on the verge of the precipice""

Sin Wan Pao published on December 13 the following article
contributed by one Chiang Yen Chung (蒋彦中) :-

ACTION AGAINST STREET VEGETABLE HAWKERS CRITICISED

On the morning of December 12, as I was walking
on Sinza Road, I saw a number of vegetable hawkers, carrying
their wares on their shoulders, walking hurriedly away in
front of me as if they were convicts. In surprise, I
stopped walking and saw two persons pursuing these hawkers,
some of whom were given several heavy slaps by the two
pursuers whose hands were "as large as rush fans" and were
deprived of their bamboo poles and scales. The two men
seized two baskets of vegetables and placed them all in a
raiding van. Those vegetable hawkers who were assaulted
had to put on a smiling face and to implore the two men
as follows: "Gentlemen, thank you. Please return the wares
because our families depend on them for food." Instead
of being moved by the words, the stone-hearted men raised
their voice and flourished their batons which they were
holding. The hawkers retreated several steps, holding their
heads in their hands. A large number of on-lookers soon
gathered; they were all in sympathy with the hawkers.
Judging from their attitude, they were all withholding their
indignation.
"Pigs", shouted the hawkers wrathfully, gnashing
their teeth at the departing van.
The vegetable hawkers who shout out their wares
on the streets or in the alleyways are following a lawful
profession. If they are not allowed to sell their wares
in the market, then where are they to sell their wares? If
it is said that these vegetable hawkers were selling their
wares unlawfully (? without licences), they still deserve
some sympathy in view of the fact that their profession is
one of great hardship. Why should it be necessary to
confiscate articles indispensable to them in their business?
Or if it is said that this measure was taken for the purpose
of improving the appearance of the streets and facilitating
traffic, then we could ask: Will the action of driving the
hawkers left and right improve the appearance of the streets
and facilitate traffic?
This incident reminds me of the fatal assault
of a 13-year old vegetable hawker by a certain foreigner
last year. The life of a vegetable hawker is indeed to
be pitied.

《新闻报》于12月13日刊登了一篇由蒋彦中撰写的文章：-

批评取缔街头菜贩的行动

12月12日上午，当我走在新闸路（Sinza Road）时，我看到许多肩挑货物的菜贩在我前面匆忙行走，仿佛他们是囚犯一般。我惊讶地停下脚步，看到两个人在追赶这些菜贩，其中一些人被这两个手掌“如蒲扇般大”的追赶者重重打了几巴掌，他们的扁担和秤也被夺走。这两人没收了两篮蔬菜，全部放入一辆搜查车中。那些遭到袭击的菜贩不得不强颜欢笑，向这两人恳求道：“先生们，谢谢。请归还货物，因为我们全家靠此糊口。”这两名铁石心肠的人非但没有被话语打动，反而提高嗓门，挥舞着手中的警棍。菜贩们抱头后退几步。很快聚集了大量围观者；他们都同情菜贩。从他们的态度来看，他们都在压抑愤怒。
“猪猡”，菜贩们咬牙切齿地对着离去的车辆喊道。
在街道或巷弄里叫卖蔬菜的菜贩从事的是合法职业。如果不允许他们在市场出售货物，那么他们该去哪里卖？如果说这些菜贩是非法售卖（？无执照），鉴于他们的职业极其艰辛，他们仍值得一些同情。为何有必要没收他们做生意必不可少的物品？或者说，如果采取这一措施是为了改善街道面貌和便利交通，那么我们可以问：将菜贩驱赶得到处跑，就能改善街道面貌和便利交通吗？
这件事让我想起去年一名外国人对一名13岁菜贩的致命袭击。菜贩的生活确实令人怜悯。

December 13, 1936. Morning Translation

Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao and other local newspapers publish
the following telegram from Nanking:-

GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK DETAINED BY GENERAL CHANG HSUEH LIANG.

On the morning of December 12 telegraphic
communications between Nanking and Sian, capital of Shensi,
were interrupted. Subsequently it was reported that
General Chang Hsueh Liang together with his forces in Shensi
had mutinied: In a circular telegram General Cheng Hsueh Liang
suggests the overthrow of the National Government and also
points out that he has given his final advice to General
Chiang Kai Shek whom he has now temporarily detained at Sian.
Upon receipt of the above report, the Central
Standing Committee of the Kuomintang and the Central Political
Council held an emergency conference at 11.30 p.m. (Dec. 12)
at which the following decisions were reached:-
1) That Dr. H. H. Kung, Vice-President of the
Executive Yuan, should act as President ad interim.
2) That the members of the Standing Committee of
the Military Affairs Commission should be increased to seven;
that the power to call meetings of the Commission should be
invested in General Feng Yu Hsiang and other members of the
Standing Committee; that General Ho Ying Ching, Minister of
War and a member of the Standing Committee, mobilize the
Nationalist Armies.
3) That the official rank of General Chang Hsueh
Liang be cashiered and all the troops under his command
be placed under the direct command of the Military Affairs
Commission.

The National Government issued a mandate to the
above effect on December 12.

It is reported that the motive of the coup by
General Chang Hsueh Liang and his north-eastern forces is
to bring about an attack on Manchuria.
Another rumour says that certain military officers
are suspected of being in conspiracy with the Reds.

Dr. H. H. Kung and Madam Chiang Kai Shek left
Shanghai for Nanking by train last night in company with
Dr. Wang Shih Chi, Minister of Education, and General Wang
Shao Hsiung, the newly appointed Chairman of the Hupeh
Provincial Government.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 15, 1936
19972
D7672

Counter-Revolt Reported
From Shensi; Rescue Of
Chiang By Loyal Forces

LATEST ACCOUNTS RECEIVED IN NANKING
LACK CONFIRMATION, ARE REGARDED
WITH THE UTMOST RESERVE

HEAVY FIGHTING IN SIANFU AND
SIENYANG FOLLOWS COUP

General Yang Hu-chen Said To Be Hero Of Ingenious
Trick Played Upon Young Marshal; Gen. Chien
Ta-chun Wounded During Attack

NANKING, Dec. 14.—A counter-revolt headed by General
Yang Hu-chen, Pacification Commissioner of Shensi, has
occurred at Sianfu, the capital of Shensi province, according to
reports reaching Nanking to-night. The reports at present lack
positive confirmation, and are regarded here with the utmost
reserve.

As a result of the counter-revolt, it is stated, General Chiang
Kai-shek, President of the Executive Yuan and Chairman of
the Military Affairs Commission, has escaped from his rebel
captors.

After having apparently joined Marshal Chang Hsueh-
liang's rebellion, General Yang is reported to have persuaded
the "Young Marshal" to transfer General Chiang to his custody
in the new, or inner, city of Sianfu. Having secured the
Generalissimo's safety, he announced his allegiance to the
Central Government, and fighting broke out between his troops
and those of Marshal Chang.

General Yang is said to have two
divisions numbering 20,000 men
against Marshal Chang's three divi-
sions totalling 30,000.

Nine Government aeroplanes flew
over the city in an attempt to aid
General Yang's forces, but with
what result is not yet known.

Hitherto there is no confirmation
of the report that General Chiang
has been able to leave Sianfu, or
that Marshal Chang has been de-
tained, but both these developments
are now considered not unlikely.—
Reuter.

Fighting At Sienyang

NANKING, Dec. 14.—Fierce fight-
ing was proceeding to-day at Sien-
yang, 15 miles north-west of Sian-
fu, the Shensi capital, between Gov-
ernment troops and Marshal Chang
Hsueh-liang's rebels.

A division of Loyalists, numbering
about 10,000, is stubbornly defend-
ing the town against superior num-
bers, according to reports brought
back by Government aeroplane.

It is learned that there was con-
siderable street fighting in Sianfu
when the revolt occurred.

Three regiments of Government
troops stationed in the city resisted
the rebels, comprising a division of
Marshal Chang's troops commanded
by General Liu To-chuan, for sev-
eral hours. Although resistance was
virtually quelled by nightfall, there
was some fighting the following
morning.

Meanwhile, although the Loyalists
continue to move towards Sianfu,
it is learned that the general Gov-
ernment drive against the
rebel stronghold may be withheld
for the present while mediation is
attempted.

Many veteran leaders such as
General Yen Hsi-shan, Pacification
Commissioner for Shansi and Sui-
yuan, and Mr. Yu Yu-jen, President
of the Control Yuan, have offered
to mediate.

Mr. Donald's Dash

Mr. W. H. Donald, Australian
confidant both of General Chiang
and Marshal Chang, to-day made a
dramatic dash by air to Sianfu in
an attempt to save the former from
possible death and deter the latter
from what may well prove a fatal
course of action.

Mr. Donald hopes to effect a
peaceful settlement of the revolt
which has confronted the nation
with one of the most dramatic crises
in its history.

With the rebels under Marshal
Chang holding the head of the Gov-
ernment and other valuable hostages
in the hollow of their hands, the
Government's chief hopes of retriev-
ing the situation rest at present
with Mr. Donald, whose singlemind-
ed honesty has in the past won him
the confidence of all Chinese.

Dr. Donald left Nanking by train
for Loyang, in Honan, last night,
and a long distance telephone re-
port from that city at noon to-day
stated that he had flown to Sianfu
at 10.30 to make contact with Mar-
shal Chang.

The fact that the rebel leader has
evidently given permission for Mr.
Donald to land at Sianfu raises
hopes that he is ready to negotiate.

Moreover, Mr. Donald's first re-
port is awaited with deep anxiety
as it will contain the first authentic
information concerning actual
events in Sianfu since the revolt
occurred on Saturday morning. It
is hoped that he will be able per-
sonally to reassure the outside world
of General Chiang Kai-shek's safety.

Troops Advance

Meanwhile, it is reliably reported
that Government troops are push-
ing rapidly ahead along the Lunghai
railway towards Sianfu, and to-day
were only about 70 miles from the
rebel stronghold.

Two divisions of Government
troops which crossed the Tungkwan
pass, on the Honan-Shensi border,
yesterday reached Hwayin to-day
and are still advancing at a fever-
ish pace, while Marshal Chang's
forces are massing at Hwahsien and
preparing defences there.

General Yang Hu-cheng, Pacifica-
tion Commissioner for Shensi, has
joined the revolt.

In an interview here to-day
General Hu Tsung-nan, Commander
of the 1st Army Corps, stated that
Lanchow, the capital of Kansu,
which adjoins Shensi province, is
at present peaceful.

General Yu Hsueh-chung, one of
Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang's most
powerful subordinates, and his
troops, which are stationed in
Kansu, are loyal to the Govern-
ment. He added that Sianfu is de-
fended by only one division of
Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang's troops.

General Hu arrived this morning
by air from Lanchow and imme-
diately called on General Ho Ying-
chin, the Minister of War, together
with other divisional commanders.
They petitioned the Government to
order a punitive expedition against
Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang. General
Hu returned to Lanchow by air
this afternoon.

Mme. Chiang's Determination

In spite of the persistent plead-
ings of friends Madame Chiang Kai-
shek is determined to go to Sianfu
to be by her husband's side. She
will probably leave by air to-
morrow.

It is learned that Mr. Donald took
two letters to Sianfu to-day—a
personal one from Madame Chiang
Kai-shek to Marshal Chang Hsueh-
liang in English and a brief note,
also to Marshal Chang, from Mr.
Chen Pu-lai, secretary-general of
the Generalissimo's headquarters.

In this note Mr. Chen said "the
Central authorities are anxious to
be informed of the daily doings of
the Generalissimo" the purpose of
which was tactfully to invite an
assurance that General Chiang was
still unharmed.

General Feng Ching-chai, one of
the two divisional commanders
under General Yang Hu-cheng,
Pacification Commissioner of Shensi,
to-day issued a manifesto pledging
his loyalty to the Central Govern-
ment.

The Nanking office of Marshal
Chang Hsueh-liang was searched to-
day, and his representative fled to
Shanghai.

It is significant that the local office
of General Yu Hsueh-chung, one of
Marshal Chang's subordinates, has
not been molested, a fact which is
held to indicate that he is consider-
ed loyal to the Government.

General Yu is in Sian, presum-
ably under detention, while his
troops are in Kansu.

Other prominent detenus are now
known to include Mr. Shao Li-tze,
Governor of Shensi, General Mao
Ping-wen and General Chen Tiao-
yuan, chairman of the Military
Advisory Council, in addition to
Generals Chiang Kai-shek, Chiang
Tso-pin, Chiang Ting-wen and Chen
Cheng.—Reuter.

南京接获的最新消息
缺乏证实，被视为需极度谨慎对待

政变后西安和咸阳爆发激战

据说杨虎城将军是智取“少帅”的功臣；钱大钧将军在袭击中受伤

南京，12月14日电。——据今晚抵达南京的报告称，陕西省会西安发生了由陕西绥靖主任杨虎城将军领导的反叛。目前的报告缺乏确凿证实，此处对此持极度保留态度。

据报道，作为反叛的结果，行政院院长兼军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军已从叛军扣押者手中逃脱。

据报道，杨将军在显然加入了张学良少帅的叛乱后，说服“少帅”将蒋将军转移至他在西安新城（或内城）的监护之下。在确保了委员长的安全后，他宣布效忠中央政府，其部队与张少帅的部队之间爆发了战斗。

据说杨将军拥有两个师，共计两万人，对抗张少帅的三个师，总计三万人。

九架政府飞机飞越该城市上空，试图援助杨将军的部队，但结果如何尚不得而知。

迄今为止，关于蒋将军已能够离开西安，或张少帅已被拘留的报告均未得到证实，但目前认为这两种情况均非不可能。——路透社。

咸阳的战斗

南京，12月14日电。——今天，在距陕西省会西安西北15英里的咸阳，政府军与张学良少帅的叛军之间正在进行激烈的战斗。

据政府飞机带回的报告称，一支约有一万人的忠勇部队正顽强地防守该镇，抵御数量占优的敌军。

获悉叛乱发生时，西安市内发生了大规模的巷战。

驻守市内的三个团政府军抵抗了由刘多荃将军指挥的张少帅部队的一个师，抵抗持续了数小时。虽然抵抗在天黑前基本被平息，但次日早晨仍有一些战斗。

与此同时，虽然忠勇部队继续向西安推进，但据悉，在尝试调解期间，政府对叛军据点的大规模进攻可能会暂时搁置。

许多资深领袖，如山西及绥远绥靖主任阎锡山将军，以及监察院院长于右任先生，已提出愿意进行调解。

唐纳尔的疾行

澳大利亚人W. H. Donald先生，既是蒋将军也是张少帅的亲信，今天戏剧性地乘飞机疾驰前往西安，试图使前者免于可能的死亡，并阻止后者采取可能证明是致命行动方针的行为。

唐纳尔先生希望和平解决这场叛乱，这场叛乱使国家面临其历史上最戏剧性的危机之一。

由于张少帅麾下的叛军将政府首脑和其他重要人质牢牢控制在手中，政府挽回局势的主要希望目前寄托在唐纳尔先生身上，他一心一意的诚实过去曾为他赢得了所有中国人的信任。

唐纳尔博士昨晚乘火车离开南京前往河南洛阳，今天中午从该市打来的长途电话报告称，他已于10时30分飞往西安，以便与张少帅取得联系。

叛军领袖显然允许唐纳尔先生在西安降落，这一事实使人产生希望，即他准备进行谈判。

此外，人们怀着深深的焦虑等待唐纳尔先生的第一份报告，因为它将包含自周六早晨叛乱发生以来关于西安实际事件的第一手真实信息。希望他能够亲自向外界保证蒋介石将军的安全。

部队推进

与此同时，有可靠报道称，政府军正沿着陇海铁路迅速向西安推进，今天距离叛军据点仅约70英里。

昨天越过豫陕边境潼关的两个师政府军今天到达华阴，并仍在以极快的速度推进，而张少帅的部队正在华县集结并在那里准备防御工事。

陕西绥靖主任杨虎城将军已加入叛乱。

第一军团司令胡宗南将军今天在此间接受采访时表示，与陕西省相邻的甘肃省省会兰州目前平静。

张学良少帅最有权势的下属之一、其部队驻扎在甘肃的于学忠将军忠于政府。他补充说，西安仅由张学良少帅的一个师防守。

胡将军今天上午从兰州乘飞机抵达，并立即拜访了军政部长何应钦将军以及其他几位师长。他们请求政府下令对张学良少帅进行讨伐。胡将军今天下午乘飞机返回兰州。

蒋夫人的决心

尽管朋友们不断恳求，蒋介石夫人仍决心前往西安，陪伴在丈夫身边。她可能明天乘飞机离开。

获悉唐纳尔先生今天带了两封信去西安——一封是蒋夫人用英文写给张学良少帅的私人信件，另一封是委员长总部秘书长陈布雷先生写给张少帅的简短便条。

在这封便条中，陈先生表示“中央当局急于了解委员长的日常起居”，其目的是巧妙地邀请对方保证蒋将军依然安然无恙。

陕西绥靖主任杨虎城将军麾下的两位师长之一冯钦哉将军，今天发表宣言，宣誓效忠中央政府。

张学良少帅的南京办事处今天被搜查，其代表逃往上海。

值得注意的是，张少帅下属之一于学忠将军的当地办事处未受干扰，这一事实被认为表明他被视为忠于政府。

于将军在西安，推测被拘留，而他的部队在甘肃。

现已知其他著名被拘者包括陕西省主席邵力子先生、毛炳文将军和陈调元将军（军事顾问委员会主席），此外还有蒋介石、蒋作宾、蒋鼎文和陈诚等将军。——路透社。

Rapid Advance On Sian
NANKING, Dec. 14.—Central Government troops are expected to be at the gates of Sianfu, capital of Shensi province, which is held by rebel forces, by to-morrow evening, according to the latest reports received here to-night.
The vanguards of the Government troops, commanded by General Fan Zung-su, have reached Weinan, only about 45 miles from Sianfu, after advancing 60 miles in two days along the Lunghai railway.
Much to their surprise, very little resistance was encountered from Marshal Chang's forces, many of whom allowed themselves to be disarmed with little or no fighting.
It is believed, however, that Marshal Chang will make a determined attempt to defend Sianfu itself.
General Fan is in telephone communication with General Feng Ching-chai, one of the two divisional commanders under General Yang Hu-cheng, Pacification Commissioner of Shensi. General Feng has pledged his loyalty to Nanking.

Chien Ta-chun Wounded
The death of General Chien Ta-chun, chief aide-de-camp to General Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Executive Yuan and Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission, was reported to-day in a telegram from Marshal Chang, but it is now stated that he is alive.
Marshal Chang's telegram said that he committed suicide, but officials here believed that he was killed when the rebels attacked General Chiang Kai-shek's bodyguard.
Apparently, however, he escaped to Sienyang, 15 miles north-west of Sianfu, after being seriously wounded in the left shoulder.
The rumours current here to-night of a counter-revolt in Sianfu are now generally discredited in the absence of official confirmation. The Government is in constant communication with the Loyalist troops in Shensi.—Reuter.

Sung Cheh-yuan's Policy
PEIPING, Dec. 14.—General Sung Cheh-yuan, Chairman of the Hopei and Chahar Political Council, has telegraphed Nanking expressing the belief that Chang Hsueh-liang is being used as a tool by the Communists, and urging that measures be taken to suppress the revolt and effect the release of General Chiang Kai-shek.
"I am ready with my troops," he says, "and await the orders of the Central Government."
In a statement announcing his policy, General Sung formulates it under three heads: (1) Preservation of peace and order in Hopei and Chahar; (2) Continuation of the anti-Communist policy of the Hopei and Chahar Political Council; and (3) Execution of the orders of the Central Government whether General Chiang Kai-shek is in Nanking or not.—Reuter.

High Officers Killed
TOKYO, Dec. 14.—Reports from Peiping said that the coup was staged on Saturday morning, when the former North-Eastern forces occupied the Sian Railway station and cut tracks east of Sian. This move forestalled General Chiang's scheduled departure by train for Loyang.
Almost simultaneously, another group of mutineers attacked General Chiang's quarters, disarming the bodyguards and killing several high officers accompanying the Generalissimo.
By 9 o'clock that morning, the rebellious troops were in control of a large portion of the Sian-Tungkuan line and of a number of post offices.—Domei.

The Money Factor
NANKING, Dec. 14.—It is stated in financial circles that the rebellion of Chang Hsueh-liang had long been planned.
On the pretext of the approach of the New Year, the Commander-in-Chief's Headquarters of the North-Western Bandit-suppression forces, of which Chang Hsueh-liang was acting Commander-in-Chief, repeatedly telegraphed to the Ministry of Finance last week requesting that the expenses of the said Headquarters be remitted on the 10th inst. in one instalment, instead of in two instalments on the 10th and 25th inst. in the usual manner. The request was turned down by the Ministry.
The fact that the rebellion broke out at Sian on the 12th inst. confirms this view.—Kuo Min.

Order To Seize Banks
NANKING, Dec. 14.—It is reliably learnt that upon the outbreak of the rebellion at Sian on Saturday, Chang Hsueh-liang, the insurgent leader, telegraphed to Major-General Huang Yun-an, Commander of the Artillery Brigade stationed at Loyang, Western Honan, to seize the banks, ammunition depot and aerodrome.
Refusing to obey the order of his superior, Major-General Huang called on Lieut.-General Chu Shao-chou, Garrison Commander of Loyang, and produced Chang's telegram after pledging loyalty to General Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Military Affairs Commission. He assisted Lieut.-General Chu in disarming his own brigade. Loyang is quiet as usual.—Kuo Min.

Yen Hsi-shan Wants Release
TAIYUANFU, Shansi, Dec. 14.—General Yen Hsi-shan, Pacification Commissioner of Shansi and Suiyuan, declared in an interview today that he had telegraphed to General Ho Ying-chin, the War Minister, endorsing the suggestion that all measures should be taken immediately to secure the release of General Chiang Kai-shek from the hands of the mutinous forces of Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang in Sianfu.
His first intimation of the trouble, he said, came from Nanking. Since then he had several conferences with his subordinates, all of whom were agreed that the first efforts had should be directed towards securing the release of the Generalissimo.
General Chiang, along with several other Nanking officials, was seized by the Young Marshal's troops on Saturday after the Generalissimo had reportedly expressed dissatisfaction with the progress of the anti-Communist campaign and indicated his intention to transfer some of the Marshal's troops, who had fraternized with the Reds instead of fighting them, to Fukien province.
Among the others held prisoner by the mutineers are said to be General Chiang Tso-pin, Minister of the Interior and former Ambassador to Tokyo; General Chiang Ting-wen, Pacification Commissioner for Fukien; General Chen Chi-chen, Pacification Commissioner for the Honan, Hupeh and Shensi borders; and General Yu Hsueh-chung, formerly a staunch supporter of Marshal Chang, who opposed the suggestion of a revolt.
General Chen Cheng, Vice-Minister of War, is also said to be a captive at Sianfu, although an unconfirmed report here says that he left the Shensi capital before the trouble started.—Reuter.

Move To Save Chiang's Life
NANKING, Dec. 14.—A stunned and uneasy Chinese nation to-day moved warily to save the life of General Chiang Kai-shek, its greatest soldier and leader of the generation, and nearly a score of high officials, being held as hostages by mutinous troops in Sian.
While drastic mandates ordering the arrest and punishment of the rebels were issued and trains rumbled westward along the Lunghai line, tactful efforts were being made to obtain the release of the prisoners by means of the typical Chinese way out of a tight spot—compromise.
Mr. W. H. Donald, adviser to the Generalissimo, who once served under General Chang Hsueh-liang, the alleged leader of the mutiny; Mr. Yu Yu-jen, President of the Control Yuan, and a known advocate of co-operation between China and the Soviet Union; General Chang Ki, a member of the Central Supervisory Committee of the Kuomintang, and one-time associate of the father of the "Young Marshal," converged by air upon Sian to solve the impasse by negotiation.

General Yen's Message
General Yen Hsi-shan, Chairman of the Shansi provincial government, telegraphed Nanking to withhold punitive measures against the insurgents and seek to save by all means the life of the captive Generalissimo.
In his message, General Yen is reported to have declared that he had been informed by radio from Sian that General Chiang was alive and safe, but had lost his liberty of movement.
While Central troops moved westward along the Lunghai line, Peiping reports received here said that two divisions under General Chang had been concentrated at Tungkwan on the eastern boundary of Shensi province, assertedly to resist an invasion by Nanking punitive forces.
The strength of General Chang's armies was estimated here at 120,-000 men, whereof only 70,000 men were in fighting trim, the other being only auxiliaries.
Two brigades of Central troops are still remaining in Shensi besides the formidable First Army Corps, consisting of 25 regiments under General Hu Tsung-nan and the four divisions under General Kuan Lin-cheng. The latter two forces, however, are now deployed along the borders between Shensi and Kansu and Ninghsia.
To be counted as potential allies of the rebels are the Red forces of Chu Teh and Mao Tze-tung, whose strength could not be accurately gauged.—Domei.

Need Of Evacuating Japanese
TOKYO, Dec. 14. — Japanese residents in the interior of China will be evacuated and concentrated in centres where adequate protection is available should the revolt of General Chang Hsueh-liang in Sian lead to a general civil war, naval authorities here said to-day.
The outbreak of hostilities would not only endanger Japanese lives in the areas directly affected, but might have repercussions in the form of civilian and military uprisings in isolated districts.
In view of the avowed anti-Japanese aim of the mutiny at Sian, such disturbances would seriously jeopardize the security of Japanese residents, naval officials here felt.
While measures to cope with such an emergency were being mapped out as a precautionary measure, Japanese officials awaited with undisguised concern reports regarding the fate of General Chiang Kai-shek, outstanding leader of the Nanking Government, and the other officials who are being held as virtual hostages in Sian.

179,

迅速向西安推进
南京，12月14日电。——据今晚在此收到的最新报告，中央政府部队预计将于明晚抵达陕西省会西安府城门，该城目前由叛军控制。
政府军先头部队在范钟苏（音译）将军指挥下，沿陇海铁路两天推进60英里后，已抵达渭南，距西安府仅约45英里。
令他们大为惊讶的是，张元帅的部队几乎没有进行抵抗，许多人未作战斗或仅作轻微战斗便缴械投降。
然而，人们认为张元帅将竭力防守西安府本身。
范将军正与冯钦哉（音译）将军保持电话联络，冯是陕西绥靖主任杨虎城将军麾下的两名师长之一。冯将军已宣誓效忠南京。

钱大钧受伤
行政院院长兼军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军的首席副官钱大钧将军的死讯，今日由张元帅在一封电报中通报，但现称其尚在人世。
张元帅的电报称其自杀，但此地官员认为，他在叛军袭击蒋介石将军的卫队时被杀。
然而显然，他在左肩受重伤后逃往位于西安府西北15英里的咸阳。
由于缺乏官方证实，今晚在此流传的关于西安发生反叛乱的谣言目前已普遍不被采信。政府正与陕西的忠义部队保持不断联络。——路透社

宋哲元的政策
北平，12月14日电。——冀察政务委员会委员长宋哲元将军致电南京，表示相信张学良正被共产党人利用为工具，并敦促采取措施镇压叛乱并实现蒋介石将军的获释。
他说：“我已准备好我的部队，等待中央政府的命令。”
在一份宣布其政策的声明中，宋将军将其归纳为三点：(1) 维持冀察地区的和平与秩序；(2) 继续冀察政务委员会的反共政策；以及 (3) 无论蒋介石将军是否在南京，均执行中央政府的命令。——路透社

高级军官遇害
东京，12月14日电。——来自北平的报告称，政变发生于周六早晨，当时原东北军占领了西安火车站并切断了西安以东的铁轨。此举阻止了蒋介石按计划乘火车前往洛阳。
几乎同时，另一群叛变者袭击了蒋介石的住所，解除了卫队的武装，并杀害了陪同委员长的数名高级军官。
到当天上午9时，叛军已控制了西潼线的大部分路段以及若干邮局。——同盟社

资金因素
南京，12月14日电。——金融界人士称，张学良的叛乱是蓄谋已久的。
以新年临近为借口，由张学良代理总司令的西北剿匪总司令部上周多次致电财政部，请求将该总部的经费于本月10日一次性汇付，而非按惯例分两次于本月10日和25日汇付。该请求被财政部拒绝。
本月12日叛乱在西安爆发的事实证实了这一观点。——《国民》

查封银行的命令
南京，12月14日电。——据可靠消息，周六西安叛乱爆发时，叛军首领张学良致电驻豫西洛阳的炮兵旅旅长黄永安少将，命令其查封银行、弹药库和机场。
黄少将拒绝服从上级命令，拜访了洛阳警备司令朱绍良中将，在宣誓效忠军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军后，出示了张的电报。他协助朱中将解除了自己旅的武装。洛阳一如往常平静。——《国民》

阎锡山要求释放
山西太原府，12月14日电。——山西绥远绥靖主任阎锡山将军在今日的一次采访中表示，他已致电军政部长何应钦将军，赞同立即采取一切措施以确保蒋介石将军从西安张元帅叛军手中获释的建议。
他说，他最初得知这一麻烦是从南京传来的。此后他与下属进行了多次会议，所有人都同意首要努力应致力于确保委员长的获释。
据报道，蒋介石将军与其他几名南京官员于周六被“少帅”的部队扣押，此前委员长曾表示对反共战役进展不满，并指示打算将张元帅麾下部分与赤色分子交好而非与之作战的部队调往福建省。
据称，其他被叛变者囚禁的人包括内政部长兼前驻东京大使蒋作宾将军、福建绥靖主任蒋鼎文将军、豫鄂陕边区绥靖主任陈继承将军，以及曾是张元帅坚定支持者但反对叛乱建议的于学忠将军。
据说陆军次长陈诚也是西安府的俘虏，尽管此处有一未经证实的报告称他在麻烦开始前已离开陕西省会。——路透社

挽救蒋介石生命的行动
南京，12月14日电。——震惊且不安的中国今日谨慎采取行动，以挽救其最伟大的军人和一代领袖蒋介石将军以及近二十名被西安叛军扣为人质的高级官员的生命。
在发布严厉命令逮捕和惩罚叛军的同时，列车沿着陇海线向西隆隆驶去，与此同时，人们正通过典型的中国式摆脱困境的方式——妥协，巧妙地努力争取释放囚犯。
曾服务于所谓叛乱首领张学良将军麾下的委员长顾问W. H. Donald（唐纳德）先生、监察院院长且以主张中苏合作闻名的于右任先生、国民党中央监察委员且曾是“少帅”父亲旧部的张继将军，乘飞机汇聚西安，试图通过谈判解决僵局。

阎将军的电文
山西省政府主席阎锡山将军致电南京，要求暂缓对叛军的惩罚措施，并千方百计挽救被俘委员长的生命。
据报道，阎将军在电文中宣称，他通过无线电从西安获悉，蒋介石将军活着且安全，但失去了行动自由。
当中央部队沿陇海线向西移动时，此处收到的北平报告称，张将军麾下的两个师已集结在陕西省东界的潼关，据称是为了抵抗南京惩罚部队的入侵。
此处估计张将军军队的兵力为12万人，其中只有7万人具备战斗状态，其余仅为辅助人员。
除了胡宗南将军指挥的由25个团组成的 formidable 第一军团以及关麟征（音译）将军指挥的四个师外，仍有两支中央部队旅留在陕西。然而，后两支部队目前部署在陕西与甘肃及宁夏的边界沿线。
被视为叛军潜在盟友的是朱德和毛泽东的红军部队，其兵力无法准确评估。——同盟社

撤离日本人的必要性
东京，12月14日电。——此地海军当局今日表示，如果西安张学良将军的叛乱导致全面内战，在华内陆的日本居民将被撤离并集中到有充分保护的地区。
敌对行动的爆发不仅会危及直接受影响地区的日本人生命，还可能以孤立地区的平民和军事暴动的形式产生反响。
鉴于西安叛乱公开宣称的反日目标，此地海军官员认为，此类骚乱将严重危及日本居民的安全。
在制定应对此类紧急情况的预防措施的同时，日本官员怀着毫不掩饰的担忧，等待有关南京政府杰出领袖蒋介石将军及其他在西安被实际扣为人质的官员命运的报告。
